title: Resolve newly verified artifact-store containment and deletion findings
description: Implement and verify the three artifact-store findings identified after TLDR-wa2g.1: (1) canonicalize and validate root plus source path before FileFactsParser reads or parses; (2) enforce canonical project containment in ArtifactManager delta submission while explicitly preserving deletion semantics for paths that no longer exist; (3) make full-project ingestion include previously known but now absent subjects in regeneration/removal so stale manifest keys cannot survive. Add focused cases to the shared certification harness and complete all repository quality gates. External CodeRabbit verification is intentionally omitted by explicit user direction.
acceptance_criteria: All three findings are fixed or rejected with direct code evidence; tests cover an in-root symlink resolving outside the root, a missing delta below a symlinked external parent, legitimate deleted-path delta handling, and full-project deletion removing stale definitions/artifacts; cargo fmt, workspace Clippy/tests, smoke, and certification pass. CodeRabbit is waived by explicit user direction.
notes: COMPLETION EVIDENCE 2026-07-27: source containment is enforced before parser invocation; daemon deltas reject existing external symlinks and missing targets beneath symlinked external ancestors while accepting legitimate in-project deletion; project ingestion removes absent file/symbol subjects and call edges. Gates passed: cargo fmt --all --check; git diff --check; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features; cargo tldr-smoke (2/2); cargo tldr-certification (9/9). CodeRabbit intentionally skipped per user instruction.

title: DECISION: No silent degradation — VectorStore-only search path, SemanticIndex fallback removed
description:
## Decision

VectorStore is the ONLY search path. The SemanticIndex fallback and JSON cache deserialization (load_with_lock, 1.1GB HashMap) are removed from the query flow entirely. On any VectorStore failure (load/build/search/save), propagate a detailed error message to the user — never silently degrade to the slow path.

## Rationale

Silent fallback to SemanticIndex (4-5s cold JSON load + per-query ONNX model reload) makes the user believe that IS the tool's performance. They never discover the fast path failed, never report the bug, and never get it fixed. The only acceptable fallback is a clear, actionable error message that tells the user what broke and how to fix it.

A tool should run at 100% performance or tell you why it can't. Running in degraded mode without the user's knowledge is a UX anti-pattern — it hides bugs behind mediocre-but-functional behavior.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Keep SemanticIndex fallback (current design)**: Rejected — hides VectorStore failures from users, makes performance bugs invisible, and preserves the slow JSON cache load path that m01/ac0 exist to eliminate.
- **Fallback with a visible warning**: Rejected — warnings are ignored by users, especially in CLI tool output. The tool still "works" so the warning is treated as noise.
- **Fallback with opt-in flag (--allow-degraded)**: Rejected — over-engineered for the problem. If VectorStore is broken, fix VectorStore.

## Affects

- TLDR-zxb: Wire search_with_store into CLI/daemon/MCP (must implement error-only, no fallback)
- TLDR-m01: Rewire EmbeddingCache onto usearch Index (store_search.rs fallback code removed)
- store_search.rs: SemanticIndex import and fallback branch removed entirely
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.
close_reason: Decision recorded and linked to zxb + m01. Enforced in zxb implementation.

title: DECISION: Incremental re-indexing lives in the daemon (RAM writable index), gated on warm path
description: Because view() is read-only (see storage-split decision), incremental updates (remove stale function vectors + add changed ones, instead of the full ~30min re-embed) REQUIRE a RAM-resident writable usearch Index. DECISION: that index lives in the DAEMON (TLDR-atc). The daemon holds the writable Index, watches file mtimes, applies per-function deltas, and periodically save()s to disk. Cold CLI invocations use read-only view() of the last saved file. CONSEQUENCE: incremental indexing is NOT a property of usearch alone — it is unlocked by usearch + the daemon warm path together. This elevates TLDR-atc from a latency win to the keystone for incremental indexing.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.
close_reason: ACCEPTED (ADR record, 2026-06-01). Decision is final and recorded; closing so it stays a durable, queryable record without sitting in the active work queue. Reopen only if the decision is revisited.

title: Add daemon warm path for semantic search (no semantic route exists — every query is cold)
description: DISCOVERED 2026-06-01 via daemon route scan + tldr explain. tldr-daemon exposes 21 routes (ping/status/tree/structure/extract/imports/calls/impact/dead/importers/arch/cfg/dfg/slice/complexity/search[BM25]/context/smells/maintainability/secrets/vuln) and ZERO semantic/similar/embed routes. crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/semantic.rs has 0 daemon references. CONSEQUENCE: every 'tldr semantic'/'similar'/'embed' invocation runs COLD in a fresh process -> SemanticIndex::build -> EmbeddingCache::open -> load_with_lock (cache.rs:236) deserializes the full ~1.1GB cache each time (RSS ~8GB), reloads the 110MB ONNX model (~0.5s), then embeds the query (~0.2s). For warm/interactive use this is a BIGGER lever than usearch: usearch view() removes the 4.3s load, but a daemon warm path removes the load AND the 0.5s model load AND keeps the index resident -> ac0 estimated ~230ms warm. SCOPE: add /semantic (+/similar,/embed) daemon route + handler that holds a warm SemanticIndex (mmap'd vectors once usearch lands) + a warm Embedder (model loaded once) in DaemonState, keyed by project+model+mtimes like other warm caches. Pairs with TLDR-ac0 (usearch storage) and TLDR-h27/y0q (CLI correctness).
acceptance_criteria: tldr semantic/similar/embed route through the daemon when running; warm query latency ~200-300ms (no per-query 1.1GB load, no per-query model reload); cold fallback preserved when daemon absent; results identical to cold path.
notes:
UNLOCKS INCREMENTAL INDEXING (research 2026-06-01): usearch view()'d mmap index is READ-ONLY (issue#97 — cannot add to disk). Incremental updates (remove stale keys + add changed-function vectors, avoiding the full ~30min re-embed) REQUIRE a RAM-resident writable index. The daemon warm path is exactly that home: hold the writable usearch Index in DaemonState, apply deltas on file-mtime change, periodically save(). So this P0 is not just a latency win — it's the prerequisite for incremental re-indexing. Cold CLI keeps using read-only view().
2026-06-02 STATUS: warm path + root-relative cache keys committed (401a7ac); off-executor spawn_blocking committed (7199f03). REMAINING: live stop-mid-build validation (was pending the cache being free). The spawn_blocking follow-up bug (handle_notify on async thread) is TLDR-qr9, now folded into TLDR-ac0.2 (in-daemon watcher → internal channel). Consider closing atc once the live stop-mid-build check is done.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.
close_reason: Warm path ships VectorStore — load_or_build_store is near-instant on fresh store. Daemon holds resident (Model, VectorStore). Remaining improvements (incremental delta, watcher, concurrent reads) are separate issues (t8f, ac0.2, ac0.1).

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: POST-ZXB (2026-06-02): The daemon now holds a resident VectorStore (Mutex<Option<(Model, VectorStore)>>) instead of SemanticIndex. Warm command uses load_or_build_store — near-instant when store is fresh on disk. The original atc acceptance ("warm query latency ~200-300ms, no per-query 1.1GB load, no per-query model reload") is MET for the common case (store exists, nothing changed). The "cold fallback preserved when daemon absent" criterion changes per TLDR-lx7: no fallback, errors propagate. Consider closing atc — the warm path works, remaining improvements (incremental delta, watcher) are separate issues (t8f, ac0.2).

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: EVOLUTION LINK (2026-07-27): TLDR-9bxa.6 extends the warm-daemon foundation with workload-specific runner states and lock separation; TLDR-9bxa.9/TLDR-9bxa.11 add generation-aware rollout and final acceptance evidence.

title: Default 0.50 similarity threshold miscalibrated for query-prefix regime (hides correct results)
description: DISCOVERED while dogfooding tldr semantic on our own codebase (TLDR-blm work). The Arctic query prefix (TLDR-dlk, default-ON) improves RANKING decisively (eval recall@5 0.071->0.857) but LOWERS absolute cosine scores, because the asymmetric prefix puts query embeddings in a different region than raw-code passages (query.passage cosine < passage.passage cosine). The user-facing 'tldr semantic' applies a fixed default --threshold 0.50. Result: the CORRECT answer for 'cosine similarity between two embedding vectors' is cosine_similarity() but it scores 0.46 -> filtered out -> CLI prints 'No matches found above threshold'. So the feature looks BROKEN to a user despite the recall win. The eval harness bypasses the threshold (pure ranking) which is why it reported 0.857. FIX OPTIONS: (a) lower/remove the default threshold and rely on top-k ranking; (b) recalibrate threshold for the prefixed-query score distribution; (c) make threshold prefix-aware. Repro: tldr semantic 'cosine similarity between two embedding vectors' crates/tldr-core/src/semantic --top 3  (default threshold -> no matches; --threshold 0.0 -> cosine_similarity appears at rank 3, score 0.46).
acceptance_criteria: tldr semantic with default settings surfaces the correct top-ranked result for the gold queries (not filtered by threshold); eval-measured ranking and CLI-visible results agree.
notes: Child of TLDR-blm epic. Surfaced by the prefix verdict; a user-facing gap between eval-measured ranking (good) and CLI-visible results (threshold-suppressed).
close_reason: Default semantic threshold 0.5->0.0 (rank top-N, no cutoff) so the prefix-regime scores (~0.46) are no longer hidden; also fixed the formatter's hardcoded 0.50 display to show the actual threshold. PROVEN: 'tldr semantic <q>' with default settings now returns cosine_similarity instead of 'No matches'. semantic.rs.

title: Re-run fully cold tldr-code semantic benchmark on authoritative runtime
description: Audit the tldr-code ignore policy against the historical cold benchmark, verify the latest installed release, clear the same project and reusable embedding stores, rebuild once from cold, and record normalized apples-to-apples evidence against the 2026-07-29 historical run and Dhan.
acceptance_criteria: The compared corpus policy is explicit; installed/release hashes match; no concurrent daemon/builder remains before cleanup; project and reusable embedding caches are demonstrably absent; one cold rebuild reaches warm with files/vectors/windows/cache hits/retries/wall time recorded; results are compared per vector and committed with Beads evidence.
notes: Completed on 2026-07-29. Tracked an audited root .tldrignore that retains tests/examples/fixtures and excludes docs, continuum, bench, archived CLI, and defensive secret/key patterns. Rebuilt all release binaries at d7f45ab; installed hashes matched. Stopped all daemons, cleared 30.3 MiB shared embeddings and 1.1 GiB project stores, verified no ArtifactStore, then ran one authoritative cold daemon build: 517 files, 15,158 new + 5 same-run duplicate vectors, 119 windows, 1,830.348s, zero retries. Historical normalized result was 110.94 ms/vector; current is 120.75 ms/vector (+8.84%). Warm semantic/BM25/hybrid probes passed. Evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-07-29-tldr-code-authoritative-cold/REPORT.md.

title: Gate ArtifactStore closure with an authoritative command-route and freshness matrix
description: Prevent another infrastructure epic from closing while consumer commands remain on stale pipelines. Define the supported top-level analysis commands and classify each execution owner as ArtifactStore projection, resident derived index, intentionally local/file-scoped, external-tool orchestration, lifecycle/mutation, or explicitly parked. Turn the classification into executable route/parity/freshness checks rather than documentation alone.
design: Use one machine-readable command capability registry or equivalent compile/test-visible contract. Tests must catch orphan DaemonCommand variants, public legacy routes with no supported consumer, silent fallback from strict daemon commands, resident-index generation mismatch, and command flag/output divergence between daemon and intentional oneshot implementations. Benchmark representative repeated queries to prove no full-project rebuild where resident data is promised.
acceptance_criteria: All supported top-level commands are classified with an authoritative owner and rationale; CI fails for an unclassified command or orphan protocol variant; daemon versus oneshot parity is tested where both are supported; edit/ignore-policy freshness is tested for stored and resident indexes; repeated-query probes prove references/definition/coupling/deps/search do not perform forbidden full-project rebuilds; TLDR-eda5 cannot close until this gate and its implementation dependencies are closed.
notes: COMPLETED 2026-07-29: machine-readable top-level owner registry covers all 68 commands and protocol registry covers every retained DaemonCommand. CI catches unclassified/orphan routes, duplicate daemon packaging, legacy APIs, generation mismatch, and freshness/parity regressions. Workspace all-feature gates pass. Clean Dhan rebuild and five-run matrix prove resident search/references/definition/deps/coupling with no Salsa answer-cache activity. Evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-07-29-dhan-authoritative-runtime/REPORT.md.
close_reason: Authoritative route/freshness matrix is executable, green, and proven on a clean Dhan runtime.

title: Classify and retire legacy cache/search APIs after authoritative routes land
description: Static reference analysis found exported APIs with no current production callers after strict daemon and ArtifactStore changes: try_daemon_route; semantic search_with_store/query_store; enriched_search_with_index, enriched_search_with_callgraph_cache, enriched_search_with_structure_cache; read/write structure cache; and hybrid_search. Some may become the correct implementation seam for resident BM25, so do not delete by reference count alone. After authoritative daemon, BM25, and command consumers are wired, classify every API and retire only obsolete runtime paths.
acceptance_criteria: For every listed API, record authoritative consumer or deletion reason; retain and test any API selected as the resident-index seam; remove dead exports/implementations and stale JSON persistence; no public API suggests a cold or fallback pipeline that the supported CLI cannot execute; focused public-API and command tests pass.
notes: COMPLETED 2026-07-29: deleted silent try_daemon_route, cold semantic search_with_store/query_store, cold hybrid_search, obsolete enriched wrappers, JSON callgraph/structure cache APIs, and stale benchmark examples. Retained only explicit local and resident seams. Executable regression test forbids reintroduction; workspace clippy/check/tests pass. Implementation ef76581.
close_reason: Obsolete cache/search APIs and misleading public fallback paths retired with regression coverage.

title: Consolidate daemon implementations and enforce protocol parity
description: Two daemon implementations coexist: the production tldr CLI IPC daemon and the standalone Axum tldr-daemon crate/binary. The standalone daemon has an unused resident BM25 cache and unused invalidation method. The production protocol also retains Search, Cfg, Dfg, Slice, Arch, Diagnostics, and ChangeImpact variants with no matching top-level client route or incomplete flag/semantic parity. Select one authoritative daemon, migrate only useful behavior, then remove or explicitly deprecate the duplicate runtime and stale protocol surface.
acceptance_criteria: One daemon is documented and built as authoritative; duplicate server/runtime packaging is removed or explicitly compatibility-gated; every retained DaemonCommand has a real typed client and full flag/output/freshness parity; orphan variants are deleted; invalidation is tested for every resident index; tldr daemon start/status/query behavior remains covered.
notes: COMPLETED 2026-07-29: removed the standalone Axum daemon crate and wrapper binary; tldr daemon is the sole runtime. Removed orphan protocol variants and added an exhaustive protocol-client registry plus CI comparison against DaemonCommand. Lifecycle/status/query and freshness tests pass. Implementation ef76581.
close_reason: Single authoritative daemon packaged and protocol parity enforced by executable registry.

title: Finish ArtifactStore adoption for remaining project-wide CLI queries
description: The redb cutover plan explicitly required references, definition, impact, dead, hubs, and coupling to use stored definitions/references/call edges. Impact, dead, and hubs are routed; references, definition, and coupling still parse or walk source locally. Deps also recomputes dependency analysis although imports are projected by GenerationSnapshot. Complete the consumer cutover while preserving command-specific semantics: split cursor/local-scope work from project-index lookup where necessary, route project-wide phases through the pinned daemon generation, and eliminate duplicate project walks.
acceptance_criteria: references, definition, coupling, and deps consume a pinned ArtifactStore generation for project-wide data; command output and flags retain parity with oneshot behavior; no query-path full-project parse/walk remains where the stored projection is sufficient; focused differential tests cover daemon versus local semantics and freshness.
notes: COMPLETED 2026-07-29: workspace references project stored classified occurrences; global definition projects stored definitions after file-local resolution; deps uses stored imports; project coupling uses stored modules/imports/call edges. Pair/cursor/local modes remain intentional local. Differential/freshness tests pass. Dhan references/definition/deps were under 0.01s and coupling 0.01s across five runs. Evidence report linked in repository; implementation ef76581 and output correction 7d21dab.
close_reason: Remaining project-wide consumers now use pinned ArtifactStore projections with parity and live evidence.

title: Audit CLI routes for stale and unused infrastructure
description: Systematically compare every tldr CLI command path with daemon routing, redb artifacts, resident indexes, response memoization, and incremental invalidation. Identify stale duplicate flows and rank integration fixes without modifying production code.
notes: Audit completed 2026-07-29. Inventory: 68 top-level Command variants; 12 project-analysis commands use strict route_for_path and semantic uses its dedicated daemon route. This does not imply 55 defects because lifecycle, git, external-tool, file-local, and mutation commands can remain local. Confirmed architectural families: (1) BM25 CLI and MCP rebuild per request despite reusable-index APIs; already tracked by deferred TLDR-utj.3 and TLDR-94k. (2) The closed ArtifactStore cutover plan explicitly required references/definition/coupling migrations that remain local; deps is another direct imports-projection candidate. Follow-up TLDR-4d8c. (3) Two daemon implementations coexist; standalone resident BM25/invalidation APIs are unused, while seven production DaemonCommand variants are orphaned or lack CLI flag parity. Follow-up TLDR-js45. (4) At least nine exported legacy cold/cache/search APIs have no production callers. Follow-up TLDR-4o3a. (5) semantic is correctly daemon-resident; similar and MCP semantic are intentionally parked/tracked by TLDR-utj.4/.5. Static validation used exact reference searches and the 2026-07-29 benchmark evidence; no source code changed.
close_reason: Static architecture and route audit completed; distinct implementation work recorded in TLDR-4d8c, TLDR-js45, and TLDR-4o3a, with existing BM25 tasks retained.

title: Add global embedding-cache clear CLI command
description: Add the top-level command `tldr embeddings clear` to remove the global content-addressed document-vector cache while preserving downloaded fastembed model weights. Provide structured output, symlink-safe bounded deletion, tests, and user documentation. This command enables honest first-index benchmarks after `tldr cache clear` removes project-local structural/vector state.
design: Create a top-level `embeddings` command group with a `clear` subcommand. Resolve the target exclusively from `CacheConfig::default().cache_dir`; never accept an arbitrary path. Recursively remove entries without following symlinks, remove the empty cache directory, emit JSON/text/compact output, and document that all daemons/builders must be stopped first.
acceptance_criteria: `tldr embeddings clear` deletes only the resolved global embeddings cache, reports files/bytes freed, preserves the fastembed model directory and unrelated vector stores, is idempotent, does not follow symlinks, is covered by CLI/unit tests, and is documented with global-impact and daemon-stop warnings.
notes:
Implemented the bounded global-cache command. The target is derived only from CacheConfig::default().cache_dir; no user path is accepted. Deletion uses symlink_metadata, refuses a non-directory root, removes nested symlinks without following them, preserves sibling fastembed model weights and project stores, and treats an absent cache as success. Added structured files/bytes/model-preserved output, CLI parse coverage, idempotence/isolation tests, a Unix external-symlink sentinel test, explicit global-impact help, and troubleshooting/daemon documentation. Validation so far: cargo test -p tldr-cli --all-features; cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy -p tldr-cli --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; git diff --check. Release install and live destructive validation remain before closure.
Installed release binaries from commit 7ba3ba8 and live-validated the command against the real macOS cache. It removed exactly one cache.redb file (71,356,416 logical bytes / 68.1 MiB), reported the resolved global path, and a second invocation returned success with zero files/bytes. The 22-file fastembed directory remained 515,296 KiB and its manifest SHA-256 remained c3a5dfd1639a1c6cc08b5e41c1649941bf1e8515869a2db00ba551663fd29429. No daemon/builder was active. Evidence is under docs/benchmarks/2026-07-29-fully-cold-runtime/.
close_reason: Implemented, documented, tested, installed, and live-validated global embedding-cache clearing with model-cache preservation and idempotence.

title: Benchmark fully cold tldr rebuild and serving performance
description: Remove this project’s structural/vector indexes, global document embedding cache, daemon runtime state, logs, sockets, and tldr temporary artifacts while retaining downloaded model weights. Rebuild from a genuinely cold semantic cache, capture correlated phase/unit/RSS metrics, then benchmark daemon startup, CLI cold/warm graph commands, lexical search, semantic search, and delta indexing.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-run inventory proves project indexes and embedding cache are absent; a single rebuild completes without concurrent builders; phase, inference, cache, publication, RSS, disk, and wall-time metrics are retained; representative CLI and search queries are timed repeatedly; delta timing is measured; results and limitations are documented and Beads updated.
notes:
FULLY COLD METHOD AND PROOF (2026-07-29): Installed release binaries from exact source commit 7ba3ba8. Stopped all daemons/builders. tldr cache clear found no pre-existing project artifact store. The new tldr embeddings clear removed exactly one global cache.redb file (71,356,416 logical bytes / 68.1 MiB), and the idempotence invocation removed zero. Project .tldr, project vector store, and PID/socket/poke paths were absent before the timed build. The 22-file, 515,296-KiB fastembed model cache was deliberately retained to exclude network download; its content-manifest SHA-256 stayed c3a5dfd1639a1c6cc08b5e41c1649941bf1e8515869a2db00ba551663fd29429 before and after all work.

WHY THE OPTIMIZATIONS WERE EXPECTED TO HELP: The earlier full-build bottleneck was excessive semantic document fragmentation and fixed-shape inference/cache-write overhead. Context-root coalescing reduced the prior clean workload from 49,215 documents to about 15,000 and cut the 57m40s run to 30m00.68s. Separately, delta indexing was slow because the affected-file path still performed project-wide corpus/freshness preparation before making the localized decision. The delta fix moves path filtering/coalescing into the watcher, publishes only affected artifact revisions, projects semantic chunks only for changed paths, and removes/replaces only those chunks in the active vector generation. The watcher now forms fixed five-second windows from the first event; completed windows enter a bounded 64-entry FIFO and one serial executor publishes them, preventing concurrent generation races while retaining later batches.

CURRENT FULLY COLD RESULT: External wall 1,670.38s (27m50.38s), correlated report 1,670.008s, semantic worker 1,665.439s. This is 130.30s faster than 30m00.68s (-7.2%) and 1,789.83s faster than the 57m40.21s clean run (-51.7%). It indexed 512 files, planned 15,061 documents, embedded 15,056 with five legitimate intra-run duplicate hits, processed 3,912,542 tokens in 1,052 inference calls and 118 durability windows, and reported zero retries/failures/limitations. Inference was 1,411.622s, planning 160.720s, cache write 76.590s, vector assembly 11.756s, publication 1.079s, and worker process peak RSS 1,618,542,592 bytes. The extra 2m10 improvement versus the immediately prior run is primarily 126.105s lower inference time; because the full-build algorithm did not materially change, treat that delta as measured runtime/current-machine variance rather than attributing it to the file-scoped delta change. The distinct reusable-embedding rebuild remains 4m15.8s.

SERVING METRICS: tldr init 0.84s. Controlled daemon restart returned in 126ms and artifact+semantic stores were ready by the 863ms poll with 512 files and 15,061 vectors. Five-run process-wall results, all exit zero with stable output: tree first 39ms/warm median 25ms; structure 74/71.5ms; watcher extract 13/13ms; dead 77/76ms; lexical search 396/401ms; enriched search 1,077/1,051ms; semantic watcher query 496/60.5ms; second semantic query 61/61ms. Semantic internal store search was 6-7ms. Query runner built one session, served ten requests, and had zero failures. Salsa telemetry recorded five misses and zero hits across the structural matrix, so stable low latency comes from loaded stores rather than reported Salsa memo hits.

WATCHER/DELTA METRICS: An mtime-only event started its batch at approximately 5.017s, advanced artifact generation 3->4, was idle by 5.363s, and made zero delta model requests: at most ~0.35s processing after the intentional window. After daemon restart with a cold delta session, a real one-line edit started its batch at approximately 5.037s; generation 7->8 appeared by 5.457s, the delta session was built by 5.945s, one request embedded 14 documents at exact shape [14,384], inference was ready by 7.125s, and the batch was idle by 7.388s. The exact reverse edit reused the session, advanced generation 8->9, made one [14,384] request, and was idle by 6.830s. Thus first real delta is <=7.39s total (~2.35s post-window) and warm delta <=6.83s total (~1.79s post-window), with zero failures and constant 15,061-vector cardinality. Edits within a five-second window coalesce; later windows queue and publish serially.

RESOURCE FOOTPRINT: Generated state after validation was ~281 MiB disk: project .tldr 104,432 KiB, global embeddings 62,260 KiB, project vector generation 121,292 KiB. Preserved model weights were 515,296 KiB. title: Queue fixed five-second watcher batches
description: Change watcher coalescing from a 750ms quiet debounce to fixed five-second collection windows. Decouple event collection from indexing so the watcher can form subsequent batches while the current batch publishes, while preserving serialized artifact/vector generations and bounded overflow escalation.
design: Use separate collector and executor tasks connected by a bounded batch queue. Keep the raw notify callback non-blocking. Reuse watcher_max_wait_ms as the fixed window and set its default to 5000ms; stop using per-file quiet deadlines for flush timing. Preserve burst file/event caps and full-rebuild fallback.
acceptance_criteria: The first accepted event opens a five-second window; all accepted paths in that window are deduplicated into one delta batch; later windows continue collecting while earlier batches execute; batches execute strictly serially; bounded queue overflow escalates safely to a full rebuild; watcher unit tests and live validation pass.
notes: Implemented 2026-07-29. Timing semantics: the first accepted watcher event opens a fixed 5,000ms window; later events join without rearming or shortening the deadline. The legacy debounce default is aligned to 5,000ms, while watcher_max_wait_ms is the authoritative window. Worker architecture: the raw OS callback remains non-blocking; a collector owns coalescing/burst state and sends completed Flush values to a bounded 64-entry queue; a separate single consumer executes batches FIFO, so collection of Batch N+1 continues while Batch N indexes but artifact/vector generations never publish concurrently. Existing raw queue remains bounded at event-cap+1 (1,001 by default); extreme backpressure therefore retains the existing overflow-to-full-rebuild safety path. Tests: fixed late event at 4.9s remains in the first batch; no flush at 4.999s; flush at 5.0s; repeated paths deduplicate; burst caps pass; deliberately blocked Batch 1 proves Batch 2 queues and cannot start early. Quality: all 43 tldr-cli lib tests pass; strict all-target/all-feature Clippy passes. Live installed release: mtime event kept artifact generation 12 unchanged at 4 seconds, then published generation 13 once at 5.472 seconds total; delta runner stayed cold with 0 sessions and 0 requests. Design docs updated.
close_reason: Fixed-window collection, bounded serial batch queue, tests, release install, and live five-second boundary validation all complete.

title: Make file-scoped artifact ingestion avoid full-corpus refresh work
description: IngestionScope::Files selects only changed files for parsing, but before selection it runs ProjectWalker discovery and source_manifest, reading and hashing every corpus file to compute a global source revision and detect removals. After parsing the changed file it reads/decodes every FileFacts callgraph_ir and recomposes the whole project call graph, publishes a complete manifest, then ArtifactManager reloads every FileFacts record and rebuilds GraphSnapshot. This is correct under the current immutable whole-generation contract but makes every watcher delta scale with corpus size. Split exact changed-file publication from periodic full reconciliation while preserving generation consistency and cross-file graph correctness.
acceptance_criteria: File-scoped ingestion does not read/hash every source file on each event; only changed FileFacts are decoded from storage; global graph work is either incrementally recomposed or explicitly measured and deferred to a coalesced reconciliation; missed events/deletes still converge correctly; generation snapshots never mix revisions; delta phase timing proves work scales with changed files rather than corpus size.
notes: Implemented the high-cost file-scoped work avoidance on 2026-07-28. Root cause: IngestionScope::Files was applied only after ProjectWalker discovery and source_manifest, so every event read/hashed all 511 source files; ArtifactManager then decoded every FileFacts artifact to rebuild its hot snapshot. Fixes: file_scope_manifest normalizes and hashes only explicit changed/deleted paths while deriving a deterministic lineage revision from the prior generation; ignore policy and full-project reconciliation remain authoritative; unchanged FileFacts are shared behind Arc and refresh_files decodes only changed paths from the new manifest. Regression test makes an unchanged source unreadable and proves a changed-file ingest still succeeds with parsed_files=1. Remaining intentionally global work: project call-graph composition still decodes all FileFacts callgraph_ir and recomposes cross-file edges for exactness; previously measured around 100ms on this 511-file corpus. Keep this issue open until that decode/compose step is incremental or moved to measured coalesced reconciliation.

title: Avoid full-corpus semantic chunk materialization on each delta
description: Live watcher validation on the 511-file tldr-code corpus showed a no-content delta taking about 4.8s and tiny comment edits taking about 16.8s/21.8s even though only 8 documents were embedded. apply_semantic_delta_batch currently calls snapshot.semantic_source_chunks(project) and collects the full project into a HashMap before removing only changed paths. RSS rose from about 864MB to 1.93GB across no-op/edit/restore while the delta runner handled only two requests. Determine the latency and retained-memory contribution, provide a changed-file-only artifact API, and verify repeated same-shape deltas plateau in RSS.
acceptance_criteria: Delta preparation reads/composes only changed files; zero-content delta latency and small-edit publication latency are benchmarked; repeated same-shape edit/restore cycles show bounded plateauing RSS; embedding counts remain output-change-only; focused watcher/daemon tests pass.
notes:
Root-cause trace 2026-07-28: semantic delta uses the bulk-only GenerationSnapshot::semantic_source_chunks(project) API (documented as complete source inputs). That API iterates every resident FileFacts, clones whole file-granularity content/hash/name fields into CodeChunk values, sorts the full Vec, then daemon.rs clones paths again into a full HashMap and removes only applied files. Existing GenerationSnapshot::file(relative) is already O(1), so semantic projection need not be corpus-wide. Separately, IndexManager::apply_delta calls delta_runner.with_token_budget before revision classification; with_token_budget calls ensure_session, loading the full ONNX delta session even for a no-content edit that performs zero inference. This explains the ~574MB first no-op RSS increase and part of its ~4.8s latency. Recommended semantic fix: add generation-pinned per-file/batch projection returning all chunks for requested paths, avoid path-key collision assumptions, and provide tokenizer budget without constructing the inference backend; time projection/planning/session-init/embed separately.
Implemented and live-validated 2026-07-28. Why the optimization should work: GenerationSnapshot already owns FileFacts in a path-keyed HashMap, so selecting changed paths can be O(changed files) rather than cloning/sorting all corpus chunks. Output hashes already decide whether embeddings are needed, so initializing ONNX before that classification is unnecessary. Fixes: added semantic_source_chunks_for direct path projection; daemon groups only selected chunks and preserves delete/multi-chunk behavior; added a commit-pinned tokenizer-only TokenBudget planner cached separately from ONNX sessions. TDD proved the old planner built one session and the new planner builds zero. Live 511-file/15,042-vector results: mtime-only 4.8s -> 1.23s (74% faster), runner remained cold at 0 sessions/0 requests; restore 21.8s -> 1.52s (93% faster), repeated edit/restore 1.49s/1.67s with exactly 8 documents and one request each. Same-shape cycles reused one session and plateaued near 1.40 GiB (about 6 MiB variation after warmup). After project cache reset: no-op 1.18s, first edit 1.99s, restore 1.65s. Evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-07-28-file-scoped-delta-fast-path.md.
close_reason: Closed

title: Coalesce trivia and declarations into semantic owners
description: The function-granularity structural planner preserves every named root AST child. In Tree-sitter Rust, line comments, attributes, and use declarations are named nodes, so they become independent embedding documents even though most have no standalone retrieval value. The 2026-07-28 read-only replay of the active 511-file generation produced 49,215 documents: 30,316 root line_comment nodes, 2,922 use_declaration nodes, and 1,502 attribute_item nodes. These three categories account for 70.6% of documents but only about 15.9% of source bytes. This is a unit-boundary error, not parser failure, fallback expansion, or source duplication: 47,495 documents were AstChild, only four used tokenizer fallback, none used parse fallback, and total overlap was 68 bytes. Preserve all source text, but stop treating trivia/context declarations as standalone semantic roots.
design: Use a small explicit classification in structural planning. Comments and attributes should travel with the following semantic owner where possible; adjacent imports/use declarations and remaining trivia should be coalesced within the existing token budget. Keep functions, impls, structs, enums, traits, modules, constants, and other retrieval-bearing declarations as preserved roots. Do not introduce a new parser, chunk representation, background queue, or heuristic scoring system. Reuse the existing merge-and-budget loop, retain deterministic AST paths/source coverage, and apply identical behavior to bulk and delta planning.
acceptance_criteria: On the same published corpus, report document counts by AST root kind before and after. All source bytes remain covered; overlap remains explicitly bounded; no document exceeds the 512-token budget; bulk and delta planning produce identical documents for the same file; comments/doc comments and attributes remain searchable as part of their owner; focused retrieval checks show no material regression; and a cold or cache-backed production benchmark demonstrates the expected large reduction in documents, ONNX calls, and inference time.
notes:
INTERMEDIATE DISCOVERY — NOT FINAL: read-only planner replay against active generation 3 exactly reproduced 49,215 chunks and 5,224,463 tokens. Chunks/file mean 96.3, p50 55, p90 206, p95 347, max 1,083. Roles: AstChild 47,495; ParentSummary 1,716; TokenizerFallback 4; ParseFallback 0. AST depth 1: 43,196 chunks. Token distribution: 32,146 chunks at 33-64 tokens and 8,318 at 65-128. Only 13,404 chunks carried a qualified symbol. Root AST classification found 42,194 named nodes, including line_comment 30,316, use_declaration 2,922, attribute_item 1,502, function_item 4,065, struct_item 1,160, impl_item 830. Planned source bytes 10,087,969 vs source 10,087,901 with only 68 overlap bytes. This strongly identifies over-preserved trivia roots as the dominant corpus inflation source.
POST-CHANGE RELEASE REPLAY (generation 15, 511 files): 49,215 -> 15,020 documents (-69.5%); 5,224,463 -> 3,902,146 tokens (-25.3%); AstChild 47,495 -> 13,299; ParentSummary 1,716 -> 1,717; TokenizerFallback remains 4. Root-kind owners: line_comment 30,316 -> 1,375 (-95.5%), use_declaration 2,922 -> 35 (-98.8%), attribute_item 1,502 -> 29 (-98.1%). Coverage: 10,093,425 source bytes, 10,093,493 planned bytes, exactly the same bounded 68 overlap bytes; zero >512-token documents. Bulk/delta fixture parity passes. Focused planner/protocol tests and CodeRabbit review (0 findings) pass. Still open before closure: production vector rebuild/cold timing and focused retrieval checks on structural-embedding-v2.
Implementation and replay tooling committed as 08657ed (perf(semantic): coalesce context roots into owners). Issue intentionally remains in_progress pending the production v2 rebuild, cold timing, and focused retrieval checks.
FINAL ACCEPTANCE (clean installed-binary run, commit 08657ed): published 15,020-vector generation in 1,800.68s (30m00.68s), down from 3,460.211s (-48.0%) and original 4,431.28s (-59.3%). Documents 49,215 -> 15,020 (-69.5%), tokens 5,224,463 -> 3,902,146 (-25.3%), inference 3,026.470s -> 1,537.727s (-49.2%), calls 1,781 -> 1,048, windows 385 -> 118, zero oversized/truncated inputs, zero retries/failures. Planning regressed 145.647s -> 167.017s (+14.7%) but net wall win is 27m39.53s. Daemon warm in 11.76s with 15,020 vectors; focused classifier query ranked is_context_root_kind #1, regression tests #2/#5; broad query returned comment/import-bearing owners. Full evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-07-28-context-root-coalesced-clean/.
Final benchmark evidence committed as a74c9d0 (docs(benchmark): record coalesced clean build).
IMPLEMENTATION AND VALIDATION NARRATIVE — FINAL (2026-07-28): The fix intentionally changed only semantic ownership boundaries. is_context_root_kind narrowly classifies comments, Rust attributes, and supported import/use node kinds as attachable context. segment_is_semantic_owner distinguishes retrieval-bearing named declarations. split_node now preserves a named-root boundary only after the current merged group already contains a semantic owner. Leading comments/attributes/imports therefore merge forward into the following declaration under the existing 512-token budget, while a comment preceding the next declaration cannot merge backward into the prior owner. Functions, impls, structs, enums, modules, constants and other declarations remain preserved roots. No text is dropped, no new parser/queue/cache or scoring heuristic was added, and oversized context still falls through the existing budget/fallback machinery. Bulk planning and delta planning share the same planner and have an explicit byte/structure/range parity test. Store CHUNK_WALKER_VERSION changed w1->w2 and worker pipeline identity changed structural-embedding-v1->v2, forcing old persisted vectors and resumable jobs to fail compatibility rather than silently mixing chunk boundaries. Tests cover attachment direction, narrow syntax classification, exact source reconstruction, symbol ownership and bulk/delta parity; focused planner/protocol tests, workspace tests/checks, formatting and CodeRabbit review all passed. CORRECTNESS/QUALITY GATES: release replay preserved all 511 files and every source byte, retained the same explicitly bounded 68-byte fallback overlap, produced zero >512-token inputs, and kept four tokenizer fallbacks. Standalone owner counts collapsed line_comment 30,316->1,375, use_declaration 2,922->35 and attribute_item 1,502->29. The remaining context-owned chunks are budget-constrained/context-only groups and remain searchable rather than dropped. After the clean production rebuild, a focused natural-language query ranked is_context_root_kind first, its classification/attachment tests second and fifth, and segment_is_semantic_owner third; a broader query returned comment/import-bearing semantic owners. PERFORMANCE CAUSALITY: compared with the immediately preceding clean 511-file run using the same Arctic-M fixed-shape backend and mixed-batch implementation, total wall fell 3,460.211s->1,800.680s (-48.0%); semantic worker 3,454.657s->1,795.518s; inference 3,026.470s->1,537.727s (-49.2%); documents 49,215->15,020; tokens 5,224,463->3,902,146; calls 1,781->1,048; windows 385->118; dummy rows 13,920->4,189; peak RSS -10.9%. The honest tradeoff is semantic planning 145.647s->167.017s (+14.7%) because larger candidate groups require more token-budget work. The 21.37s planning cost is overwhelmed by 1,488.743s less inference plus 162.653s less cache writing and 23.555s less vector assembly. This is why a 25.3% token reduction produced a 48.0% wall-time reduction.
close_reason: All acceptance gates passed: source coverage and bounded overlap, 512-token budget, bulk/delta parity, exact before/after owner-kind accounting, clean production rebuild/timing, and focused installed retrieval checks.

title: Rebuild indexes when ignore policy changes
description: Changing .tldrignore, .gitignore, nested ignore files, .ignore, or .git/info/exclude reloads the live watcher matcher but does not invalidate and rebuild already-published structural and semantic generations. Newly ignored files can therefore remain searchable until an unrelated rebuild, while future file events alone are filtered.
design: Treat ignore-policy changes as corpus-boundary changes, not per-file deltas. Queue one single-flight full warm: invalidate the resident semantic store immediately, re-run authoritative project discovery and artifact ingestion under the new policy, then publish a complete replacement vector generation. If a build is already running, retain one pending rebuild request and execute it after the current build. Never read ignore files on the query path and do not delete reusable per-document embedding cache entries.
acceptance_criteria: A watched ignore-policy event schedules FullRebuild rather than a file delta; the resident semantic store is invalidated; project discovery removes newly ignored artifact records; a complete replacement semantic generation is published; a policy change during an active warm queues one follow-up rebuild; repeated policy events coalesce; ordinary source events retain delta behavior; focused watcher/daemon tests and relevant crate tests pass.
notes: IMPLEMENTED + VALIDATED 2026-07-28: watcher policy events now emit a typed FullRebuild signal and bypass file deltas. The daemon invalidates the resident semantic store and runs the existing authoritative project warm, whose corpus discovery removes newly ignored artifact records before the replacement vector generation is published. A synchronized warm state coalesces repeated policy changes and guarantees one follow-up rebuild when policy changes during an active warm. Query paths do not read ignore files. Per-document embedding cache remains reusable; correctness comes from replacing the logical generation. Validation: watcher tests 10/10, daemon tests 5/5 including artifact removal after adding .tldrignore, tldr-cli lib 40/40, cargo check --workspace --all-targets passed.
close_reason: Implemented full generation replacement on ignore-policy changes with active-build coalescing and passing focused/workspace checks.

title: Exclude non-product, test, fixture, example, and archived sources from semantic indexing
description: The approved corpus policy should exclude root documentation/continuum/benchmark material plus recursive tests, fixtures, examples, and the unconnected archived CLI command tree. These sources either are not product code or can pollute semantic retrieval with synthetic, sample, or obsolete implementations.
design: Implement only .tldrignore patterns using Git-ignore syntax. Do not add filename heuristics that could hide active files such as test_recognizer.rs, test_idioms.rs, or fixed_shape_benchmark.rs.
acceptance_criteria: Root-anchored docs/, continuum/, and bench/ are excluded; tests/, fixtures/, and examples/ are excluded recursively; crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/archived/ is excluded; active production source and scripts remain visible; a no-embed tree scan confirms the expected corpus reduction.
close_reason: Local .tldrignore policy added and verified with a no-embed corpus scan: 49 non-product/sample files removed, active production and scripts retained.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY 2026-07-28: .tldrignore now excludes root docs/, continuum/, and bench/; recursive tests/, fixtures/, and examples/; and crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/archived/. A no-embed tldr tree scan reduced supported source candidates from 560 to 511 and reported zero excluded-policy paths still visible.
