title: Rank findings and approve the smallest pre-backend optimization set
description: Individual audits can produce locally attractive changes that overlap, damage retrieval quality or add complexity without moving the 30-minute target. Synthesize all evidence into one decision before implementation: which mistakes are real, which costs are intentional, which fixes compose, and how much cold-build and delta time remains after applying defensible work-avoidance and orchestration changes.
acceptance_criteria: Produce an evidence table for every candidate with affected documents/tokens/executions, expected and upper-bound wall saving, measured quality effect, memory/recovery impact, complexity and confidence. Select a minimal ordered fix set with dependencies and dedicated Beads tasks, explicitly reject unjustified work, estimate whether the 30-minute target is plausible without backend/model/cloud changes, and define the point at which backend evaluation should begin.

title: Prove delta indexing performs only necessary embedding work
description: A cloud or faster backend is unnecessary for normal edits if delta indexing embeds only changed semantic text. The architecture has content hashes, shared corpus filtering and an in-memory writable store, but it needs workload evidence for small edits, line shifts, renames, deletes and edit bursts. Detect any path that re-plans, re-tokenizes or re-embeds unchanged documents, or accidentally escalates to a full rebuild.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark and trace one small function edit, large function edit, metadata-only line shift, rename, delete and multi-file burst. For each, report files planned, documents compared, cache hits, new embeddings, model executions, cache writes and publication latency. Zero-content-change cases perform zero inference; changed cases embed only output-changing documents; any violation becomes a dedicated correctness/fix issue.
notes:
2026-07-28 live daemon probe on tldr-code (511 files, 15,020 vectors, Arctic-M): mtime-only watcher.rs event advanced artifact generation 2->3, vector count unchanged, delta model requests stayed 0 (zero inference), but delta-batch took about 4.8s and lazily loading the delta runner raised RSS ~864MB->~1.44GB. One-word module-comment edit advanced generation 3->4 and embedded 8 documents in 1 model request; observed delta-batch about 16.8s. Restoring the word advanced generation 4->5 and embedded 8 documents in 1 model request; observed roughly 21.8s. RSS ended ~1.93GB peak from ~864MB baseline. Git content restored; only pre-existing .beads/interactions.jsonl remains dirty. Static trace identifies apply_semantic_delta_batch collecting snapshot.semantic_source_chunks(project) for the entire corpus before selecting changed paths as a likely avoidable planning/composition cost. Dedicated bug required by acceptance.
Fast-path evidence added 2026-07-28. Live watcher on 511 files/15,042 vectors: no-content events 1.18-1.23s, zero delta sessions/requests when cold; one-word edit/restore 1.49-1.99s, exactly 8 documents, one request per event, one reused session. Repeated shapes plateaued near 1.40 GiB after ONNX warmup. tldr cache clear removed 11 project index/cache files (562.2 MiB); clean project-store rebuild completed in 255.8s with 15,042 content-hash cache hits, zero new vectors, and post-reset deltas retained the fast path. This is not the full acceptance matrix (rename/delete/burst/large edit remain), so leave open. Evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-07-28-file-scoped-delta-fast-path.md.

title: Quantify remaining cross-window packing and dummy-row waste
description: The first mixed-batch promotion improved representative inference by 14.5%, but durability windows of 128 vectors may still force partially filled fixed-shape buckets to execute with dummy rows. Durability and inference packing are independent concerns; coupling them can waste compute. Determine the exact remaining waste after the shipped promotion and evaluate the simplest bounded cross-window packing design without changing model outputs or recovery guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Using identical document order, report real rows, dummy rows, tensor cells, executions and measured latency by shape before/after the shipped promotion; calculate a defensible saving bound; verify whether packing across durability windows is possible while caching each completed 128-vector checkpoint; document bounded memory and crash semantics; and create an implementation task only if the measured full-pipeline value is material.
notes:
INTERMEDIATE — NOT FINAL: authoritative full baseline before shipped promotion: 51,171 real rows / 74,308 capacity, 23,137 dummy. Shape utilization: 128=41,846/51,008 (82.0%); 256=3,705/12,800 (28.9%); 384=2,034/5,460 (37.3%); 512=3,586/5,040 (71.2%). Shipped promotion improved a representative corpus but has no post-change full-corpus row accounting yet.
INTERMEDIATE FULL-CORPUS RESULT — NOT YET ISOLATED (2026-07-28): controlled empty-cache run with installed mixed-bucket promotion + approved .tldrignore corpus policy completed in 3,460.211s (57m40s), versus 4,431.280s baseline (73m51s): -971.069s/-21.9% combined. Inference 3,026.470s vs 3,894.830s: -868.360s/-22.3%. Files 559->511; inferred rows 51,171->49,212; calls 2,217->1,781 (-436/-19.7%); capacity 74,308->63,132; dummy rows 23,137->13,920 (-39.8%); row utilization 68.9%->78.0%; weighted cell padding 61.5%->54.6%. Post-change shapes: 128=751 calls, 34,144/48,064 rows (71.0%, all 13,920 remaining dummy); 256=232 calls, 7,424/7,424; 384=210, 2,940/2,940; 512=588, 4,704/4,704. Promotion eliminates dummy rows in longer shapes but remains bounded by 385 durability windows. This run proves combined production value, not batching-only causality, because corpus membership also changed. Artifacts: docs/benchmarks/2026-07-28-clean-mixed-batch/{RUN_CONTEXT.md,SUMMARY.md,report.json,report.units.jsonl}. Acceptance remains open for identical-order isolation, cross-window crash semantics, and an implementation decision.

title: Audit embedding-text composition at fixed-shape token boundaries
description: Arctic-M executes fixed 128/256/384/512-token shapes. Low-value optional fields can push a document just above a boundary and multiply tensor work even when the added text contributes little retrieval value. Current metrics show bucket totals but not which fields caused promotions or whether composition repeats information already present in code.
acceptance_criteria: Measure documents and tensor cells within configurable margins above each boundary; attribute tokens to required code versus each optional field; estimate executions/cells saved by candidate composition changes; test retrieval equivalence or improvement on the frozen oracle; and create narrowly scoped fix tasks only where benefit justifies quality risk. The audit must not solve this by truncating code silently.

title: Explain and audit the 51,174-document chunk explosion
description: The clean corpus turns 559 files into 51,174 embedding documents, averaging about 92 documents per file. This may be correct structural coverage or may expose tiny fragments, repeated context, duplicate representations, fallback splitting, or low-information nodes that waste inference. Trace document production by planner path and quantify exact duplicates, normalized duplicates, near-identical overlaps, tiny units, fallback units and repeated metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Account for document counts by source file, language, structural kind and planner path; publish size/token distributions and top outliers; quantify exact and normalized duplicate embedding texts and overlap; identify root causes rather than merely thresholds; evaluate representative merge/drop/dedup candidates against the retrieval oracle; and create fix tasks only for proven waste.
notes:
INTERMEDIATE ROOT-CAUSE AUDIT (generation 3, 511 files): deterministic no-inference replay exactly reproduced 49,215 documents and 5,224,463 tokens. Mean/p50/p90/p95/max chunks per file = 96.3/55/206/347/1,083. Roles: AstChild 47,495; ParentSummary 1,716; TokenizerFallback 4; ParseFallback 0. Depth-1 chunks: 43,196. Root named nodes: 42,194, dominated by line_comment 30,316, use_declaration 2,922, attribute_item 1,502 versus function_item 4,065. The first three categories are 70.6% of documents but ~15.9% of source bytes. Only 13,404 chunks have a qualified symbol; 32,146 documents are 33-64 tokens. Source coverage is 10,087,969 planned bytes versus 10,087,901 source bytes with 68 bytes overlap. Root cause is proven: preserve_named_roots treats Tree-sitter trivia/context nodes as standalone semantic owners. Fix tracked in TLDR-1hld.12. Duplicate/near-duplicate and retrieval-oracle acceptance remain open until the fix is evaluated.
POST-FIX EVIDENCE: release-mode generation-15 replay reduced documents 49,215 -> 15,020 (-69.5%) and tokens 5,224,463 -> 3,902,146 (-25.3%) with complete 511-file coverage and unchanged 68-byte bounded overlap. Standalone root owners collapsed: line_comment 30,316 -> 1,375; use_declaration 2,922 -> 35; attribute_item 1,502 -> 29. Fix remains tracked in TLDR-1hld.12; production rebuild/retrieval oracle still pending.
ROOT-CAUSE METHOD AND REASONING — FINAL NARRATIVE (2026-07-28): We began from the authoritative 73m51.28s empty-state run, where inference alone consumed 3,894.830s (87.9%). The first question was therefore not how to make ONNX faster, but why 559 source files became 51,174 model inputs. We deliberately replayed the retained artifact generation through the planner without inference so discovery did not require another hour-long build. The replay reproduced the production count and token total, then classified every output by planner role, AST depth/root kind, token bucket, symbol ownership, source coverage and overlap. This eliminated several plausible explanations: parser failure was not responsible (0 ParseFallback), tokenizer fallback was negligible (4 chunks), duplicated/overlapping source was negligible (68 bytes), and the corpus was not being repeatedly expanded by a second representation (47,495 outputs were ordinary AstChild chunks). The decisive evidence was structural: 30,316 line comments, 2,922 use declarations and 1,502 attributes were independently preserved named roots. Those three categories were 70.6% of documents but only about 15.9% of source bytes; 32,146 documents were only 33-64 tokens and only 13,404 had qualified symbols. Tree-sitter correctly marks comments/imports/attributes as named nodes, but the planner incorrectly equated every named root with a retrieval-bearing semantic owner. That boundary mistake, not the parser or embedding backend, explained the document explosion. EXPECTED PERFORMANCE MECHANISM: coalescing context into declarations would not discard much text, so token reduction was expected to be smaller than document reduction. The speed hypothesis was instead that fewer document objects would mean fewer durability windows, fewer fixed-shape model calls, fewer dummy/capacity rows, fewer cache writes, less vector assembly and less publication work. This predicted a potentially large wall-time win even if total tokens fell modestly. The production result confirmed that mechanism: documents -69.5%, tokens -25.3%, windows -69.4%, calls -41.2%, capacity rows -69.6%, cache-write time -69.0%, vector assembly -64.7%, inference -49.2%, total wall -48.0%. The broader duplicate/near-duplicate audit remains open, but this dominant root cause and its fix are proven.

title: Audit corpus membership for irrelevant and accidentally indexed sources
description: The semantic corpus includes fixtures, performance corpora, archived commands, scripts and continuum/reference material. Some may be valuable search targets; others may be accidental linear inference cost. Current aggregate metrics cannot distinguish them. Classify files/documents/tokens by directory and source role, identify generated/copied/archived/vendor/benchmark material, and measure whether each category contributes useful results to the frozen and representative query sets.
acceptance_criteria: Report files, documents, tokens and projected inference time by corpus category; list current include/exclude rule provenance; identify only evidence-supported exclusion candidates; quantify recall/MRR impact or query coverage for each candidate; and create a separate fix task for every approved policy change. No blanket exclusion of tests or fixtures is accepted without retrieval evidence.
notes: INTERMEDIATE — NOT FINAL: retained per-file planning evidence includes 20 continuum/ files and at least 25 paths whose names match perf-fixture, performance, benchmark or fixture directories. Their planning time is negligible; their document/token/inference share and retrieval usefulness remain unknown until TLDR-1hld.1 supplies document lineage. Do not exclude them yet. IGNORE VERIFICATION (2026-07-28): applying git check-ignore --no-index to all 559 accepted semantic_file_plan identities returned zero matches. Full semantic enumeration uses ProjectWalker defaults, whose canonical config enables .gitignore, global Git ignore, .git/info/exclude, parent ignore traversal, hidden filtering and .tldrignore. Therefore these suspicious categories are present because current ignore policy does not exclude them, not because semantic walking bypassed Git ignore rules. Known separate edge case TLDR-boa.8 concerns positive negation in .tldrignore, not ordinary accepted .gitignored files.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: FIRECRAWL RESEARCH 2026-07-28: ignore v0.4.x is already the appropriate specialized Rust traversal/matching library; gix-ignore 0.22 is a lower-level parser/search utility and would require composing traversal and Git ignore-source discovery ourselves. Full semantic enumeration currently configures one WalkBuilder with Git sources plus .tldrignore, so rules are evaluated together with precedence during traversal, not text-concatenated or expanded into a separate ignored-path list. Important semantic choice: custom .tldrignore has higher precedence than other ignore files; therefore the effective policy is not a simple deny-wins union when negation is allowed. Confirm whether .tldrignore is intended to override/re-include .gitignore entries or only add exclusions. Current project uses ignore 0.4.25; 0.4.30+ build_matchers may eliminate the separate single-file matcher path.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: IGNORE POLICY UPDATE — FINAL FOR TLDR-boa.8: additive Git + .tldrignore semantics are implemented and verified. This removes policy drift and prevents .tldrignore from reopening Git-ignored corpus files, including nested rules and delta/deleted-path checks. It does not itself remove currently accepted fixtures/benchmarks; those remain legitimate inputs to this corpus-utility audit until evidence supports new .tldrignore exclusions.

title: Build a no-rebuild semantic workload accounting report
description: The retained benchmark reports total files, documents, tokens, windows and executions, but it does not provide one joinable document-level accounting table. Without that table, every optimization estimate risks relying on guesses or requiring another 74-minute build. Extract or deterministically replay planning from retained artifacts and emit bounded aggregate data covering source category, document identity, content hash, token count, selected fixed shape, window, cache outcome and measured/estimated execution cost.
acceptance_criteria: One documented command or analysis produces reproducible aggregate counts matching the authoritative baseline within explained tolerances: 559 files, 51,174 documents, 5,511,333 tokens, 400 windows and 2,217 executions. It supports the remaining epic investigations without running model inference and records provenance for every input artifact.
notes:
INTERMEDIATE — NOT FINAL: retained artifacts provide 559 semantic_file_plan units, 400 windows, 2,217 per-batch records, token totals and exact shape/capacity/latency, but omit per-document file identity, content hash, structural kind and token-field attribution. The no-rebuild report therefore needs deterministic planner replay joined to retained batch evidence; it does not need ONNX inference. Initial consistency checks match baseline totals: 559 files, 51,174 checked inputs, 5,511,333 tokens, 51,171 embedded rows + 3 hits, 400 windows and 2,217 executions.
INTERMEDIATE ACCOUNTING PROTOTYPE: a temporary read-only Rust replay against GenerationSnapshot + the exact Arctic-M TokenBudget reproduced the active production totals (511 files, 49,215 chunks, 5,224,463 tokens) without ONNX inference in ~2 minutes. It emitted per-file counts, role/depth/token distributions, source coverage/overlap, top outliers and root AST-kind counts. The prototype was removed after diagnosis; acceptance remains open until this becomes a documented bounded production/reporting command rather than ad-hoc instrumentation.

title: (EPIC) Eliminate avoidable semantic work before changing the embedding backend
description: The corrected empty-state semantic build is reliable but takes 4,431.28s for 559 files and 51,174 documents. Inference consumes 3,894.83s (87.9%), yet changing the model, runtime, hardware, or cloud provider would be premature until we prove whether TLDR is embedding irrelevant corpus, creating redundant or excessively granular documents, crossing fixed-shape token boundaries for low-value metadata, repeating tokenization, flushing underfilled inference work, or paying unnecessary durability costs. This epic investigates work avoidance and orchestration mistakes with the current Arctic-M output contract. It is intentionally separate from model/provider evaluation: first determine whether TLDR is asking the model to do unnecessary work.
design: Use the completed 2026-07-28 clean benchmark as the authoritative baseline. Start with read-only accounting and deterministic replay over retained artifacts; do not require another 74-minute build merely to discover distributions already present in metrics/artifacts. For every suspected waste class, record affected files/documents/tokens/model executions, estimated upper-bound wall-time saving, retrieval-quality risk, implementation complexity and recovery/durability impact. Prefer simple removal or reuse over new schedulers and caches. No optimization ships from inference-free estimates alone: corpus/chunk/text changes require the frozen n=52 retrieval oracle plus representative real queries; scheduling/persistence changes require document/vector equivalence and crash-recovery contracts. Do not mix this epic with cloud/model selection. Conclude with an evidence-ranked decision: fix, retain intentionally, or defer.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible audit explains why 559 files become 51,174 embedding documents and accounts for corpus categories, exact/normalized duplication, chunk-size distribution, token bucket boundary crossings, padding/dummy work, repeated tokenization, cache/delta reuse and durability-write cost. Each finding includes measured scope and an honest saving bound. Any proposed change has a simple design, dependencies, quality/correctness gates and a dedicated follow-up task. The epic closes only after we can state which suspected mistakes are real, which are intentional tradeoffs, and whether work avoidance plus orchestration can plausibly meet the 30-minute target before any backend/model/cloud change.
notes:
INTERMEDIATE DISCOVERY — NOT FINAL (2026-07-28): The retained clean-build report confirms 51,171 real inference rows executed in 74,308 row slots, leaving 23,137 dummy rows across 2,217 model executions. By shape: 128-token 82.0% utilized; 256-token 28.9%; 384-token 37.3%; 512-token 71.2%. This is the pre-promotion authoritative full baseline; the shipped mixed-batch improvement has only representative-corpus evidence, so remaining full-corpus waste is not yet known. Per-file planning identities show 20 accepted continuum/ files and at least 25 paths matching fixture/performance/benchmark naming, which is evidence for a corpus audit but not proof they should be excluded. The retained report can reconstruct window/batch/timing data and file identities, but not document-to-file/token/field lineage; TLDR-1hld.1 must obtain that through deterministic planning replay without model inference. No optimization or time saving is approved yet.
INTERMEDIATE CORRECTNESS DISCOVERY 2026-07-28: live ignore-policy reload currently affects only future watcher filtering. It does not purge already-published artifact/vector records, and a resident same-model semantic warm can skip corpus freshness. TLDR-1hld.11 implements a correctness-first full-generation rebuild on ignore-policy changes, including a queued follow-up when policy changes during an active build. This finding is intermediate until focused and crate-level validation passes.
VERIFIED CORRECTNESS RESULT 2026-07-28 (TLDR-1hld.11): ignore-policy changes are now corpus-generation events. They trigger a single-flight full artifact/vector replacement, coalesce repeated events, and queue one follow-up when an older build is active. A regression test proves a newly ignored source disappears from the replacement artifact generation. Normal semantic queries remain index-only with no ignore-file latency. Code validation passed; no production embedding rebuild was run as part of this code-only implementation.
MEASURED CLEAN RUN 2026-07-28 — COMBINED CORPUS + MIXED BATCH (not isolated): latest installed CLI/worker, empty artifact/vector/document caches, preserved model weights. Wall 73m51s->57m40s (-16m11s/-21.9%); inference 64m55s->50m26s (-14m28s/-22.3%); calls 2,217->1,781; dummy rows 23,137->13,920; files 559->511; inferred rows 51,171->49,212. All remaining dummy rows are in 128-token batches; 256/384/512 row capacity is fully occupied by promotion. 385 durability windows still constrain packing, so cross-window carry is the remaining evidenced batching lever. Peak worker RSS ~1.64 GiB. Fresh daemon loaded 49,215 vectors within one second; semantic smoke query repeat 70ms process wall / 21ms internal, 0 failures. Full artifacts retained under docs/benchmarks/2026-07-28-clean-mixed-batch/.
INTERMEDIATE — NOT FINAL (2026-07-28 planner audit): exact replay of generation 3 reproduced 49,215 chunks/5,224,463 tokens without inference. 30,316 documents (61.6%) are individual root line_comment nodes; adding 2,922 use declarations and 1,502 attributes means 70.6% of all documents represent these context/trivia declarations while covering only ~15.9% of source bytes. 47,495 chunks are normal AstChild, only 4 tokenizer fallbacks, 0 parse fallbacks, and 68 overlap bytes, so the inflation is not reparsing, errors, fallback windows, or duplicated source. 43,196 chunks are depth-1; 32,146 are only 33-64 tokens; only 13,404 carry a qualified symbol. New task TLDR-1hld.12 captures the simple fix: merge comments/attributes with semantic owners and coalesce imports/trivia under the existing token budget, retaining full deterministic source coverage and bulk/delta parity.
CORRECTION/NUANCE from the same flow trace: FileFactsParser parses each source once to produce the shared artifact generation, but semantic plan_file subsequently calls parse_with_path again because the persisted semantic source artifact contains full source text, not a reusable Tree-sitter tree. Thus the cold flow performs two Tree-sitter parses per indexed file. The first measured artifact AST phase was 2.64s; the second is folded into the 145.647s semantic-planning phase and is not separately timed. This is real duplicate work and should eventually be measured/removed, but it cannot explain the 3,026s inference bottleneck or the 30,316 comment documents.
TLDR-1hld.12 CLOSED with clean production evidence: context-root coalescing cut documents 69.5% and end-to-end clean wall time 48.0% (57m40s -> 30m00.68s), with retrieval checks passing. Semantic planning itself rose 14.7%, now a separately visible optimization opportunity.
PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT LADDER AND DECISION RECORD — FINAL (2026-07-28): Baseline: reliable empty-state Arctic-M build at 4,431.28s (73m51.28s), 559 files, 51,174 documents, 2,217 inference calls, 23,137 dummy rows, inference 3,894.830s. Stage 1 combined correctness/corpus cleanup plus mixed-shape batch promotion: 3,460.211s (57m40.21s, -21.9%), 511 files, 49,215 documents, 1,781 calls, 13,920 dummy rows, inference 3,026.470s. This proved orchestration/corpus work mattered but also showed document count barely changed; padding alone could not reach 30 minutes. Stage 2 no-inference planner audit found that named Tree-sitter trivia/context roots accounted for 70.6% of documents while carrying 15.9% of bytes. The approved smallest fix was context-root coalescing, because it removed model execution units without dropping source or changing the model/backend. Final clean installed-binary result: 1,800.680s (30m00.68s), 511 files, 15,020 documents, 1,048 calls, 4,189 dummy rows, inference 1,537.727s. Improvement is -48.0% versus the immediately prior clean run and -59.3% versus the original baseline, saving 43m50.60s. The 30-minute target was therefore met with the same Snowflake Arctic-M model and fixed-shape ORT backend; no cloud/provider/model swap was required. WHY THE ORIGINAL EXPECTATION WAS SOUND: per-document fixed costs matter independently of token count. Each standalone comment/import/attribute consumed planner metadata, a position in a 128-document durability window, batch capacity, inference scheduling, cache persistence, a vector record, verification and publication. Merging context into its owner retained 74.7% of tokens but removed 69.5% of documents, which reduced windows and storage work roughly in proportion to documents and model calls by 41.2%. Measured phase deltas validate this model: inference -49.2%, cache write -69.0%, vector assembly -64.7%, generation/records 3.125s->0.834s, verification 0.817s->0.278s and publication 4.014s->1.144s. LIMIT/next evidence: semantic planning increased 14.7% to 167.017s, so future work should target repeated candidate tokenization and the second semantic Tree-sitter parse (TLDR-1hld.13) without undoing the proven ownership contract. The broader epic remains open for duplicate, delta, durability and tokenization audits, but backend replacement is no longer justified merely to hit the 30-minute target.

title: Unify hierarchical build and atomic-unit timing with existing metrics
description: Extend the existing semantic BuildMetrics/PhaseRecord mechanism instead of adding a tracing framework. Give one build a run_id and correlate daemon/artifact producer/embed-worker process roles. Record major phase wall times for scan, AST parse, artifact write, semantic planning/chunking, cache lookup, model load, inference, vector assembly, verification and publication. For atomic units such as file parse, planning window and inference batch, keep aggregate count/total/min/max/percentiles plus a bounded slowest-N list by default; an explicit detailed metrics mode may stream raw unit records as JSONL. Surface the same machine-readable report through the build/diagnostic command.
acceptance_criteria: Running the documented timing command on a codebase returns total AST parse wall time, per-language file counts and timing distribution, slowest parsed files, every semantic phase, per-window and inference-batch timings, process role and run correlation, total build wall time and concurrency semantics. Aggregate mode has measured overhead below 1% or an explicitly justified bound and bounded memory; raw per-unit output is opt-in and streaming; schema and fake/small-corpus tests verify clocks, aggregation, nesting/correlation and malformed/incomplete process reports.
close_reason: Correlated run/process/phase and bounded atomic-unit timing implemented, including AST language/file and opt-in raw JSONL.

title: (BUG) Build timings are fragmented and cannot explain component or atomic-unit cost
description:
## Problem
Timing exists in disconnected forms. Semantic BuildMetrics records phases, batches, cache, RSS and throughput for `tldr embed --metrics`, while callgraph construction exposes env-gated scan/parse/compose totals through `TLDR_PHASE_TIMING`. Fresh init/warm spans artifact ingestion, AST parsing, daemon orchestration, worker planning, cache lookup, inference, vector assembly, verification and publication across processes, but there is no correlated report. Normal users therefore cannot reliably answer how much total time AST parsing took, which language/files were slow, how long each semantic window took, or which process owned elapsed time.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `TLDR_PHASE_TIMING=1 tldr calls <path> -l <language> --respect-ignore -f json`; observe one stderr line with aggregate scan/parse/compose/total only when the callgraph rebuild path executes.
2. Run `tldr embed <path> --metrics <report.json>` with no owning daemon; observe a separate semantic-only report with no correlated artifact/AST process timing.
3. Run the normal installed `tldr warm <path>` flow; observe that there is no documented metrics output that correlates daemon, artifact producer and embedding worker or reports per-language AST/file timing.

## Expected Behavior
One documented build metrics surface should correlate the full run, expose major component wall times, summarize bounded atomic-unit timings, and optionally stream exact raw unit timings for detailed diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria: A single build metrics artifact correlates the full run and process roles; reports wall time for each major structural and semantic component; reports atomic-unit aggregates with count/total/min/max/percentiles and bounded slowest-unit identities; offers opt-in raw per-unit JSONL when exact individual timings are required; answers AST parse time by language and file population; distinguishes wall time from summed concurrent work; has measured low overhead in aggregate mode; and is exposed through a documented user command rather than only an environment-gated stderr line.
close_reason: tldr warm now emits one correlated structural+semantic metrics artifact and optional exact unit JSONL.

title: Run clean-install semantic release certification
description: After implementation and focused gates pass, repeat the full removal/build/install/init/warm/query workflow from empty state using the benchmark protocol. Do not seed or resume the current benchmark job. Capture binary provenance, structural readiness, semantic phase progress, total time, CPU/RSS/disk, cancellation/stop behavior and installed CLI/hook/MCP results.
acceptance_criteria: The documented benchmark proves all epic acceptance gates from empty state, publishes a fresh semantic generation, returns a successful installed semantic query, stops cleanly, updates the benchmark report and relevant epics, and records exact commit/machine/corpus metadata for reproduction.

title: Certify cache-backed recovery and a fresh installed build
description: Use the existing shared contract runner for four semantic-owned recovery boundaries: kill before first durable cache write, kill after a completed window but before publication, compatible restart with retained cache, and incompatible restart. Then repeat the inventoried clean/build/install/init/warm/query benchmark from empty state, capture provenance and performance evidence, and update linked Beads records. Daemon/launchd stop remains tracked by TLDR-cxa.3.
acceptance_criteria: All four scenarios are hermetic and deterministic; compatible restart reuses completed inference, incompatible job metadata does not consume retry budget, and old-or-new generation visibility is atomic. Repository quality gates and semantic smoke/certification pass apart from explicitly linked pre-existing failures. The installed fresh build publishes, queries successfully, records commit/machine/corpus/cache/progress/time/CPU/RSS/disk data, and updates the benchmark and linked issues.
notes:
INTERMEDIATE ONLY — NOT FINAL clean-install certification at ~20m: installed release, empty runtime state, 559 AST parses complete, 91 durable windows (~11,648 vectors), 155 semantic files planned, no retry/crash, worker ~909% CPU/~1.41 GiB RSS. Publication, final metrics, daemon init and installed semantic query are pending.
FINAL CERTIFICATION: all four recovery contracts pass; clean installed empty-state build published 51,174 vectors in 73m51.28s with zero retries/failures; daemon became warm within 13.83s after init; installed semantic query passed in 1.70s wall/40ms indexed search. Busy-worker daemon stop separately passed in 0.21s with no orphan/respawn. Quality gates pass except linked pre-existing TLDR-jci4. Full evidence retained under docs/benchmarks/2026-07-28-corrected-semantic-build/.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make cancellation and daemon stop terminate the full worker tree
description: Define cancellation ownership across daemon, BulkWorker and tldr-embed-worker, and align tldr daemon stop with launchd supervision. Stop must cancel the job, terminate/reap the worker, stop or unload the managed service as specified, and report observed process/service state rather than registry state alone.
acceptance_criteria: Busy-worker cancel and daemon stop finish within 5 seconds; no daemon/worker remains orphaned; launchd does not immediately respawn after an explicit stop; restart remains available through an explicit start/init action; tests close TLDR-cxa.3's false-success scenario on macOS and cover portable child reaping.
notes: Implemented shared daemon-lifetime BuildCancellation in IndexManager; daemon shutdown now cancels the active bulk worker. Explicit macOS stop unloads launchd while preserving the plist, waits on the recorded daemon PID for up to 5s, and refuses false-success cleanup if PID remains alive. Installed-release certification during active model_load stopped daemon PID 71336 and worker PID 71359 in 0.21s; launchd service absent afterward; no tldr daemon/worker remained.
close_reason: Closed

title: Profile and remove the measured cold-build bottleneck
description: Measure the corrected cache-backed pipeline before choosing an optimization. Identify whether planning, inference or publication dominates, then implement the smallest change that materially improves that phase while preserving document/vector/retrieval equivalence and acceptable RSS. Parallel planning, tokenizer memoization and inference tuning are options only when measurements justify their added complexity.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible empty-state record identifies phase time, throughput, CPU utilization and peak RSS; the retained change materially improves the measured dominant phase and preserves the frozen semantic oracle; the 30-minute M2 Max target is evaluated honestly and becomes a mandatory platform gate only after a reproducible pass; if the target is missed, evidence identifies the next dominant phase before any further design is approved.
notes:
INTERMEDIATE ONLY — NOT FINAL profiling evidence at ~20m: AST complete (559 files); 91 durable semantic windows; 519 inference batches; model download ~100s; semantic inference is dominant; worker ~909% CPU/~1.41 GiB RSS. Planning/inference totals and 30m target remain undecided until report closes.
INTERMEDIATE ONLY — NOT FINAL: empty-cache run crossed 30m before publication (155 durable windows/~19,840 vectors; 235 files planned; 880 inference batches). The target is missed for this run; full phase report is still required before selecting any inference change.
FINAL BASELINE: 73m51.28s total; inference 64m54.83s (87.9%) is the measured dominant phase. Planning 2m47.487s, cache write 3m39.796s, model 1m42.560s, publication 3.273s. 51,174 chunks at 13.138 embeddings/s, 400 windows/2,217 batches, ~813% average CPU, 1.65 GiB peak RSS. The 30m target failed; planning parallelism is not justified. Next change must be the smallest safe fixed-shape inference throughput improvement.
IMPLEMENTED/MEASURED: fixed-shape planner now promotes shorter inputs into otherwise-dummy rows of an already-required partial longer-sequence batch. It preserves the finite shape set, batch-one query behavior, fixed 128-vector durability window, immediate cache checkpoints and bounded memory. Identical 1,538-chunk empty-cache before/after: inference 122.839s -> 105.019s (14.5% faster), executions 76 -> 64 (15.8% fewer), total 140.697s -> 123.822s (12.0% faster), peak RSS +7.1% and still ~1.40 GiB. Arctic-M fixed-shape executor matches/passes FastEmbed throughput gates. 30m full-corpus target remains unproven and must not be claimed without another full run.
close_reason: Closed

title: Stream worker events and expose live semantic progress
description: Refactor BulkWorker to consume worker stdout concurrently and feed a shared versioned progress snapshot. Extend worker events and daemon status with phase and planned/completed files, chunks, batches, vectors, elapsed time, throughput, retries and checkpoint age. Preserve bounded messages and fail clearly on protocol violations.
acceptance_criteria: A slow test worker produces visible status changes within 5 seconds while alive; stdout cannot block; events are ordered/validated; malformed and oversized events fail deterministically; compact/JSON status remain schema-tested; no percentage is emitted before a valid denominator exists.

title: Implement cache-backed windows, live progress and atomic publication
description: Process the deterministic semantic stream in one fixed maximum window size, initially 128 vectors. For every window, reuse compatible embedding-cache entries, infer only misses, and immediately persist new vectors through the existing cache path. After durability, emit a small live event and reconcile advisory job counters. On restart, repeat the scan and cache lookup. Build and verify the complete VectorStore, then publish through the existing atomic generation path. Do not add staged vectors or a cross-store transaction.
acceptance_criteria: A corpus larger than 128 vectors produces multiple live window events; a one-window corpus and final partial window work; status changes within 5 seconds and reports phase, files seen/total when cheaply known, cache hits, new vectors, elapsed and retries; termination after a completed window causes those vectors to be cache hits on restart with no repeated inference; a crash before publication leaves the old generation visible; only the fully verified new generation activates; malformed/oversized worker events fail without deadlock.
close_reason: 128-vector cache-backed windows, live bounded events, reconciled status, retry recovery, and measured atomic publication implemented and certified.

title: Reuse stable semantic identities and invalidate incompatible jobs
description: Stop hashing the full WorkerBuildRequest. Project worker compatibility from the existing source/artifact digest, ManifestId and EmbeddingRecipeId, excluding temporary paths, retry policy, PID, timestamps and transport details. Do not introduce another public BuildRecipe. Detect incompatible worker/job metadata before model load, record the reason, replace the advisory job record and begin a new scan without consuming retry budget. Leave cache reuse to existing cache-key compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Requests differing only in temp path or process/transport metadata select identical semantic identities; changes to source digest, model, embedding schema or output-affecting chunk configuration change the appropriate existing identity; incompatible job metadata restarts without spending retry budget; compatible cache entries remain reusable only when their existing keys match; TLDR-cxa.2 recipe-change coverage passes.
close_reason: Stable manifest/source identity projection and incompatible advisory-job invalidation implemented with regression coverage.

title: Build a deterministic cold-build profiling and fault harness
description: Create a reusable harness over the shared contract-test architecture that starts from empty structural/semantic state, records planning/cache/inference/staging/publication metrics, samples worker/parent CPU and RSS, and can terminate at deterministic batch/publication boundaries. Freeze the 558-file tldr-code benchmark metadata and a small fast corpus for routine tests.
acceptance_criteria: The harness emits machine-readable planned totals, phase timings, throughput, cache hits/misses, checkpoints, retries, CPU/RSS and final query result; supports uninterrupted, cancel, kill and restart modes; uses isolated state; and reproduces the current 0/1 checkpoint defect before implementation.

title: Baseline and specify the cache-backed recovery contract
description: Freeze the smallest correct ownership model and reproduce the current defect in the existing contract-test runner. The embedding cache is durable vector truth, the active generation is publication truth, and the job ledger is advisory status/retry metadata. Capture one cold baseline with phase, cache, elapsed, CPU/RSS and publication data. Document that restart may repeat planning and cache lookup but must not repeat compatible cached inference; an exact whole-corpus chunk plan is not required.
acceptance_criteria: One isolated scenario fails on the current implementation because live progress, cache reconciliation or restart reuse is missing; one machine-readable cold baseline is captured; docs define cache/progress/publication ownership, compatibility/invalidation, atomic visibility and timing vocabulary; the timing contract distinguishes run, process, phase and atomic unit plus wall time versus concurrent summed work; the design explicitly rejects a duplicate recipe, staged-vector ledger, cross-store transaction, whole-corpus preplan, dual count/time checkpoint policy and a second tracing framework.
close_reason: Recovery ownership/timing contract documented; deterministic baseline contracts added and passing.

title: Fresh semantic build has no enforced completion SLO
description: The project now retains a reproducible empty-state release benchmark with source/binary provenance, machine/corpus data, correlated phase/unit timing, progress, CPU/RSS/disk evidence, publication, daemon warm, query, and lifecycle verification. The corrected build completes in 73m51.28s but misses the aspirational 30m target, so 30m is documented honestly and is not promoted to a mandatory platform gate.
acceptance_criteria: The completed benchmark and raw reports are versioned under docs/benchmarks; phase regressions are attributable; publication/query are verified; 30m becomes mandatory only after a reproducible pass, and the current miss identifies inference as the next dominant phase.
close_reason: Closed

title: Semantic planning and token-fit accounting are sequential and uninstrumented
description: Semantic planning was suspected to dominate and lacked timing. The corrected instrumentation measures every semantic file plan and the aggregate phase. The completed 559-file baseline measured planning at 167.487s (3.8% total) versus inference at 3,894.830s (87.9%); therefore parallel planning/tokenizer complexity is not justified. The measured inference fix is tracked and completed in TLDR-bjux.14.
acceptance_criteria: Per-file and aggregate planning/token timing is reproducible; the complete baseline establishes its budget and relative cost; no parallelism is added when measurement shows it is not a material bottleneck; deterministic documents remain unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Parent buffers worker events until child exit
description:
BulkWorker polls child.try_wait and calls read_events only after the child exits. WorkerEvent::Started and future BatchCommitted/progress messages are therefore not consumed live and cannot update daemon status during a long build. This also prevents bounded protocol backpressure once real per-batch events are emitted.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a test worker that emits Started and multiple progress JSONL frames before sleeping and exiting.
2. Drive it through BulkWorker::build.
3. Poll parent-visible state before child exit.
4. Observe no event is processed because read_events is called only after try_wait returns a terminal status.
acceptance_criteria: Read bounded JSONL worker events concurrently while the child is alive, validate ordering and schema, update shared progress immediately, prevent stdout pipe blockage, and retain the final completion/error contract. Tests cover slow workers, malformed/oversized events and child exit races.
notes: FIXED: BulkWorker reads bounded JSONL concurrently while the child is alive, validates ordering/schema/size, updates progress immediately, prevents pipe blockage, and reaps the child. Slow, malformed, oversized, cancellation and exit-race paths are covered.
close_reason: Closed

title: Semantic build status lacks phase and quantitative progress
description: Semantic status formerly exposed only building/busy. It now streams bounded worker JSONL events while the child lives and exposes phase, files seen/total, completed windows, cache hits, new vectors, last-window duration, elapsed time, and retries. It intentionally avoids inventing an exact percentage before the vector denominator is known.
acceptance_criteria: Status changes within 5 seconds of worker start and exposes the versioned progress fields used by the epic; cold/failed states remain honest; progress events are bounded and consumed live; no misleading percentage is required.
close_reason: Closed

title: Embedding cache progress is disconnected from the durable job ledger
description: The old worker ledger contradicted the embedding cache. The corrected simple ownership model makes compatible cache records authoritative for completed inference and keeps job counters advisory. Every window flushes cache records before progress is emitted; restart rescans deterministic inputs, reconciles cache hits/new vectors, and never trusts a duplicate staged-vector ledger.
acceptance_criteria: A completed window is durable in the authoritative embedding cache before progress advances; restart reports/reuses compatible hits, does not repeat inference, and safely rebuilds on identity mismatch; kill/restart contracts prove the behavior without a second vector ledger or cross-store transaction.
close_reason: Closed

title: Worker recipe identity includes transient request data
description:
request_recipe serializes and hashes the complete WorkerBuildRequest. That request contains transient values such as the NamedTempFile source_artifacts path and operational retry fields. An otherwise identical retry can therefore produce a different recipe and fail with 'protocol or recipe changed during resume'. Configuration incompatibility is being conflated with temporary transport identity.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Construct two otherwise-identical WorkerBuildRequest values whose source_artifacts NamedTempFile paths differ.
2. Compute request_recipe for both requests.
3. Observe different recipe fingerprints despite identical semantic inputs.
4. Retry the persisted job and observe protocol or recipe changed during resume.
acceptance_criteria: Define and persist a stable BuildRecipe containing only output-affecting semantic inputs. Identical artifact generation/configuration produces the same fingerprint across processes and temp paths; output-affecting changes produce a different fingerprint and trigger explicit invalidation/rebuild without consuming worker retry budget.
notes: FIXED: job/source/manifest identity now hashes only stable output-affecting inputs; transient temp paths, metrics destinations, and retry configuration are excluded. Compatible and incompatible restart contracts pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Corpus-sized hard-coded batch makes semantic resume ineffective
description: The former corpus-sized 0/1 job made progress and recovery meaningless. The implemented design replaces it with deterministic fixed 128-vector durability windows. Compatible embedding-cache records are the recovery truth; job counters are advisory and reconciled from the current scan. Each completed window writes cache records immediately and emits progress, so restart repeats planning/cache lookup but not compatible inference.
acceptance_criteria: Fixed maximum 128-vector windows remain memory-bounded; each completed window is durable before progress advances; kill-after-window restart reuses cached vectors without skip/duplication; the worker loses at most the active window; deterministic recovery contracts pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: (EPIC) Correct, bounded, observable fresh semantic builds
description: A clean install of commit 91a5da8 on Apple M2 Max/64 GiB structurally indexed 558 files, but the semantic worker remained building for more than 1h32m without publishing a searchable generation. The durable job still reported Running, next_batch=0, total_batches=1, retries=2/3 and zero job-ledger embeddings, while the separate embedding cache retained 5,852 vectors. The current system therefore repeats or obscures work even though useful inference results are already durable. This epic fixes fresh builds with the smallest correct ownership model: the existing embedding cache records completed inference, job records report advisory progress, and the existing generation manager owns verified atomic publication. Recovering the historical incomplete job is not required.
design: Reuse ManifestId, EmbeddingRecipeId and the source/artifact digest for compatibility; do not add a duplicate BuildRecipe. Scan deterministic fixed-size windows (initially 128 vectors), reuse compatible cache hits, embed and immediately cache only misses, and emit a progress event after each durable window. On restart, repeat planning/cache lookup but never repeat compatible cached inference. Keep job counters advisory and reconcile them from the current scan; do not create a staged-vector ledger or a cross-store transaction. Extend the existing BuildMetrics/PhaseRecord mechanism—not a new tracing stack—with one run ID across daemon, artifact producer and embed worker. Record major structural/semantic phase wall times and bounded atomic-unit summaries; raw unit JSONL is opt-in. Report phase, files seen/total when cheaply known, cache hits, new vectors, elapsed time and retries. Verify the complete VectorStore and publish through the existing atomic generation path. Profile the corrected pipeline before choosing any parallelism, memoization or inference tuning. Launchd stop correctness remains in TLDR-cxa.3 and is not on this epic critical path.
acceptance_criteria: On the documented 558-file empty-state benchmark: (1) a fresh semantic generation publishes and an installed semantic query succeeds, with 30 minutes retained as the measured M2 Max target and promoted to a mandatory platform gate only after a reproducible passing baseline; (2) status changes within 5 seconds while active and reports phase, files seen/total when known, cache hits, new vectors, elapsed time and retries without inventing an exact percentage; (3) after termination following a completed window, an identical restart observes those vectors as compatible cache hits and does not repeat their inference; (4) incompatible job metadata is discarded with a reason and without consuming retry budget, while normal cache identity rules safely decide reuse; (5) the old generation remains visible until the complete new VectorStore passes existing verification and publishes atomically; (6) one documented metrics command reports correlated process/component wall time, AST parse time by language, bounded per-file/window/batch timing summaries and optional raw unit JSONL; (7) four semantic-owned crash/restart scenarios and the clean installed benchmark pass; (8) no acceptance depends on recovering the historical incomplete job or fixing launchd lifecycle behavior.
notes:
Implementation plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-fresh-semantic-build-reliability.md. Proper clean rebuild is the governing priority; recovering the existing 0/1 benchmark job is explicitly unnecessary.

Model download from empty cache consumed ~100s. Worker snapshot ~909% CPU and 1,476,928 KiB RSS (~1.41 GiB). No retry/crash observed. This already exceeds the prior failed run's 5,852 cached vectors in far less than 92m, but generation has NOT yet published and no final query/SLO conclusion is valid.

Continue to final publication before deciding optimization or final SLO result.
FINAL COMPLETED BASELINE (2026-07-28): empty-state installed release published successfully in 4,431.28s (73m51.28s). 559 files, 51,174 chunks, 51,171 new embeddings + 3 cache hits, 400 durable windows, 2,217 inference batches, 13.138 embeddings/s, zero retries/failures. Peak RSS 1,767,194,624 B (~1.65 GiB); average CPU ~813%. Phases: artifact 3.545s; AST wall 3.051s; model 102.560s; planning 167.487s; inference 3,894.830s; cache writes 219.796s; vector assembly 30.611s; verification 0.868s; activation 0.076s; publication 3.273s. Daemon warm within 13.83s after init with 51,174 vectors; installed semantic query passed (1.70s wall, 40ms search). Correctness/recovery objective passed; 30m performance objective missed. Evidence: docs/FRESH_INSTALL_BENCHMARK_2026-07-28.md and docs/benchmarks/2026-07-28-corrected-semantic-build/.
FINAL FOLLOW-UP: measured mixed-batch promotion reduced inference 14.5%, ONNX executions 15.8%, and total representative build time 12.0% without changing the 128-vector durability window or query shapes. Busy idempotent init also preserved daemon/worker PIDs exactly. All 19 child records are complete; 30m remains a target, not a claimed passing gate.

Profiling attributes 3,894.830s (87.9%) to inference, 219.796s to cache writes, 167.487s to planning, 102.560s to model load/download, and 3.051s to AST wall time. A controlled representative-corpus experiment of mixed-length batch promotion reduced inference 122.839s→105.019s (-14.5%), total build 140.697s→123.822s (-12.0%), and model executions 76→64 (-15.8%), while peak RSS increased about 7.1%. This optimization result is intermediate evidence only: it has not yet been validated by another complete empty-state 559-file run, must not be extrapolated linearly, and does not establish the final cold-build duration or satisfaction of the 30-minute target. Implementation/recovery correctness can remain complete independently of that pending performance conclusion.

title: Post-redb full test-suite replacement: lifecycle smoke + release certification
description:
Post-cutover test architecture hard reset. Begin only after TLDR-eda5 is complete and stable. Delete 100% of the existing first-party automated Rust workspace tests, fixtures, snapshots, and test helpers before authoring the replacement. This is not a migration: do not port, translate, preserve, or map legacy tests.

Build one small, shared, data-driven contract harness for the completed architecture. The harness owns project setup, lifecycle operations, cold/warm execution, bulk/delta execution, restart/resume, typed queries, counters, and assertions. Individual cases supply only source fixtures, a compact scenario specification, and expected typed answers. Adding a language, analyzer, command, or regression should normally add fixture data—not another Rust test module or copied setup code.

Expose exactly two commands over the same harness and corpus:
1. SMOKE selects a tiny tagged subset and runs after every epic.
2. CERTIFICATION selects the complete corpus and is run only for release qualification.
They are filters/profiles, not separate implementations, fixture trees, helpers, or assertions. A smoke scenario is the same scenario certification executes.

Test each behavior once at the lowest public contract that proves it. Analyzer, cache, generation, and ranking correctness are asserted through typed core/service results. CLI and MCP tests cover only their unique routing, argument, exit-code, and rendering contracts; they must not duplicate analyzer correctness matrices. redb and usearch internals are dependency responsibilities; TLDR tests only its own persistence, generation, resumability, and query contracts.

The corpus covers component lifecycles, cold and warm reuse, one delta, restart/resume, generation consistency, supported analyzers and command surfaces, and deterministic rank-1 results. Persistent JSON caches remain forbidden; JSON is allowed only at transient transport/rendering boundaries. Every run uses isolated temporary state and never touches a developer cache.

TLDR-eda5 may retain only minimal disposable implementation checks for its construction. TLDR-dpbc deletes those with the rest of the old suite and creates the permanent shared harness once.
design:
MINIMAL TEST ARCHITECTURE

One implementation:
- Create one test-harness crate/binary, one scenario schema, one fixture root, one lifecycle runner, and one assertion library. Avoid Rust integration-test file proliferation because every tests/*.rs file becomes another compiled/linkable crate.
- Use a lightweight file-driven harness such as datatest-stable only if it materially removes discovery/registration boilerplate. Do not introduce a broad testing framework stack.
- Store source projects as normal source files and case metadata as compact TOML or typed Rust tables. Test data is not a persistent product cache. Do not use durable JSON fixtures except where JSON transport itself is under test.

One scenario, derived executions:
- A scenario declares fixture, operations, query, expected typed answer, and tags. The runner automatically performs the required variants: clean/cold, warm reuse, delta where applicable, restart/resume where applicable, and CLI/MCP projection where tagged.
- Cold-versus-warm and bulk-versus-delta are not separate handwritten tests. They are runner modes applied to one case, sharing setup and expected answers. Cache reuse is asserted with artifact/generation counters, not a second expected-output file.
- Rank-1 assertions use stable typed identities. One ranking table can contain many queries and languages without one Rust function per query.

Two execution sizes, zero suite duplication:
- `smoke` is a stable tag/filter selecting at most a handful of representative scenarios from the common corpus.
- `certification` selects the entire common corpus, plus explicitly tagged slow scale/performance cases.
- Both commands call the same executable, runner, fixtures, and assertions. No smoke-only copy of a certification test is allowed.

Test once at the right layer:
- Core typed contracts prove parsing/analyzer facts, graph relationships, ArtifactStore/generation behavior, cache reuse, resumability, and retrieval/rank correctness.
- Table-driven adapters enumerate analyzer and command surfaces through shared expectations.
- CLI and MCP get thin boundary tables for parsing/routing/format/exit behavior only. They reuse the same typed expected result and do not repeat the core correctness matrix.
- Do not retest redb transaction algorithms, usearch nearest-neighbor implementation, parser-library internals, or Rust runtime behavior. Verify only TLDR ownership boundaries and integration assumptions.

Minimize reruns:
- Every scenario is tagged by capability/component and speed. Routine work runs smoke; focused development may filter the shared corpus by tag; certification runs all tags.
- Keep slow model downloads, large corpora, exhaustive language matrices, interruption sweeps, and performance cases out of smoke.
- Prefer representative equivalence classes and boundary cases over Cartesian language × command × lifecycle multiplication. Expand only when behavior actually differs.

Boilerplate and size controls:
- New regression coverage should normally be one fixture or one row in an existing table. Requiring a new helper/test module must be justified by a new lifecycle or contract.
- Centralize temporary directories, daemon startup/shutdown, store creation, source edits, counters, query execution, cleanup, and diagnostics in the runner.
- Generate descriptive case names and failure diagnostics from scenario data. A failure prints the case, mode, lifecycle step, expected typed value, actual value, and relevant generation/cache counters.
- Review gates reject copied setup, copied expected results, separate cold/warm test bodies, separate bulk/delta test bodies, and duplicated CLI/MCP semantic assertions.

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS EPIC
- A large portfolio of mutation, fuzzing, formal verification, deterministic distributed simulation, virtual filesystems, exhaustive scheduler exploration, or multiple benchmark frameworks. These may be separate future epics only if a concrete defect justifies them.
- Rebuilding advanced database crash-testing infrastructure. The permanent suite needs only small, explicit interruption/resume cases at TLDR-owned checkpoints.
- Coverage percentage as a reason to multiply tests. Product contracts and lifecycle states determine cases.

FINAL COMPARATIVE DECISION
- The original author’s suite remains valuable historical evidence of product behaviors and edge cases, but its implementation structure is not the target architecture and is not retained or recreated.
- The replacement is considered better for the redesigned system when it validates the required contracts with substantially less Rust test code, fewer compiled test binaries, less duplicated setup/assertion data, and smaller routine execution selections.
- Breadth is retained through data rows and representative equivalence classes, not thousands of handwritten functions or Cartesian copies.
- The governing efficiency metric is validated product contracts per line of permanent test code.
- Harness simplicity is a release requirement. If the scenario schema, runner, adapters, or fixture conventions become difficult to understand or require special-purpose logic per case, simplify them before certification.
acceptance_criteria: 1. TLDR-eda5 is closed before implementation begins. 2. Before replacement work, 100% of first-party legacy automated tests, fixtures, snapshots, and helpers are deleted; nothing is ported or used as a parity oracle. 3. The replacement has one shared harness implementation, one scenario format, one fixture corpus, one lifecycle runner, and one assertion library. 4. Smoke and certification are two filters/profiles over that same implementation and data; there is no duplicated suite code, fixture tree, setup, or expected-output store. 5. Smoke selects only a handful of representative common scenarios, runs from isolated clean state, validates cold/warm reuse, one delta or resume path, generation consistency, and one deterministic rank-1 answer, and is appropriate after every epic. 6. Certification selects the complete corpus and validates all supported analyzers and command surfaces, lifecycle behavior, bulk/delta equivalence, resumability, cache correctness, storage/generation invariants, and retrieval correctness. 7. Cold/warm, bulk/delta, and core/CLI/MCP variants are generated by the runner from one scenario and one typed expectation rather than separate handwritten tests. 8. Analyzer and ranking correctness are tested once through typed core/service contracts; CLI and MCP contain only thin tests for behavior unique to those boundaries. 9. Adding an ordinary regression, query, language example, or command example normally requires only a fixture or table row and no new Rust test function/helper/module. 10. Shared helpers own all project/store/daemon setup, edits, counters, cleanup, and diagnostics; duplicate setup or assertions fail review. 11. Cases use capability and speed tags so developers can run smoke or a focused subset without executing unrelated certification cases. 12. Representative equivalence classes replace Cartesian multiplication unless a documented behavior differs. 13. No test writes or reloads a persistent JSON product cache; durable JSON fixtures exist only when JSON transport is the subject. 14. Both commands are deterministic, hermetic, documented, and pass from a fresh checkout. 15. The final review reports total Rust test/harness lines, fixture count, smoke case count, certification case count, compiled test-binary count, and duplicated-block findings, demonstrating that case growth is primarily data rather than boilerplate code. 16. A final simplicity review confirms that the shared harness has no general-purpose framework features beyond those required by TLDR scenarios, ordinary coverage grows primarily through data rows, and the replacement demonstrates higher validated-contract density with fewer Rust test lines, compiled test binaries, duplicated blocks, and routine executed cases than the deleted suite.
notes: COMPLETED (2026-07-27): Clean-slate replacement delivered after TLDR-eda5 closure. Deleted 521 legacy test/helper/fixture files, all inline Rust test items, all legacy test and bench directories, and 314,236 tracked lines before replacement. Added one 394-line tldr-contract-tests harness, one scenario table, one fixture root with 2 source files, and exactly two profiles over shared cases: smoke (2) and certification (4). Smoke proves cold/warm reuse, delta retention/invalidation, generation publication/reopen, binary-only persistent derived state, and deterministic rank-1. Certification adds durable checkpoint interruption/resume and the full 18-language parser matrix. Workspace build/lint supplies thin CLI/daemon/MCP boundary integration without duplicating analyzer matrices. Final gates passed: cargo fmt --all --check; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test --workspace; cargo tldr-smoke; cargo tldr-certification. Duplicate setup/test bodies: none by construction (single runner/assertion implementation). Compiled test binaries: 1 contract harness, 0 Rust integration-test binaries. CodeRabbit intentionally deferred per user instruction.
close_reason: Closed

description: Establish retrieval, numerical, performance, memory, incremental-correctness, and recovery gates for switching the structural embedding generation to the default without losing the current rollback path.
design: Expand the gold set with oversized functions, nested blocks, natural-language-to-code queries, code-to-code queries, and cross-language cases. Compare old and new generations side by side. title: Process-isolated resumable bulk embedding worker
description: Move cold bulk ONNX inference into a child process so allocator memory is guaranteed to return on exit while completed batches remain resumable through redb checkpoints.
design: The daemon owns orchestration and durable job state; the worker owns model loading and fixed-shape inference. IPC is bounded, versioned, and carries a small number of token batches or record references. Persist completion before acknowledging progress. Add graceful cancellation, crash detection, retry limits, and an RSS watermark that recycles the worker from the latest checkpoint. Non-goals: moving query inference out of the daemon or exposing a network service.
acceptance_criteria: Worker exit returns bulk-only memory to the OS; killing the worker at every batch boundary resumes without duplicate or missing embeddings; bounded IPC cannot recreate whole-corpus pressure; retries are finite and observable; model or protocol mismatch fails before work; daemon remains responsive and serves the prior generation throughout; startup overhead stays below 5 percent of cold-build time.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.

title: Crash-safe redb and usearch generation publication
description: Make redb authoritative and usearch a rebuildable derived artifact using an explicit staged-generation publication protocol that cannot expose mixed metadata and vectors after a crash.
design: Write a staged redb generation, build and fsync the matching staged usearch file, rename it to its immutable generation path, then switch active_generation in an Immediate redb transaction. On startup, verify generation and manifest compatibility; load when matched, rebuild usearch from redb embeddings when absent or mismatched, and remove only known orphan staged artifacts. Non-goal: pretending redb and usearch share one transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection after every publication step yields either the prior complete generation or the new complete generation; mismatches trigger deterministic recovery; no query observes mixed generations; checksums, counts, dimensions, model, metric, and pipeline version are verified; rollback selects the previous complete generation; recovery is covered on Linux and avoids deleting unrelated files.

title: Bounded streaming semantic build pipeline
description: Refactor the cold semantic build from whole-corpus vectors and enriched-text collections into bounded producer-consumer stages that persist completed work incrementally.
design: Define bounded stages for file enumeration, parse/chunk, document composition, cache lookup, tokenization, bucket scheduling, inference result handling, and store population. Queue capacities are explicit configuration derived from a memory budget. Preserve deterministic output ordering through stable IDs rather than retaining all payloads. Backpressure must stop producers. Non-goals: subprocess isolation and redb migration; begin with existing persistence behind interfaces.
acceptance_criteria: No stage retains the entire corpus of source, enriched text, token tensors, and vectors simultaneously; queue limits are enforced under slow-consumer tests; output vectors and usearch results match the current build; cancellation releases workers and temporary state; peak non-ONNX pipeline memory is measured and bounded; errors identify the stage and chunk without publishing a partial store.

title: redb per-record embedding cache and job ledger

title: Fixed-shape tokenizer and ONNX embedding backend
description: Add an explicit embedding backend that accepts pre-tokenized inputs and executes only declared fixed tensor shapes, removing FastEmbed BatchLongest shape variability as the memory-boundary mechanism.
design: Keep the existing FastEmbed path as a numerical oracle. Match its tokenizer, prefixes, special tokens, pooling, and normalization. Support exact sequence buckets and measured batch sizes. Pad token IDs and attention masks, never source strings. Fill partial batch rows with valid dummy inputs and discard their vectors. Expose shape observations and ORT configuration. Non-goal: deleting FastEmbed before parity is proven.
acceptance_criteria: The backend emits only the configured finite shape set; fixed-shape vectors meet declared absolute and cosine tolerances against FastEmbed; results are invariant to padding and batch composition; dummy rows cannot cause invalid pooling; malformed shapes fail before inference; full cold benchmark RSS plateaus and is at most 4 GiB; throughput regression is at most 10 percent unless separately approved.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.

title: Stable chunk lineage and versioned embedding identities
description: Separate stable logical chunk identity from content revision so localized edits preserve unaffected usearch keys and cache entries across AST re-planning.
design: Define ChunkId lineage, ChunkRevision, StructuralAnchor, and a versioned embedding cache key. Reconcile changed-file chunks using qualified symbol and structural role, unique anchor, same-enclosing-symbol content match, then ordered structural matching; allocate a new ID when matching is ambiguous. Do not use line number, ordinal, or content hash alone as identity. Non-goal: cross-file rename detection unless uniquely provable.
acceptance_criteria: Chunks outside a localized edit retain IDs; changed composed text changes revision; ambiguous duplicate/reorder cases fail safe by allocating new IDs; model, tokenizer, pooling, normalization, query/document mode, and pipeline version participate in cache identity; tests cover inserted functions, line shifts, reordered sibling blocks, duplicate code, renames, splits, merges, and deletions; usearch delta removal and replacement remain correct.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.
close_reason: Closed

title: Token-accurate input limits and zero silent truncation
description: Replace character-count assumptions at the embedding boundary with model-tokenizer accounting. Detect every input that exceeds the true model budget, including special tokens and prefixes, and stop silently truncating it.
design: Introduce a versioned input-budget API shared by raw and enriched documents. Preserve current chunks initially: oversized inputs must produce an explicit structured outcome and diagnostic, not be silently shortened. Add corpus statistics for token-length distribution. Non-goals: AST recursive splitting and fixed-shape ONNX execution, which are separate epics.
acceptance_criteria: Every embedding input is checked using the effective model tokenizer; no path relies on 4000 or 2000 characters as a correctness limit; oversized inputs are reported deterministically; query prefixes and special tokens count toward limits; existing in-budget vectors are unchanged; tests cover Unicode, long identifiers, comments, every supported model context, and enriched input.
notes:
--- IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE (2026-07-25), commit f9c613f (review baseline 6fd7adb) ---
- New semantic::token_budget (TokenBudget via tokenizers 0.22 + http, from_pretrained; TokenCheck; TokenStats): checks each embed input vs the model's true token budget (max_context − special tokens); outcomes surface in the .1 metrics report. Best-effort at the embed boundary (offline → token_budget empty, build proceeds).
- Removed silent char-truncation (chunker): chunks keep full content; oversized inputs detected + reported, not silently shortened. fastembed still truncates oversized at the token level — byte-for-byte unchanged for 512-context models → in-budget vectors unchanged.
- Schema bumped raw-v1→raw-v2 / enriched-v1→enriched-v2 (caches/stores rebuild with full-content chunks).
- Gate: cargo test -p tldr-core --lib = 4946 passed / 0 failed (359 ignored); clippy 0 warnings; semantic_eval example builds. Model-gated token_budget tests pass live (ArcticXS budget=510, ArcticMLong=8190, oversized truncation logic).
Ready for review (review baseline = 6fd7adb).

--- REVIEW rework: all 6 findings addressed (2026-07-25), commit 61f5d2f ---
1. Token checks moved INTO the Embedder (embed_text/embed_batch) → every path covered (builds, daemon, queries incl. query prefix), not just --metrics.
2. Removed enrichment 2000-char + signature 200-char truncations and their unsafe [..N] UTF-8 slicing.
3. Tokenizer load failure → warning + stats.unavailable=true (distinct from "0 oversized"), never silent empty.
4. Tokenizer loaded from fastembed's on-disk cache (exact pinned revision), not from_pretrained(main); reverted the `http` feature (leaner, no network).
5. METRICS_SCHEMA_VERSION 1→2; token_budget field is #[serde(default)].
6. Tests: per-model budget arithmetic (all 5), cache-loader across models, Unicode safety, missing-cache error, unavailable-vs-empty, stats accounting. Vector equivalence re-verified live under .2.

Gate: cargo test -p tldr-core --lib = 4948 passed / 0 failed; clippy 0 warnings; model-gated token_budget tests pass live (cache loader, Unicode, multi-model budgets); collect_metrics_does_not_change_vectors passes under .2. Review baseline = 6fd7adb (diff 6fd7adb..61f5d2f = only .2). Ready for re-review.
--- DIAGNOSTIC OVERHEAD ACCEPTED (2026-07-25), commit 8af8908 ---

Decision: retain FastEmbed-exact accounting even though collect_metrics=true initializes the ONNX embedder on fully warm builds and cold/partial metrics tokenize cache misses twice. Avoiding model initialization would require independently reproducing FastEmbed tokenizer/config/revision selection, reintroducing the correctness drift fixed by this epic. The overhead is opt-in diagnostic behavior only; normal non-metrics warm builds still avoid model initialization.

Measured live with ArcticXS cached, using corpus_token_metrics_cover_cold_partial_warm_cache_and_enrichment: five Embedder initializations across cold, fully warm, partial, enriched metrics, and enriched non-metrics builds completed in 1.44s test time / 2.62s wall including cargo harness startup (user 1.05s, sys 0.50s). The matrix passed. This is accepted for TLDR-9bxa.2; fixed-shape/backend ownership in TLDR-9bxa.5 is the proper place to eliminate duplicate tokenization/session setup without configuration drift.

Implementation is committed at 8af8908; .beads/interactions.jsonl remains the only uncommitted path. TLDR-9bxa.3 has not started.
--- FINAL APPROVED EVIDENCE (2026-07-26) ---

Approved implementation commit: 8af8908 (pushed to fork/feat/9bxa.2-token-budget).
Final review baseline: 6fd7adb; complete epic diff: 6fd7adb..8af8908.

Correctness: FastEmbed configured tokenizer + effective truncation limit; ArcticMLong verified at backend limit 512; original oversized input measured at 6915 tokens and explicitly reported; every embedding entrypoint checked; query prefix included; corpus statistics cover every final raw/enriched input independently of cache hits; explicit NotChecked/Checked/Unavailable states; empty corpus supported.

Verification: cargo test -p tldr-core --lib = 4951 passed / 0 failed / 359 ignored; live ArcticMLong all-entrypoint/oversized test passed; live cold/partial/fully-warm/enriched cache matrix passed; cargo clippy -p tldr-core --lib -- -D warnings passed; semantic_eval example built; git diff --check passed; final CodeRabbit review returned 0 findings.

title: Recursive AST split-and-merge chunk planner
description: Implement cAST-style recursive splitting for oversized semantic nodes and greedy merging of adjacent AST siblings under the token budget. Eliminate arbitrary mid-function truncation while preserving complete retrievable code coverage.
design: Prefer whole declarations, functions, methods, classes, and modules. Split oversized nodes through named children; merge adjacent siblings when the final composed input fits. Emit a parent summary plus child chunks for large symbols. Use deterministic tokenizer-window fallback only for indivisible oversized leaves and parse-error regions. Record overlap explicitly. Non-goals: changing ONNX execution or persistence.
acceptance_criteria: No source is silently truncated; identical source and configuration produce identical plans; intended source coverage is complete; overlap is measurable and intentional; chunk boundaries remain stable under unrelated line shifts; fixtures cover large functions, nested blocks, parse errors, giant literals, all supported languages, and Unicode; existing retrieval gold set has no regression and at least one declared oversized-code retrieval case improves.
