title: Embedding observability and reproducible memory baseline
description: Add trustworthy instrumentation for the existing embedding pipeline before changing behavior. Capture exact token lengths where available, actual batch dimensions, per-batch latency, padding ratio, cache hits, throughput, process RSS, peak RSS, and phase boundaries. Produce a reproducible cold-build harness for a fixed corpus.
design: Instrument without changing chunking, vectors, cache semantics, model configuration, or search results. Measurements must be machine-readable and quiet-mode compatible. Reuse existing benchmark and daemon status surfaces where possible. Include a run identifier, model, corpus digest, batch size, and schema version. Non-goal: fixing memory in this epic.
acceptance_criteria: A documented command reproduces a complete cold embed; output records every observed batch shape and an RSS timeline; peak RSS agrees with OS measurement within 10 percent; instrumentation adds under 3 percent wall-time overhead; tests verify metric accounting; behavior and vectors remain unchanged.
notes:
--- Step 0 baseline + instrumentation recon (2026-07-25; baseline run in progress) ---

COLD-BUILD INVOCATION (for the reproducible harness):
- `tldr embed <root> --no-cache` is the standalone cold build (clap def: crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/embed.rs:22). `tldr semantic` is search-only (no cold fallback).
- MUST run `tldr daemon stop` first — embed refuses if a daemon covers the path (embed.rs:69-81).
- Cold = wipe ~/.cache/tldr/embeddings/ (dedup cache) + ~/.cache/tldr/stores/<hash>/ (usearch store). Keep ~/.cache/tldr/fastembed/ (ONNX model weights). `--no-cache` bypasses the dedup layer in-process (embed.rs:115; vector_store.rs:1196-1200).
- Embed loop is VectorStore::build (crates/tldr-core/src/semantic/vector_store.rs:1146+): Phase 1 content-addressed cache hits, Phase 2 embeds misses via embed_batch_indexed.

REUSABLE INSTRUMENTATION (no greenfield RSS code needed):
- RSS already implemented + tested in crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/daemon/rss.rs:
  - peak_rss_bytes() — getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss; correctly handles macOS=bytes vs Linux=KB unit split. Best-effort Option. (rss.rs:57)
  - current_rss_bytes() — macOS mach task_info / Linux /proc/self/statm. (rss.rs:19/42)
  - Module doc already cites the 22.7 GiB live observation (TLDR-yll) — same problem domain.
- => .1 peak RSS = call peak_rss_bytes(); RSS timeline = a small sampler thread on current_rss_bytes().
- Status type already carries rss_bytes/peak_rss_bytes (daemon/types.rs:691; consumed in status.rs:329; populated in daemon.rs:1606).
- Existing bench crates/tldr-core/benches/embedding_cache_bench.rs does NOT run the embedder and does NOT measure RSS (rkyv/json serialization only) — NOT reusable for memory baseline.

BASELINE RUN (in progress; corpus = tldr-code repo itself, cold, --no-cache, default model):
- First ~3.5 min: RSS flat at ~3.98 GiB (model + ONNX runtime loaded; pre-embed parse/chunk phase shows no growth). Expected climb toward the documented 25.75 GiB once embed batches flow.
- Embed log is silent (0 lines) so far — confirms .1 must add structured per-batch/shape output; nothing machine-readable to scrape from `tldr embed` today.
- Final peak + timeline pending; will append once the run completes.

--- Step 0 progress update (~31 min into cold run, 2026-07-25) ---

- Peak RSS observed: ~13.96 GiB (14,641,680 KB) at kill time, still monotonically rising. Run duration ~41.6 min, 497 samples. Startup RSS ~9.6 MiB.
- Confirmed: (a) cold build is reproducible via `tldr embed . --no-cache` after `tldr daemon stop`; (b) the monotonic arena-growth symptom reproduces (4 GiB pre-embed -> 14 GiB and climbing); (c) `tldr embed` emits ZERO output during the entire run (0 log lines) — .1 must add structured per-batch/shape/phase output; (d) reusable RSS module crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/daemon/rss.rs (peak_rss_bytes + current_rss_bytes), so no greenfield RSS code.

--- IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE (2026-07-25) ---
Branch: feat/9bxa.1-embedding-observability, commit 16be947.

Built (observe-only; vectors/cache/chunking unchanged when collect_metrics is off, and unaltered even when on):

Assessment: all 5 valid (#5 partially — strict %s are real-run acceptance gates). Fixes:

title: Bound embed-phase peak via shape bucketing (Tier 1: sort+batch consecutive, Tier 2: explicit bucket padding)
description:
Child of TLDR-vbw0. Implements the 'production inference server' shape-bucketing strategy to make embed-phase peak memory O(1) in corpus size, with the ONNX arena plateauing at a small constant instead of climbing to 25GB.

ROOT CAUSE (verified in fastembed 5.8.1 source this session):
- fastembed text_embedding/impl.rs:318 calls tokenizer.encode_batch with PaddingStrategy::BatchLongest (common.rs:99)
- encoding_length = longest token count in each batch of 32 -> ONNX session sees shape (32, L_batch_longest)
- ~14k chunks / 32 = ~450 batches -> up to ~450 distinct shapes -> arena grows monotonically (never releases), reproducing the 195x128MB / 25.75GB peak from TLDR-vbw0

INSERTION POINT:
- crates/tldr-core/src/semantic/vector_store.rs::build, ~L1230-1250, between the cache hit/miss split and the single embedder.embed_batch(texts, ...) call. Today ALL uncached texts go into one embed_batch call in their original (random) order; fastembed internally chunks them into 32s.

TIER 1 (implement first, cheapest, biggest bang):
- Sort the uncached texts by length (char count proxy is fine; no new dep)
- Form batches of 32 from the SORTED list (consecutive, not interleaved)
- Each batch's longest is close to the next -> ~450 distinct L values collapses to ~14
- Arena plateaus at a much smaller constant
- ~30 lines, no new deps, no fastembed patch, easy to revert
- Call embed_batch per sorted slice (or extend embed_batch to accept pre-grouped batches)

TIER 2 (only if Tier 1 insufficient):
- Assign each text to a bucket by token count (buckets at 128/256/384/512 tokens)
- Pad each text to its bucket upper boundary BEFORE passing to fastembed
- With BatchLongest, fastembed pads nothing extra -> every batch in a bucket has shape exactly (32, bucket_len)
- 4 buckets -> 4 shapes total -> arena plateau is tiny and truly O(1) in corpus size
- Costs: padding-token compute waste (~10-20% on short chunks); either char-count proxy or bring tokenizers crate (already a transitive dep via fastembed) for exact bucket assignment

TIER 3 (only if Tier 1+2 insufficient, NOT currently planned):
- Bypass fastembed embed() and call ort directly with pre-tokenized fixed-padded inputs
- Reimplements fastembed inference loop; most control, most invasive

VERIFICATION (mandatory):
- Run embed_bench.rs (or cold tldr embed) with the change
- Watch RSS via ps/vmmap across the full run
- Expectation: RSS plateaus at a small constant instead of climbing to 25GB
- If still climbs, escalate to next tier
- MallocStackLogging diagnosis (TLDR-vbw0 protocol) can run in parallel to confirm arena attribution independent of the fix

ACCEPTANCE:
- Full cold embed on tldr-code (1592 files) with peak_rss (getrusage) bounded and RSS plateauing; target consistent with TLDR-3rh's <=4GB acceptance line
- No regression in embedding quality (vectors bit-identical for untruncated chunks; padding does not change unpadded outputs)
- Embedding wall-time within +10% of current (Tier 1 may even be faster due to less padding waste; Tier 2 padding cost acceptable)

SEQUENCING:
1. Tier 1 implementation in vector_store.rs::build
2. embed_bench.rs RSS capture, log curve here
3. If plateau achieved -> close. If not -> Tier 2.
4. Tier 2 implementation + re-measure if needed
notes:
SCOPE NARROWED (2026-07-25, owner decision): Tier 2 deferred. Pre-padding the text string is NOT safe -- fastembed's tokenizer treats pre-padded spaces as real tokens (attention_mask=1), so the model attends to padding and embeddings differ from the unpadded version, violating the 'vectors bit-identical' acceptance criterion. Verified fastembed 5.8.1 public API exposes only batch_size/cache_dir; PaddingStrategy::BatchLongest is hardcoded in common.rs:99 with no public override. Safe Tier 2 would require either patching fastembed (fork/PR to expose PaddingStrategy::Fixed(N)) or bypassing embed() via tokenizers crate + ort directly -- both significantly more invasive. Tier 1 implemented first; benchmark; escalate only if plateau still too high. Tier 2 plan retained here for reference but NOT active scope.
TIER 1 IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25 (unverified -- build blocked by unrelated pre-existing error):

FILES CHANGED (3):
1. crates/tldr-core/src/semantic/embedder.rs -- added Embedder::embed_batch_indexed(indexed: Vec<(usize, &str)>, show_progress) -> TldrResult<Vec<(usize, Vec<f32>)>>. Sorts by byte length (stable sort_by_key), calls existing embed_batch, returns (orig_index, embedding) pairs. Original embed_batch unchanged so position-sensitive callers/tests keep their semantics.
2. crates/tldr-core/src/semantic/vector_store.rs::build (~L1218-1253) -- replaced the single embed_batch(texts, ...) call with embed_batch_indexed(indexed, ...). Builds (chunk_index, text) pairs via uncached.iter().enumerate() (enriched_texts is positional, chunks[i].content is by-chunk-idx); writeback uses vectors[i] / cache.put(&chunks[i], ...).
3. crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/daemon/index_manager.rs -- embed() helper signature changed Vec<&str> -> Vec<(usize, &str)>, returns Vec<(usize, Vec<f32>)>; delegates to embed_batch_indexed. Single call site at the delta-embed path (~L383) updated to build (position, text) pairs and write back via keyed[i].0.

BLOCKER (not caused by Tier 1, pre-existing in uncommitted in-flight work):
cargo build --workspace --features semantic fails in crates/tldr-core/src/semantic/cache.rs:391 and :578 with E0423 'expected value, found enum rkyv::rancor::Infallible' -- a rkyv 0.8 API misuse in the externally-modified (concurrent process) embedding cache code, NOT in any file Tier 1 touched. This blocks tldr-core lib from compiling, so compiler confirmation of the three Tier 1 edits + cargo test + embed_bench RSS measurement are ALL pending until cache.rs is resolved.

OWNER DECISION (2026-07-25): stop here, owner handles cache.rs + build/test/bench. Tier 1 code is in place but UNVERIFIED -- do not commit/push until cargo build + cargo test -p tldr-core --features semantic + embed_bench RSS plateau are all confirmed. Acceptance gate from bead description still applies (RSS plateaus, no embedding-quality regression, wall-time within +10%).
FULL DESIGN (2026-07-25): The researched AST-aware, token-budgeted, fixed-shape embedding pipeline is documented at docs/STRUCTURAL_EMBEDDING_PIPELINE.md. It supersedes byte-length sorting as the final architecture; Tier 1 remains a benchmarkable interim optimization.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Partially absorbed and linked to TLDR-eda5. Shared persistence/generation/invalidation concerns move into the new ArtifactStore, while the issue’s distinct algorithm, quality, memory, serving, or evaluation work remains valid.

title: Embed-phase RSS grows unbounded: suspected ONNX Runtime CPU arena never releases (195x128MB blocks, 25.75GB peak)
description:
REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-07-25 (TLDR-30f session): cold embed on tldr-code (1592 files) ran 84+min, RSS climbed 14.68GB -> 21.93GB (peak_rss 25.75GB via getrusage), vmmap showed 145->195 IDENTICAL 128MB MALLOC_LARGE blocks = ~93% of resident memory. Matches the 'never plateaus over 8+min' behavior flagged in 48f38be's commit message. NOT the fixed AST-retention issue (549MB, TLDR-9ae/myd) and NOT embedding vectors (wrong allocation signature).

SUSPECTED MECHANISM: ONNX Runtime CPU memory arena (stack: fastembed 5.8.1 -> ort 2.0.0-rc.11 -> onnxruntime C lib). Arenas never return memory to the OS by default (hold peak-ever), and dynamic input shapes (varying token lengths per batch) trigger repeated arena extension in large fixed chunks -- consistent with the uniform 128MB block signature.

DIAGNOSIS (do first): restart daemon with MallocStackLogging=1, force cold rebuild, run malloc_history -allBySize on the 128MB allocations; confirm onnxruntime/BFCArena frames. Protocol already detailed in TLDR-30f notes.

FIX LEVERS (documented ONNX Runtime features, least->most invasive):
1. RunOptions memory.enable_memory_arena_shrinkage (shrink arena after each run)
2. SessionOptions enable_cpu_mem_arena(false) -- standard fix for this exact symptom; plain malloc/free, memory returns to OS, small throughput cost
3. arena_extend_strategy = kSameAsRequested (no power-of-two chunk growth)
4. enable_mem_pattern(false) (designed for dynamic shapes)
5. Shape bucketing: pad batches to a few fixed token lengths

RISK: fastembed 5.8.1 owns ort session construction and may not expose these options -- if so: PR/patch fastembed, or construct the session via ort directly (fastembed is mostly tokenizer + session glue).

ACCEPTANCE: full cold embed on tldr-code with peak_rss (getrusage) bounded and RSS plateauing; target consistent with TLDR-3rh's <=4GB acceptance line.
notes:
FIX LEVER 6 (owner proposal, 2026-07-25): job-scoped session lifecycle -- split the embed run into small jobs; create session -> embed N batches -> persist -> DROP session -> next job. Arena growth is bound to session lifetime and shapes-seen-within-lifetime, so peak becomes max(per-job peak) instead of the accumulated staircase to 25GB. KEY ADVANTAGE over levers 1-5: requires zero fastembed/ort config API access, only lifecycle management. LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION to verify: dropping the TextEmbedding/session actually returns arena memory to the OS (macOS MALLOC_LARGE blocks are mmap-backed and munmap'd on free, so it SHOULD -- but a global/env-level arena inside onnxruntime would break this; verify, don't assume). VERIFICATION: modify embed_bench.rs to drop/recreate every N batches, watch RSS -- ~1hr, definitive. FALLBACK with guaranteed reclamation: subprocess-per-job worker (process exit returns everything unconditionally; costs IPC + per-job model reload). TUNING: job size balances model-reload cost (~0.5-2s/job) vs per-job arena peak; target reload overhead <5% of runtime (e.g. 500-1000 chunks/job). Levers 1-5 remain complementary (shrink even the per-job peak). SEQUENCE: (a) MallocStackLogging diagnosis, (b) drop/recreate embed_bench test, (c) in-process job-scoped sessions if (b) reclaims, else subprocess worker.
STRATEGY REFINEMENT (2026-07-25, after owner design discussion): owner's requirement formalized as the invariant 'peak memory = O(1) in corpus size'. The streaming pipeline with fixed batch=32 already satisfies this by construction EXCEPT the ONNX arena, which accumulates state proportional to shape-diversity x session-lifetime. Revised solution hierarchy:
1. PRIMARY (root cause): fixed-shape bucketing -- pad every batch to a small fixed set of token lengths (e.g. 128/256/512). Session then sees a FINITE shape set; arena plateaus permanently regardless of corpus size; single long-lived session becomes O(1) naturally. No fastembed/ort config access needed. Cost: padding-token compute waste; usually offset by uniform-shape throughput gains. (Supersedes 'lever 5' as the lead fix, promoted from last place.)
2. SECONDARY: arena config (levers 1-4) if fastembed exposes it.
3. BACKSTOP (refines lever 6): watermark-triggered worker/session recycling -- recycle ONLY when observed RSS crosses a threshold, NOT unconditionally per job. Zero steady-state cost; hard ceiling against current AND future allocator pathologies. Industry precedent: Apache MaxRequestsPerChild / gunicorn max_requests.
Combined target design: bucketed shapes -> one long-lived session -> watermark recycle as circuit breaker. Diagnosis step (MallocStackLogging confirm) still first.
OWNER DECISION (2026-07-25): adopted shape-bucketing strategy ('production inference server' pattern). Filed child bead for implementation with two tiers: Tier 1 = sort uncached texts by length + batch consecutive in vector_store.rs::build (~30 lines, collapses ~450 distinct ONNX shapes to ~14, no new deps); Tier 2 = explicit bucket padding (128/256/384/512 token boundaries, 4 shapes total, true O(1) arena plateau). Tier 3 (bypass fastembed, call ort directly) held in reserve. fastembed 5.8.1 mechanism confirmed in source: BatchLongest padding -> shape (32, longest_in_batch) per batch. Verification: embed_bench.rs RSS must plateau; target <=4GB peak consistent with TLDR-3rh. MallocStackLogging diagnosis runs in parallel to confirm arena attribution. Watermark-triggered session recycling (lever 6) retained as defense-in-depth backstop only.
FULL DESIGN (2026-07-25): Root-cause response and long-term architecture are documented at docs/STRUCTURAL_EMBEDDING_PIPELINE.md: cAST-style structural chunks, exact token/attention-budgeted shapes, separate query/delta/bulk sessions, process-isolated bulk ONNX inference, redb checkpoints, and usearch generation publication.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Partially absorbed and linked to TLDR-eda5. Shared persistence/generation/invalidation concerns move into the new ArtifactStore, while the issue’s distinct algorithm, quality, memory, serving, or evaluation work remains valid.

title: Re-measure daemon memory instruments (warm/callgraph + cold-embed) on current main
description:

LIVE REPRO (2026-07-25, daemon PID 69720, uptime ~1h, tldr-code 1592 files, semantic_index.state=building, salsa misses=3/genuinely cold start): RSS climbed continuously with NO plateau across three samples over ~5min -- 14.68GB -> 14.87GB (+185MB/60s) -> 20.82GB. vmmap -summary confirms this is NOT fragmentation (0% frag) and NOT AST/callgraph retention (that path is fixed at 549MB per TLDR-9ae/TLDR-myd, 3 orders of magnitude smaller). Signature: MALLOC_LARGE region count climbed 311->324->149-of-exactly-128.0MB (uniform block size), i.e. a small number of identically-sized giant allocations growing monotonically, matching a pool/arena allocator that grows by fixed-size blocks and does not release them between batches. Consistent with the ONNX Runtime arena-non-release hypothesis flagged in 48f38be's commit message (14,370-chunk corpus, same behavior, never plateaued over 8+min). LIMITATION: no MallocStackLogging was enabled at daemon launch, so this is allocation-pattern evidence (uniform 128MB block count), not a symbolicated call-stack proof of the exact allocation site -- that requires a fresh daemon restart with MallocStackLogging=1 + malloc_history/leaks sampling (TLDR-335's original Phase-A protocol), not yet run against this hypothesis specifically. title: Enforce additive Git + .tldrignore semantics across full and delta traversal
description: TLDR currently combines ignore::WalkBuilder custom .tldrignore precedence with a separate root-only deny matcher that strips !. This creates split semantics: nested policy files are not covered by the deny matcher, full traversal and the shallow single-file corpus gate disagree on positive negation, and the watcher delete matcher cannot represent the same hierarchical sources as the build. The approved contract is additive: Git/standard ignore sources are an immutable deny floor; .tldrignore may exclude additional paths and may negate only its own earlier exclusions, never reopen a Git-ignored path. Upgrade ignore from 0.4.25 to 0.4.31 and use WalkBuilder::build_matchers/IncrementalIgnore to share hierarchical matching across full walks, single-file delta checks, callgraph filtering and vanished watcher paths.
design: Retain WalkBuilder for efficient recursive traversal. Build two independent incremental matchers from canonical configs: Git/standard sources and .tldrignore-only. A path is ignored when either matcher returns ignore; source-local negation remains Git-compatible but cannot cross the Git hard floor. Apply the matcher as a final full-walk correctness filter, replace the ancestor-pruned single-file walk, reload watcher snapshots for nested policy-file changes, and preserve separate hidden/generated/language/size gates. No hand-parsing, pattern concatenation, expanded ignored-path list or new ignore library.
acceptance_criteria: ignore resolves to 0.4.31; full ProjectWalker, ProjectWalker::classify_path, semantic is_corpus_file, callgraph filter and watcher deleted-path decisions agree for root/nested .gitignore and .tldrignore, negation and ignored parents; .tldrignore cannot reinclude a Git-ignored path but can reopen its own earlier exclusion; global Git excludes and .git/info/exclude remain honored; nested policy changes reload live; focused tests, ignore_matcher_unification contract, formatting and workspace construction pass.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: FIRECRAWL RESEARCH 2026-07-28: TLDR already uses the correct specialized library family: BurntSushi/ripgrep's ignore crate. Project currently resolves ignore v0.4.25. Current v0.4.31 WalkBuilder supports .gitignore, parent files, global Git ignore, .git/info/exclude, and custom ignore filenames; add_custom_ignore_filename gives custom files higher precedence. New in 0.4.30+ (absent from 0.4.29 docs, present in 0.4.30) is WalkBuilder::build_matchers(), which builds IncrementalIgnore matchers from the same configuration without recursive traversal. This is a strong simple fix candidate for this shallow-vs-bulk drift: upgrade to >=0.4.30, build the canonical matcher once, use it for existing-file/delta membership, then layer TLDR's DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_DIRS/generated-sentinel/content/language gates. Validate positive negation, ignored-parent non-reinclude, nested .gitignore/.tldrignore, global exclude and .git/info/exclude parity before closing. Sources: https://docs.rs/ignore/latest/ignore/struct.WalkBuilder.html and https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore. This is research, not an approved implementation yet.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
## Design record (2026-07-18 Amp thread) — shipped

### Product decisions (locked with user)
- Primary UX like beads: tldr init / tldr init --remove (+ optional -p/--project).
- NO user-facing tldr init --warm — warm is system-owned.
- tldr setup <agent> DEFERRED (see TLDR-2o4.4).
- LaunchAgent is process babysitter only; warm is daemon policy (warm-if-cold).
- All logic in tldr-code (no tldr-ctl revival). Templates are data; logic is Rust.

### Architecture
tldr init/remove (CLI)
  -> lifecycle/ (Rust): project seed, service.json, launchd render/install
  -> templates/launchd/daemon.plist.template (placeholders only)
  -> daemon start (absolute --project --foreground via launchd)
  -> ensure-warm: WarmJob on start + init queues warm if needed

### Files
- crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/init.rs
- crates/tldr-cli/src/lifecycle/{mod,project,service_state,launchd}.rs
- crates/tldr-cli/templates/launchd/daemon.plist.template
- Daemon hook: warm-if-cold after daemon_ready in daemon.rs

### State and logs
- .tldr/config.json (seed once), .tldrignore, .tldr/service.json
- service.json: label, plist_path, tldr_bin, platform, logs{stdout,stderr,daemon}, template_version
- LaunchAgent logs: ~/Library/Logs/tldr/<slug>.{out,err}.log
- Project log: .tldr/daemon.log
- --remove keeps config/cache/logs; deletes service.json + plist + stops daemon

### Label scheme
com.parcadei.tldr-daemon.<basename-slug>-<8hex-path-hash>

### Acceptance verified (smoke)
init -> running daemon + absolute --project in plist; structure works; idempotent init; remove cleans service; second remove ok; 6 lifecycle unit tests pass.

title: embed is an ungated parallel writer of the daemon-owned store — gate per ADR-10
description: tldr embed <path> calls load_or_build_store(path, store_dir_for(path), ...) — the SAME store_dir the daemon's IndexManager builds/saves. embed has ZERO daemon-awareness (no is_daemon_running / DaemonRoute / --oneshot gate), so running it while a daemon covers the path = two concurrent writers of one usearch store -> rebuild livelock + cache.json flush race (the exact hang a user hit 2026-06-28: a standalone 'tldr embed .' alongside a daemon warm looping on 'source changed; rebuilding', daemon RSS ballooned to 20GB over 2h). embed predates the ADR-10 (TLDR-14i) no-silent-fallback conversion that the other ~12 commands got. FIX (decided): hard-refuse when a live covering daemon exists (daemon_router::daemon_project_for), message points to 'tldr warm <path>' (daemon-owned build) or 'tldr daemon stop' for a standalone build. No --oneshot override: a local build writes the shared store_dir so it can't be made safe while the daemon is live. Related: TLDR-14i (ADR-10), TLDR-7vb (daemon-vs-local divergence).
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.

title: Grammar-frontier canary — 'tldr doctor --grammar-frontier <lang>' with ERROR-node assertion
description:
## Why
Epic finding B: extraction success cannot distinguish 'grammar parses t-strings' from 'error-recovery salvaged the file'. The eval's probe (PEP695 def f[T]/class Box[T]/type alias + match + t"..." t-string + a function AFTER the t-string) extracted everything on tree-sitter-python 0.23.6 — but whether ERROR nodes were emitted is UNKNOWN. That distinction is exactly what predicts future silent loss.

## What
Bundle a per-language newest-syntax snippet set (Python: the eval's probe file, reproduced below; others per grammar). 'tldr doctor --grammar-frontier python' parses each snippet and reports: definitions extracted (expected list), ERROR-node count (MUST be 0 for 'full support' verdict), grammar version. Output: per-feature PASS/RECOVERED/FAIL table.

Python probe (from the eval):
  type SymbolList = list[str]
  def first[T](items: list[T]) -> T: ...
  class Box[T]:
      def get(self) -> T: ...
  def kind(x):  # match statement body
      match x:
          case []: return 'empty'
          case _: return 'other'
  def template(name: str): return t"hello {name}"
  def after_tstring() -> int: return 42

## Acceptance Criteria
- doctor subcommand ships with snippet sets for at least python/typescript/rust; PASS requires expected-definitions AND zero ERROR nodes; RECOVERED verdict when definitions present but ERROR>0; CI runs it per grammar bump.
notes:
ENRICHMENT (2026-06-07): the canary's value is now PROVEN by a live case — the pinned 0.23.6 grammar lacks template_string (verified via node-types.json), so the eval's t-string extraction success was RECOVERED-not-PASS. A zero-ERROR-node assertion would have caught this today. Use t-strings-on-0.23.6 as the canary's own regression fixture: it must report RECOVERED until the pin moves to a #368-bearing release, then flip to PASS.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27: tldr doctor --grammar-frontier ships typed Python/TypeScript/Rust probes with PASS/RECOVERED/FAIL semantics, definition assertions, grammar versions, parse recovery counts, JSON/text output, and non-zero exit on FAIL. Current pinned Python PEP 750 t-string correctly reports RECOVERED; focused tests and full workspace gates pass.
close_reason: Grammar-frontier canary implemented and verified for Python, TypeScript, and Rust.

title: [EPIC] Parser/grammar assurance — tree-sitter stack findings (dogfood eval, 2026-06-07)
description:
## Why
Second eval round (after TLDR-6rt's Django-awareness round): assessed the PARSING LAYER itself — what tldr is built on and whether it can be trusted on modern Python. Method: tldr explored its own Rust codebase to locate the stack; then a ground-truth differential + a syntax-frontier probe against the Stock-Monitor-Django corpus (Python 3.14).

## FINDINGS — what works (baseline to protect)
1. Stack identity: tree-sitter =0.25.0 core, EXACT-pinned grammars per language with documented ABI-compat rationale in Cargo.toml (tree-sitter-python =0.23.6 for Python). The pinning discipline is a strength — keep it.
2. BYTE-PERFECT extraction on real Django code: 95/95 files with ZERO function/class count mismatches vs CPython's own ast module (harness: ast.walk FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef/ClassDef vs structure definitions).
3. Frontier resilience: PEP 695 generics (def f[T], class Box[T]), match statements, AND Python 3.14 t-strings (PEP 750) all extracted — including definitions AFTER the t-string. No silent downstream loss even past the grammar's nominal vintage.

## FINDINGS — gaps/risks (the children)
A. Silent-degradation invisibility: tree-sitter error-tolerance means a future grammar gap looks like 'fewer functions found' with zero signal (already filed as TLDR-6rt.5; the canary+differential children here are its systematic siblings).
B. AMBIGUITY in finding 3: unknown whether t-strings PARSE cleanly in 0.23.6 or were recovered via ERROR nodes — extraction success alone cannot distinguish. A canary must assert zero ERROR nodes, not just presence of definitions.
C. PEP 695 type aliases ('type SymbolList = list[str]') are NOT reported by extract/structure at all — not a function, not a class, just absent. Type aliases are API surface; tools consuming structure for API extraction miss them.
D. No upgrade policy for exact-pinned grammars: pins are correct but frozen — no process tracks upstream grammar releases (e.g., official t-string support, future 3.15 syntax) against the ABI matrix.

## Corpus & reproducibility
Same pinned corpus as TLDR-6rt (github.com/udhaya10/Stock-Monitor-Django); probe file = PEP695 generics + match + t-string snippet set (reproduced in child descriptions).
notes:
FIRECRAWL ENRICHMENT (2026-06-07) — AMBIGUITY B RESOLVED with primary-source evidence: tree-sitter-python v0.23.6's own node-types.json (raw.githubusercontent at the pinned tag) contains NO 'template_string' node → the eval's t-string probe success WAS error recovery, not parsing. This is a live instance of the silent-degradation failure mode on our CURRENT pin — extraction survived (definitions intact) but the t-string body parsed as garbage/ERROR. Upstream PR #368 'feat: Add PEP 750 template string support' exists; latest upstream release = v0.25.0 (releases page) → concrete pin-bump target. Conversely CONFIRMED native in 0.23.6: type_alias_statement, type_parameter (PEP 695), match_statement — the generics/match probe results were TRUE parses. Sources cached: .firecrawl/search-tsp-tstring.json, tsp-releases.md, /tmp/tsp-0236-nodes.json technique (re-derivable: curl raw node-types.json at any tag).

COMPLETED 2026-07-27: all 4 children are closed. Parser recovery is visible in output/warnings/daemon stats; doctor frontiers distinguish native support from recovery; the pinned CPython differential covers all 217 corpus files with zero mismatches; PEP 695 aliases are represented; and exact-pin upgrade/rollback gates are documented and automated. Full workspace formatting, warnings-denied Clippy, all-target tests, smoke, and certification pass.

title: Cross-file call edges for function-local imports — fix calls graph + recursive impact depth on Python

title: Dotted-string reference resolution — settings/urls/config string literals count as references
description:
## Why
THE Django-specific blind spot (epic GAP CLASS 1): Django wires code via dotted-path STRINGS — settings.MIDDLEWARE, INSTALLED_APPS, LOGGING '()' factories, urls, DRF settings, Celery/Procrastinate task-name strings. AST reference counting sees zero refs → false possibly_dead (reproducer: build_console_formatter in the corpus). This false-positive class erodes trust in 'dead' on every Django/Flask/Celery codebase.

## What
In reference counting (and 'references' output): treat string literals matching a dotted-path shape (\b[a-z_][\w.]+\.[A-Za-z_]\w*\b with >=1 dot, resolving to a known module.symbol in the index) as references of kind 'string-ref' (new kind; confidence lower than call/import). Scope-limit to cheap wins first: only scan py files whose path matches settings|urls|conf|config or all string literals project-wide if perf allows (measure). Resolution: split on last dot → module path lookup in existing module index → symbol lookup.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Corpus reproducer: build_console_formatter no longer in possibly_dead; references build_console_formatter shows a string-ref hit at config/settings.py with line number.
- New kind documented; --kinds string-ref filter works; zero regressions on existing reference goldens.
- Perf: <10% indexing-time increase on the corpus (measure cold+warm).
notes:
PRIOR-ART ENRICHMENT (2026-06-07, firecrawl): NO incumbent does dotted-string resolution — vulture's answer to settings-string wiring is manual whitelists (sources on 6rt.3). Implementing string-ref resolution makes tldr the first mainstream tool that gets Django LOGGING/'()'/MIDDLEWARE strings right automatically — a marketable differentiator, not just an FP fix.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27: ReferenceKind::StringRef serializes/filters as string-ref; Python static dotted strings are accepted only when the complete module.symbol path resolves to an indexed definition. The same one-pass AST traversal feeds resolved strings into dead-code refcounts. Corpus evidence at 1e56243d5258e0b310a45ca3cfae60c455328b76: build_console_formatter returns one string-ref at config/settings.py:245 and is absent from dead/possibly_dead. Performance vs pre-change 816b47f: cold 9.24s -> 9.24s; repeat mean 6.74s -> 6.73s (0% regression). Focused dead test, certification 12/12, formatting, diff check, and warnings-denied Clippy pass.
close_reason: Implemented resolution-backed dotted-string references and dead-code rescue with corpus and performance proof.

title: [EPIC] Fast lane: code-verified bugs + proven cheap wins (pre-rewrite)
description:
Groups the CODE-VERIFIED bugs and MEASURED/cheap quality wins that proceed AHEAD of the gated rewrite (strategy ratified 2026-06-06, recorded on TLDR-n74). Membership rule: an item belongs here iff (a) the defect is code-verified or the lever is measured/proven-cheap, AND (b) it has no dependency on the rfz-gated CSR/17d rewrite.

## Bug members (all code-verified)
- Wrong-answer daemon arms interim disable (child issue): slice daemon arm hardcodes Backward + ignores --variable (audit 9/64, 7vb inst.4); impact daemon arm returns weaker answers. Until n74, correctness > speed: route these to the correct local path.
- TLDR-lkx: DataClumps detector nonexistent (always 0 findings), FeatureEnvy empty without --deep. Decision: implement or remove from advertised surface.
- TLDR-bpf cluster: .tldrignore not honored end-to-end — TLDR-1qv (semantic corpus over-indexes excluded dirs = WASTED EMBED TIME + search noise), TLDR-1j2 (watcher gaps), TLDR-9w8 (two divergent matcher impls).

title: T3: CAS persistence (warm restarts) + mark-and-sweep GC + byte-budget LRU; retire OnceCell buckets; closes jsi class
description:
Parent: TLDR-17d. Implements T3 persistence + lifecycle for the CAS (spec: TLDR-n74 2026-06-06 comment; Codex F6/F8).

1. On-disk content-addressed store for S2 -> WARM RESTARTS (restart re-parse only verifies hashes; unchanged files' facts load from CAS). Reuse the VectorStore content-keyed persistence pattern (Codex F8), do not fork a second regime.
2. GC = MARK-AND-SWEEP from the current file set: live = body hashes referenced by current parses; sweep on idle/threshold. Per-segment LRU alone is INSUFFICIENT — stale body hashes stay valid keys forever and accumulate across edits (Codex F6).
3. RAM tier: per-segment byte budgets + LRU; eviction always safe (recompute on miss) because keys are content-addressed.
4. RETIRE the daemon per-language OnceCell buckets (state.rs invalidate_caches blunt clear) — the CAS + generationed snapshot replace them; no layered second regime.
5. CLOSES the TLDR-jsi bug class: cache clear = atomic CAS drop; content-addressed keys cannot serve stale-wrong data; daemon quiescence no longer a coherence requirement for clear.
DEPENDS ON: S2 child (the store being persisted).
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): The legacy implementation path is absorbed by TLDR-eda5 and the one-shot shared redb ArtifactStore plan. The underlying user-visible requirement is preserved in that plan; this issue is superseded as an implementation vehicle, not erased as historical evidence.

title: S6: search segments — BM25 per-file delta postings + S2-keyed embeddings (caching contract for utj.3)
description:
Parent: TLDR-17d. Implements segment S6 (spec: TLDR-n74 2026-06-06 comment).

BM25 postings become a resident, per-file-delta-updatable segment: file edit -> remove old file's postings, add new ones — never whole-index rebuild on the query path (today public search rebuilds BM25 + full graph EVERY query; that dies). Embeddings ride S2 (content-keyed, t8f incremental — align, don't fork).
COORDINATES WITH TLDR-utj.3 (BM25 resident in daemon + RRF fusion): utj.3 owns search QUALITY (fusion); this issue owns the CACHING/INVALIDATION contract (delta postings, content keys). Decision input: TLDR-rfz prototype 2 decides rebuild-vs-incremental-postings ON NUMBERS — if full rebuild measures cheap enough, this issue collapses to 'rebuild from warm S2 on dirty' and only the segment KEYING ships.
acceptance_criteria: BM25 is constructed from a pinned ArtifactStore generation rather than walking source on a query; edits, deletes, renames, language/path scope, and ignore-policy changes update or replace postings correctly; no mixed-generation BM25/vector/structural answer can publish; CLI and MCP share the same index contract; instrumentation and a repeated-query test prove zero corpus rebuild/tokenization on the query path; cold/not-ready behavior is explicit.
notes: COMPLETED 2026-07-29: SearchIndexManager publishes generation-pinned per-language BM25 from exact ArtifactStore source. Query paths never walk/tokenize the corpus. Delta refresh rebuilds only affected languages and reuses unaffected index Arcs; edit/delete/rename/ignore-policy and cold/mismatch tests pass. CLI/MCP share the contract. Dhan repeated lexical queries are 0.00-0.01s. Evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-07-29-dhan-authoritative-runtime/REPORT.md; implementation ef76581.
close_reason: Resident BM25 caching, invalidation, shared clients, and Dhan repeated-query proof complete.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: CONTRACT ADDITION (A8, user-ratified): embedding lane is ASYNC (L2-async; ONNX ~100ms+/fn, 11.5GB arena class — see TLDR-3rh); results JOIN-VERIFIED against pinned generation (dead keys dropped, positions rebased); response carries embedding-staleness field. Stale = mis-rank possible, dead symbols impossible.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: KEY-CORRECTNESS NOTE (2026-06-06, surfaced in user discussion): the embedding KEY is NOT body-hash alone. Enrichment text includes signature + CALLEES — a callee rename in ANOTHER file changes foo()'s embedding text while foo's body hash is unchanged. Embedding key = (body hash, ENRICHMENT-SLICE hash [signature + resolved callee list from the pinned generation], model ver). Consequence: a compose-input change elsewhere can legitimately queue re-embeds via the async lane — bounded by O(functions whose resolved callee set changed), never whole-corpus. Without this, stale enrichment silently survives cross-file renames.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: A12 (2026-06-06, user-ratified): EMBEDDING KEY IS BODY-LOCAL — key = (body hash, signature hash, model ver). Resolved-callee context is NEVER baked into embedding text; structural context (callers/callees) joins AT QUERY TIME from the pinned generation (O(deg) from L3) and fuses via RRF with dense + BM25 signals (rides utj.3). SUPERSEDES the earlier enrichment-slice-hash note: that note correctly identified the staleness hazard but solved it in the wrong direction (honest key over volatile inputs -> frequent invalidation); A12 removes the volatile input from the artifact instead. CONSEQUENCES: (1) a callee rename re-embeds ZERO functions — only a function's own body edit re-embeds it; (2) query-time context is FRESHER than baked-in (current at query moment vs stale-between-re-embeds); (3) deployed baseline already runs enrich OFF (memory 00) so this costs nothing today; (4) GATE: any future baked-in enrichment proposal must BEAT query-time fusion in the eval harness before earning a place in the embedding key. Design principle extracted: never bake volatile cross-file data into the most expensive immutable artifact — serve volatility from the always-fresh cheap structure.

title: S4/S5: identity-ordered FuncIds + slice-hash reuse tickets for derived artifacts via pinned-generation lookup
description:
Parent: TLDR-17d. Implements S4 identity discipline + S5 reuse tickets (spec: TLDR-n74 2026-06-06 comment; Codex F3/F4).

1. FuncId assignment DETERMINISTIC FROM IDENTITY ORDERING (file, qualified name, ordinal) — never positions. Rides on/coordinates with TLDR-n74's CSR build.
2. SLICE-HASH REUSE TICKETS for derived artifacts: pagerank/betweenness/hubs-rank/SCC/cycles/layers <- blake3(identity table + CSR bytes, positions EXCLUDED, + array lengths); coupling/cohesion <- module-edge hash; inheritance closure <- type-edge hash; clones index <- S2 fingerprint multiset (incremental: re-compare changed functions only); health/debt aggregates <- monoid fold over S2 metric rows.
3. JOIN CONTRACT (the F4 epoch-mismatch killer): artifacts are ALWAYS looked up THROUGH a pinned generation — the pinned snapshot's slice hashes select the artifact. Generation = consistency token; slice hash = reuse ticket. Epoch mixing (old pagerank vector against new node table) is unexpressible by construction, not guarded by checks.
4. Replaces 'first query per generation pays' with 'first query per input-slice-change pays': a body-only edit (no call-edge change) produces a new generation with IDENTICAL topology hash -> pagerank/betweenness survive the rebuild warm.
ARBITRATED: no secondary equality check on hash match (blake3-256; user-ratified drop of Codex F3 rec).
DEPENDS ON: TLDR-n74 (CSR must exist), S2 child (fingerprints, metric rows).

title: S3: closed compose-input fact set — fold receiver/local-type extraction into FileIR; compose goes source-blind
description:
Parent: TLDR-17d. Implements segment S3 (spec: TLDR-n74 2026-06-06 comment).

Define the CLOSED SET of per-file facts compose consumes, each independently blake3-hashed: (a) signature set, (b) call-site list, (c) import list, (d) RECEIVER-INDEX / LOCAL-TYPE FACTS. Item (d) is the load-bearing piece (Codex F5 BLOCKER: today apply_type_resolution scans full file source; Python/TypeScript receiver indexes are built from source text; ImportMap depends on body parse). This issue executes ADR-9's 'fold receiver indexes into FileIR' move: extraction happens ONCE per file-version during the parse walk; compose afterward consumes ONLY these hashed facts — never raw source. The compose key (multiset of per-file S3 hashes) determines S4 rebuild.
NOTE: this is the byte-identical-output incremental step toward lever C (the oracle swap itself stays USER-DEFERRED per TLDR-t0s).
ACCEPTANCE: compose provably source-blind (type-level: compose signature takes facts, not source); frozen-corpus byte-hash gates green; single parse walk computes all hashes (no source re-reads per invalidation cycle, Codex F7).

title: S2: per-function fact CAS — (body-hash, env-hash) keyed bundles/metrics/fingerprints/embeddings, position-relative
description:
Parent: TLDR-17d. Implements segment S2 of the cache model (spec: TLDR-n74 2026-06-06 comment).

PER-FUNCTION content-addressed store. Key = (function body hash, FILE SEMANTIC-ENV HASH, lang, analyzer ver) where env = imports + enclosing-class chain (Codex F1: identical text across files is NOT semantically identical — receiver resolution depends on file context). Values, all identity-free:
1. Analysis bundle: source slice + tree + CFG + DFG + SSA — POSITION-RELATIVE to function start (Codex F2: absolute 1-indexed lines are pervasive today in cross_file_types.rs; consumers must be audited; absolute start line + qualified identity live ONLY in the generation node table, rebased at join/render).
2. Metric row: cyclomatic/cognitive/halstead/loc/smell-facts (serves complexity/cognitive/halstead/loc/smells/debt/health/hotspots as one fact set).
3. Normalized token fingerprint (serves clones/dice/similar).
4. Embedding (semantic; already content-keyed per t8f — align keying, don't fork).
INVARIANTS: editing fn A keeps all sibling functions' entries warm (49/50 property); an edit ABOVE a function never invalidates it (body hash is position-independent); import/class-context edits invalidate the whole file's entries HONESTLY. Consumers: reaching-defs, taint, slice, chop, available, dead-stores, cognitive, complexity, smells, clones, semantic — one warm memo serves the whole agent sequence.

title: [EPIC] Content-addressed cache segment model: warm-once cross-command reuse + minimal invalidation
description:
Tracks implementation of the CONTENT-ADDRESSED CACHE SEGMENT MODEL (spec: TLDR-n74 comment 2026-06-06; Codex review + arbitration: TLDR-5qm same date; user-ratified). Goals: (a) WARM ONCE — cache segments shared across CLI flows, not per-command caches; (b) MINIMAL INVALIDATION — a single-file edit kills only the segments whose input slice actually changed.

## The contract (binding for every child)
Every cached artifact declares its exact input slice; key = blake3 of that slice + (schema, analyzer, grammar) versions; invalidation = key mismatch, NEVER explicit flush. No identity (names/paths/absolute positions) inside cached values — identity lives in the generation node table, joined at query time.

## Segments -> children
- S2 per-function fact CAS (child issue): bundles/metrics/fingerprints/embeddings keyed (body hash, file-env hash)
- S3 closed compose-input set (child issue): receiver/local-type facts fold into FileIR
- S4/S5 reuse tickets (child issue): identity-ordered FuncIds + slice-hash keyed derived artifacts via pinned-generation lookup
- S6 incremental search segments (child issue): BM25 delta postings (coordinates with TLDR-utj.3)
- T3 persistence + GC (child issue): on-disk CAS, mark-and-sweep, byte-budget LRU
- S1 (parse) needs no new work beyond keying discipline; S7 (external truth: churn/diagnostics/doctor/coverage/fix) is local-by-design, NO daemon residency — captured here only as a constraint.

## Invalidation cascade (the acceptance story, end-to-end)
Single-file edit: hash file -> re-parse (one walk computes ALL hashes, no source re-reads) -> diff per-function body hashes -> only changed functions' S2 entries die -> S3 sub-hashes recomputed -> compose-input change? O(V+E) rebuild, new generation -> S5 artifacts reused where slice hashes match (body-only edit keeps pagerank/betweenness/clones warm). Comment edit above a function invalidates NOTHING below it (position-relative S2 + identity-ordered FuncIds).

## Gates
- Blocked by TLDR-rfz (measurement gate: CSR + BM25 + edit-path hash fan-out budgets) — no child starts before its verdict.
- Frozen-corpus byte-hash gates apply to all output-identical changes (TLDR-hqb).
- Codex review per child on TLDR-5qm (standing mandate).

## Kills
TLDR-jsi bug class (cache-clear coherence) becomes unexpressible; daemon per-language OnceCell buckets retire (with ADR-9 Am.2).

title: Measurement gate (pre-n74): CSR + BM25 prototype benchmarks on frozen rust corpus — confirm ADR-9 budgets before implementation
description:
## Purpose (the gate)
Discharge the user-ratified MEASUREMENT GATE (TLDR-5qm comment 2 arbitration of Codex F1 BLOCKER; recorded on TLDR-n74 comments 1/10/24) BEFORE n74 implementation starts. ADR-9's complexity contract ("single-digit ms rebuild at 26k edges", O(V+E) scaling, O(deg)/O(answer) queries) is currently DERIVED from data-structure analysis, not MEASURED on real corpora. ADR-3 discipline: measure before committing. This issue is the research-phase home for that measurement — it blocks TLDR-n74; n74 must not start until the verdict here is recorded.

## Corpus
Primary: frozen rust corpus /tmp/tldr-bench@001fdcb — 745 files / 20,320 funcs / 26,312 edges (TLDR-hqb baseline). If the /tmp copy is gone, regenerate per scripts/bench_phase_timing.sh harness at pin 001fdcb. Scaling check: synthetic 10x/100x replication of the edge list (the 100x point matches ADR-9's monorepo design target ~2.6M edges) — django/zod/nest/caddy corpora optional corroboration.

## Prototype 1 — minimal CSR build + query (the F1 blocker itself)
Throwaway bench (bench/ or /tmp, NOT production code; criterion or simple Instant loops with warmup):
1. INGEST: dump the real edge list once from the existing pipeline (function nodes + call edges with file/line meta) to a flat file — ingest cost is NOT part of the measured rebuild (per ADR-9 the rebuild consumes per-file facts already in RAM).
2. BUILD (the measured core): intern table (symbol->u32), Vec<FuncMeta> SoA nodes sorted by file, forward CSR (offsets+targets+edge_meta), reverse CSR via counting sort, name->SmallVec<FuncId> index, file->Range<FuncId> index, per-file sorted (start,end,FuncId).
3. MEASURE build: full snapshot build time from in-RAM fact vectors at 1x/10x/100x. GATE BUDGET: single-digit ms at 26k edges; scaling consistent with O(V+E) (no superlinear bend at 100x). Record peak RSS of the snapshot at each scale (informs the ~200MB@100x projection in ADR-9).
4. MEASURE queries on the built snapshot: callers/callees by-name (O(deg), expect sub-microsecond); reverse-BFS closure from a hub node (impact, O(touched)); full O(V) dead scan; by-name lookup; cursor binary search. Record p50/p99 over >=1k iterations.
5. ArcSwap publish + read overhead: sanity-check only (expect ns).

## Prototype 2 — resident BM25 (audit 10/64 addition)
Over the same corpus's function texts: (a) full index build time; (b) query latency p50/p99; (c) SINGLE-FILE UPDATE cost both ways — full rebuild vs incremental postings update — and DECIDE rebuild-vs-incremental on the numbers (reserve both seams per audit 10). Tokenization can be naive whitespace+ident-split; this measures the data structure, not search quality.

## Explicitly OUT of gate (do not prototype unless triggered)
Per-name occurrence postings (audit 28/64): prototype ONLY IF the live-scan path measures painful here — postings are a prefilter, never a verification replacement.

## Acceptance / exit criteria
- Numbers recorded as a comment HERE and cross-posted to TLDR-n74; Codex review of methodology+numbers logged on TLDR-5qm (standing mandate).
- VERDICT recorded, one of: CONFIRMED (budgets hold -> ADR-9 contract becomes measured fact; n74 unblocked) | REVISED (budgets fail -> amend ADR-9/TLDR-t0s numbers + n74 acceptance BEFORE implementation; user arbitrates) | INVALIDATED (structural surprise -> back to design; user arbitrates).
- BM25 rebuild-vs-incremental decision recorded on n74.
- Prototype code stays throwaway (committed under bench/ or a scratch branch for reproducibility, never wired into crates).
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.

comments.text:

title: [EPIC] Codex design review: ADR-9/10/11 architecture + per-command CLI flow audit feedback
description:
All Codex review output for the new serving architecture lives here (created 2026-06-05, user-mandated).

## Scope
1. ONE-OFF: whole-design review of ADR-9 (resident graph snapshot / daemon-is-the-database, TLDR-t0s), ADR-10 (no silent fallback, TLDR-14i), ADR-11 (render-at-the-edge / binary transport / compact-first, TLDR-kd6) — recorded as the first comment(s) on this epic.
2. PER-COMMAND: every one of the 64 CLI subcommands audited in TLDR-uiy gets a MANDATORY Codex review of its proposed new flow before the audit entry is considered final. Codex feedback recorded here, cross-referenced to the TLDR-uiy audit comment.

## Method per command
- Claude drafts the flow analysis (tier, lifetime, verdict) per TLDR-uiy method
- Codex reviews the draft (codex rescue subagent)
- Accepted feedback folded into the TLDR-uiy record; rejected feedback recorded here WITH rationale
- Disagreements between Claude and Codex surfaced to user for arbitration

## Relationship
- Parent: TLDR-7pp (implementation epic)
- Sibling: TLDR-uiy (the audit itself — this epic is its review gate)
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): The legacy implementation path is absorbed by TLDR-eda5 and the one-shot shared redb ArtifactStore plan. The underlying user-visible requirement is preserved in that plan; this issue is superseded as an implementation vehicle, not erased as historical evidence.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
CODEX WHOLE-DESIGN REVIEW (one-off, 2026-06-05) — ADR-9/10/11 reviewed adversarially, grounded in repo code. RAW FINDINGS:
F1 BLOCKER/ADR-9: codebase doesn't match the ADR — daemon today caches whole ProjectCallGraph per Language via OnceCell (tldr-daemon/src/state.rs:52-65), IR is HashSet/HashMap (cross_file_types.rs:1534-1624), so CSR complexity + 'single-digit ms rebuild' claims are projections, not measured on the real pipeline. REC: benchmark a minimal CSR prototype on real corpora before committing.
F2 MAJOR/ADR-10: current CLI is fallback-FIRST by design (daemon_router.rs:28-131 returns None on any error -> local compute; calls.rs:113-192). ADR-10 rollout is a hard UX break unless every call site updates in lockstep; no central daemon-required contract exists. REC: shared routing policy per command class, structured daemon-missing errors, explicit --oneshot/--local, upgrade-aware messaging.
F3 MAJOR/ADR-11: transport today is axum HTTP + JSON envelopes (server.rs:121-153); no rkyv/bincode path, no schema negotiation, version field unused for handshake. rkyv has alignment/validation/schema-evolution/debuggability sharp edges. REC: versioned envelope + conservative serializer (bincode) first, JSON debug fallback until binary path proves stable; rkyv only with a concrete daemon/CLI-skew migration story.
F4 MAJOR/cross-cutting: dirty-state + concurrent rebuild UNSPECIFIED — what happens when N requests hit a stale snapshot, build fails midway, or watcher invalidates during in-flight rebuild. Today invalidation is blunt clear() (state.rs:231-239). REC: generationed snapshot protocol — readers pin a generation, rebuild off to the side, atomic publish only on success, explicit 'stale-but-serving' / 'rebuild-failed' semantics.
F5 MAJOR/ADR-9+11: 'answer blobs die' cost model incomplete — daemon still returns owned Vecs of edges/strings; no answer cursors/paging/partial materialization specified, so compact-first is not operational yet. REC: define output contracts per query class (full/paged/summary/compact) and verify token savings on real calls/impact/dead/semantic outputs.
F6 MINOR/ADR-10: version-skew underspecified — socket path embeds version (server.rs:49-71) but no handshake; reachable-but-incompatible daemon fails at deserialization. REC: handshake endpoint enforced before routing index-backed commands.
F7 MINOR/ADR-9: 'daemon IS the database' framing oversells — the real design is a typed query service over a resident generationed index; naming it a database drags in semantics the implementation doesn't need.
VERDICT (Codex): direction plausible, design overconfident vs current code. Top-3 before implementation: (1) prototype-benchmark the CSR claims, (2) redesign per-command routing policy with escape hatches before flipping ADR-10, (3) concrete transport compatibility + failure-mode matrix before replacing JSON.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
CLAUDE ASSESSMENT of Codex whole-design review (accept/reject per epic method; disagreements -> user arbitration):
F1: ACCEPT-AS-AMENDED. Codex misreads ADR-9 as a claim about current code (it is the TARGET spec; OnceCell/HashMap state is exactly what's being replaced). But the KERNEL is valid and is pure ADR-3 discipline: 'single-digit ms rebuild' and the O() contract are derived from data-structure analysis, NOT measured on a prototype. PROPOSED ACTION: add a MEASUREMENT GATE to TLDR-n74 — minimal CSR build benchmark on the frozen rust corpus (745/20,320/26,312) must confirm the rebuild budget BEFORE the snapshot lands. Downgrade severity BLOCKER->MAJOR (it blocks ratification of n74's perf claims, not the design direction).
F2: ACCEPT. Known (it is what TLDR-npl exists for) but the concrete recs are better than npl's current sketch: per-command-CLASS routing policy table (which the TLDR-uiy audit is literally producing), structured daemon-missing error type, --oneshot/--local escape hatches, upgrade-aware messaging. FOLD INTO TLDR-npl.
F3: ACCEPT-AS-HEDGE. Within ADR-11's letter ('rkyv preferred OR bincode acceptable'). Codex tips the order: bincode + versioned envelope FIRST, JSON debug fallback retained, rkyv only with a skew-migration story. NEEDS USER ARBITRATION (changes ADR-11's stated preference).
F4: ACCEPT — strongest finding. ADR-9 says 'lazy parallel recompose' but never specifies single-flight/generation semantics. Needs an ADR-9 AMENDMENT: generationed snapshot protocol + an explicit user decision on stale-reads policy (serve-old-while-rebuilding vs block-until-fresh). USER ARBITRATION REQUIRED on the stale-reads question.
F5: ACCEPT — and note the per-command output-contract work IS epic TLDR-uiy; each audit entry will now record the command's output contract (full/paged/summary/compact). Token verification on real outputs = TLDR-5kw acceptance criterion.
F6: ACCEPT. Fold handshake-before-routing into TLDR-npl (pairs with F2).
F7: NOTE ONLY. Rhetorical: 'typed query service over a resident generationed index' IS ADR-9 minus the slogan. No action.
PROCESS CHANGES ADOPTED FROM THIS REVIEW: every TLDR-uiy audit entry from 2/64 onward records (a) index-backed vs FS-truth (ADR-10 Am.1), (b) OUTPUT CONTRACT class (F5), (c) routing policy class (F2).

F5 -> output-contract class becomes a standard field of every TLDR-uiy audit entry. F7 -> note only. F1 BLOCKER: body-hash sharing across files UNSOUND — identical text != identical semantics; receiver resolution reads full source/imports/enclosing class (resolution.rs apply_type_resolution, Python/TypeScript receiver indexes, ImportResolver keyed on current_file).

F3 MAJOR: topology-hash keying needs collision hardening; repo already treats u64 collisions as correctness bugs (vector_store.rs).

F5 BLOCKER: 'compose never reads bodies' FALSE today — apply_type_resolution scans full source; receiver indexes built from source text; ImportMap depends on body parse.

F7 MAJOR: hashing fan-out (file + per-function + S3 sub-hashes + slice hashes) unproven vs ~4ms edit budget; avoid multiple source re-reads per invalidation cycle.

title: [EPIC] CLI x ADR-9 fit audit: every command walked through the tier model, one at a time
description:
Systematic design review (started 2026-06-05, user-driven): walk EVERY CLI subcommand through the ADR-9/10/11 architecture (tier model, resident CSR snapshot, render-at-the-edge, no-silent-fallback) and record whether its flow fits, what it needs, and any design decisions that fall out. The audit IS the design review for epic TLDR-7pp — misfits surface here before implementation, not during.

## Method (per command, recorded as a comment on this epic)
1. WHAT it computes (inputs -> output)
2. WHICH tier serves it (T0 filesystem / T1 per-file facts / T2 project snapshot+indexes / T3 persist / per-query compute)
3. LIFETIME of its answer (per file-version / project-version / query / external-input)
4. VERDICT: CLEAN-FIT | FIT-WITH-NOTE (works, needs a recorded design note) | MISFIT (needs design work — gets its own issue)
5. DECISIONS arising (added to this epic; promoted to ADR if architectural)

## Command inventory (64, audit order = help order)
tree structure calls impact dead reaching-defs taint available slice search context smells extract imports importers complexity churn debt health hubs whatbreaks patterns inheritance change-impact deps diagnostics doctor references clones dice loc cognitive halstead coverage hotspots embed semantic similar daemon cache warm stats surface contracts dead-stores chop specs invariants verify cohesion temporal resources coupling interface explain todo secure definition diff api-check vuln fix bugbot help

## Expected clusters (hypothesis, to be verified command-by-command)
- Graph queries (calls/impact/dead/hubs/...) -> T2 CSR primitives
- Per-file/per-function analyses (complexity/cfg/dfg/slice/...) -> T1 facts or on-demand per-file compute
- Semantic flow (search/embed/similar) -> Flow-2, untouched (boundary per utj note)
- External-tool wrappers (diagnostics/doctor/fix) -> out of scope for the tier model, but ADR-10 routing still applies
- Infra (daemon/cache/warm/stats) -> the machinery itself
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.
close_reason: Audit complete: all 64 CLI subcommands walked through the ADR-9 tier model, each Codex-reviewed (TLDR-5qm) and user-ratified. Outputs: 7 ADR amendments + 15 cross-cutting contracts folded into TLDR-n74 spec; divergence/bug findings filed as TLDR-7vb, TLDR-lkx, TLDR-jsi. TLDR-5qm stays open as the standing Codex-review log for the n74 implementation phase.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
AUDIT 1/64: tree — VERDICT: FIT-WITH-NOTE.
WHAT: file tree (--ext filter, -H hidden). Today: whole-project JSON blob (warm step 3) / cold FS walk.
TIER: not a graph query — a RENDERING of the file table (ADR-11's purest case). Daemon ships filtered path list; CLI renders.
LIFETIME: invalidated by create/delete/rename, NOT content edits — different class than FileIR memo.
DECISIONS ARISING:
- D1 (-> TLDR-iqr/TLDR-4vb): watcher contract gains EVENT-TYPE granularity: modify -> evict 1 memo entry + dirty; create/delete/rename -> file-table version bump + dirty.
- D2 (-> TLDR-bpf): resident FILE TABLE (sorted paths + per-dir Range slices + per-entry flags lang/ignored/hidden) becomes a first-class T2 artifact, shared with the unified ignore oracle — one membership source of truth.
- D3: raw-FS views (-H etc.) are EXPLICIT live FS walks — they query the filesystem, not the index; honest semantics, and the resident table never holds node_modules/target junk (millions of paths at 100x).
OPEN QUESTION (ADR-10 boundary, awaiting user): loud-failure for ALL commands vs only INDEX-BACKED answers (FS-truth commands like tree -H / doctor run local — nothing to be stale about). Recommendation: index-backed only.

Per-command classification (index-backed vs FS-truth) becomes a standard field of each audit entry from 2/64 onward. ALSO: process change from this point — every audit entry gets a MANDATORY Codex review before being considered final; Codex feedback logged on new epic TLDR-5qm (whole-design review of ADR-9/10/11 happens first, also on TLDR-5qm).

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
AUDIT 2/64: structure — VERDICT: FIT-WITH-NOTE. (Codex-reviewed: AGREE-WITH-CHANGES, log on TLDR-5qm.)
WHAT: per-file functions/classes/imports for a path -> CodeStructure. Today: daemon whole-JSON blob OR silent local fallback; language auto-detect silently defaults to PYTHON; one language per call; max_results = hard truncation (stops at N files, no marker).
TIER: T2 projection — node table sliced via file->Range<FuncId> (O(slice); directory = concat slices over file-table subtree) + imports folded into snapshot per D1.
LIFETIME: project-version. ADR-10 CLASS: index-backed -> daemon-required. OUTPUT CONTRACT: paged-list (first command where O(answer) = whole project at 100x; scoped by default, whole-project dump = T3 export).
DECISIONS RATIFIED (user, 2026-06-05):
- D1: per-file IMPORT summaries FOLD INTO the T2 snapshot at compose (one-tier read; import resolution already feeds the project-version module index). Serves structure/imports/importers/deps.
- D2 -> PROMOTED to ADR-9 Amendment 2 (TLDR-t0s): snapshot is LANGUAGE-UNIFIED — one snapshot, unified FuncId space, file table carries per-file language, -l becomes a filter, silent Python default dies. Per-language normalization to be defined in TLDR-n74 spec.
- D3 (cross-cutting, applies to ALL list-shaped commands from here on): PAGED-LIST standard contract — total count + truncation marker + continuation cursor in the response envelope; replaces hard caps. Lands with bincode envelope in TLDR-n74.
CODEX NEW FIND folded: ignore-spec DIVERGENCE today — local fallback uses IgnoreSpec::default(), daemon structure handler passes None -> silently different results between paths. Cross-filed to TLDR-bpf (one-oracle rule); ADR-10's dual-path kill also kills this divergence class. NEXT: 3/64 calls.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
AUDIT 3/64: calls — VERDICT: FIT-WITH-NOTE (+ live defects filed as TLDR-7vb). (Codex-reviewed: AGREE-WITH-CHANGES; log on TLDR-5qm — NOTE: Codex grounded two BLOCKERs in the WRONG daemon, the unwired tldr-daemon axum crate; I re-verified against the real in-CLI daemon and the conclusions held with different evidence.)
WHAT: whole cross-file call graph — nodes = full function inventory (BUG-AGG12-4) + edges truncated at max_items=200 via LEXICAL STRING SORT as 'importance'. json/text/dot (dot already renders at the CLI edge — ADR-11-conformant).
TIER: T2 — purest snapshot client; the answer IS the CSR enumerated. O(page) serving; whole-graph dump = T3 export (100x full JSON ~850MB disqualified).
LIFETIME: project-version. ADR-10: index-backed -> daemon-required. OUTPUT CONTRACT: paged-list.
DEFECTS CONFIRMED (filed TLDR-7vb, closed by n74): (A) daemon path DEAD — schema mismatch -> silent fallback always; (B) V1-vs-V2 oracle split daemon-vs-local; (C) warm step caches an answer no consumer can deserialize. ADR-10 exhibit.
DECISIONS RATIFIED (user, 2026-06-05):
- D1: canonical paging order = SNAPSHOT ORDER (FuncId-major, deterministic across identical snapshots); lexical sort-on-truncate dies (at 100x it would sort 2.6M strings to show 200).
- D2: SPLIT the conflated answer — calls = EDGES (paged, snapshot order); node INVENTORY is its own paged view; envelope totals preserve BUG-AGG12-4 faithful-count intent. Schema break versioned with the bincode envelope (n74).
- D3 (cross-cutting -> TLDR-npl): FLAG-PARITY RULE — every behavior-affecting CLI flag rides the request envelope; the daemon never substitutes its own defaults for unforwarded flags. (Today: DaemonCommand::Calls lacks max_items/respect_ignore; router does not even forward language.)
- D4 (-> TLDR-n74): TWO daemon implementations in-tree (real: tldr-cli/src/commands/daemon/daemon.rs 104KB, what daemon start spawns; unwired: tldr-daemon axum crate with divergent schemas). n74 spec MUST OPEN with the host decision. MISFIT-class finding, recorded not yet ratified.
NEXT: 4/64 impact.

title: ADR-11: Render-at-the-edge — binary daemon-to-CLI transport; all user formats are CLI-side renderings; compact is the primary surface; 100x scale is the design target
description:
## Decision
(2026-06-05, user-ratified) Three bindings:
1. INTERNAL TRANSPORT IS BINARY: the daemon->CLI hop is machine-to-machine and ours on both ends — it carries rkyv (preferred; zero-copy, the bytes ARE the structure) or bincode (acceptable), never a JSON document. The expensive boundary ceases to exist; nothing is serialized 'constantly, again and again, periodically' for internal movement.
2. FORMATTING COST IS PAID ONLY FOR WHAT THE HUMAN/AGENT ASKED TO SEE (the ratified philosophy): -f json / jsonl / text / compact are RENDERINGS applied at the CLI edge to the (usually small) answer. JSON demotes from 'the data' to 'one view of the data' — no consumer contract breaks, and rendering 200 rows costs nothing.
3. -f compact IS THE PRIMARY SURFACE (user: 'will be the most used method'): the agent-facing token-lean rendering is a first-class product feature, measured in TOKENS (the product metric), not milliseconds. JSON key-repetition costs 2-4x tokens for identical information.

## Scale target: 100x current (user-stated plan)
~75k files / ~2M functions / ~2.6M edges. Derived budgets that this ADR's choices must hold at:
- Snapshot resident ~200-300MB; rebuild O(V+E) ~50-150ms (lazy per edit) — holds.
- Graph walks 10-50ms worst case — holds (linear math).
- Full dump: JSON ~850MB/5-8s = DISQUALIFIED at target scale; rkyv view ~50-80MB/sub-second = required, not optional. This is why transport-binary is an architecture decision, not an optimization.
- First warm ~25-35s once; per-save parallel recompose ~1-3s; Tier-1 memo ~1-3GB.

## Tripwires armed (measure, then act — ADR-3 discipline)
- T1: if per-save recompose at real scale measures painful -> incremental compose re-enters the design space.
- T2: if restart (~30s re-parse at 100x) or memo RAM (~GBs) measures painful -> UNPARK TLDR-zde's disk chunk store (rkyv per-file facts, mmap restart) — it slots under Tier 1 unchanged; the seam was kept clean for exactly this.
- T3: rebuild-vs-surgery for the CSR snapshot revisited only on measured rebuild pain.

## Rejected
- Swapping the user-facing default format as a PERF measure (perf lives in the transport + answer-size, not the edge rendering).
- Document formats (incl. MessagePack/JSONL) for the internal hop — strictly dominated by zero-copy.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.
