title: Eval harness benchmarks ArcticM (code default) but users run their configured model (e.g. ArcticL) — benchmark doesn't measure what's deployed
description: The semantic_eval harness builds its index with Some(Default::default()) (semantic_eval.rs:121) -> EmbedOptions::default() -> EmbeddingModel::default() = ArcticM (768-dim, the #[default] enum variant). It NEVER reads ~/.tldr/config.json. The real CLI path uses EmbeddingModel::resolve(config) which DOES read config. On this machine the global config sets model=arctic-l (1024-dim), so the user's actual 'tldr semantic' runs ArcticL while the benchmark runs ArcticM. CONSEQUENCE: the prefix verdict (recall@5 0.071->0.857, MRR 0.685) is measured on ArcticM and is UNVALIDATED for the model the user actually deploys. The handoff's claim 'benchmark with the PRODUCTION model ArcticM' was imprecise — ArcticM is the shipped enum default, not necessarily the user's configured/production model. There is no beads decision establishing ArcticM as 'production' (searched). FIX: make the eval resolve the model the same way the CLI does (EmbeddingModel::resolve via TldrConfig::resolve), OR accept a model arg/env so the benchmark can target the deployed model. Then re-run the prefix verdict on ArcticL to validate. Also revisit which model is the intended default/production target — separate product decision.
acceptance_criteria: Eval harness benchmarks the same model the CLI resolves (config-aware or explicit arg); prefix verdict re-confirmed on ArcticL; intended production/default model documented.
notes: Child of TLDR-blm. Measurement-validity gap surfaced during the prefix-verdict dogfooding. Pairs with TLDR-h27 (threshold) — both are 'eval passes but CLI behaves differently' gaps: eval hardcodes ArcticM + threshold 0.0, CLI uses ArcticL + threshold 0.50.
close_reason: semantic_eval now resolves the deployed model via TldrConfig::resolve (matches the CLI), with TLDR_EVAL_MODEL override, instead of the hardcoded EmbeddingModel::default() (ArcticM). Eval now benchmarks the model users actually run (e.g. ArcticL). semantic_eval.rs.

title: LLM-generated function descriptions for embedding (summary-augmented retrieval)
description: Highest-leverage quality lever for semantic search. At index time, call a cheap/fast LLM (e.g. Haiku) per chunk to generate a 1-line natural-language description of what the function does, then embed THAT (alongside or instead of code). Attacks the root cause: queries are English but raw code lacks query words; an English description bridges the gap (e.g. 'combines two ranked lists via reciprocal rank fusion' matches a 'combine two rankings' query). Known RAG pattern (document/summary augmentation; cousin of HyDE). NEITHER llm-tldr (python) NOR tldr-core has attempted this (verified by grep). User will provide LLM API key.
design: Indexing stage: (1) per-chunk LLM call -> 1-line description; (2) CACHE keyed by content_hash so we pay once per function and only re-summarize changed functions (mirror the embedding cache's incremental model); (3) feed description into build_embedding_text. Cost: ~one cheap call per function, one-time + incremental, fully cached. Provider/key via existing config (config.rs already has embedding provider/api_key_env scaffolding). DEFERRED to a later iteration per user; this task captures it.
acceptance_criteria: Per-chunk descriptions generated via configurable LLM provider; cached by content hash; included in embedding text; measurable recall@5/MRR lift vs the prefix+enrichment baseline on the eval harness.
notes:
SEQUENCING (2026-06-01): TLDR-d8f (embed EXISTING docstrings, free, no API key) is the cheaper precursor — do it first and measure. 9m2's LLM-generated descriptions then target the functions that LACK docstrings (or to augment thin ones). Both attack the same modality gap; d8f is the zero-cost slice, 9m2 the full-coverage version. Still needs your LLM API key (Haiku per spec).
OWNER PRIORITY (2026-07-27): Version-two retrieval work postponed until the shared artifact architecture, watcher scheduling, and command-surface adoption are complete.

title: Phase 1a: wire enrichment.rs into SemanticIndex::build
description: enrichment.rs (build_embedding_text, 8-field recipe matching the Python original) is fully implemented but NEVER called. index.rs:310-313 embeds raw chunk.content. Wire enrich_chunks+build_embedding_text into the build path. MUST bump cache key with an embed-recipe version tag (e.g. embed_schema=enriched-v1) so stale raw-embedded vectors aren't reused. Biggest quality lever; no new dependency.
notes:
QUADRATIC FIXED: enrichment re-parsed each file ~3x PER FUNCTION via get_cfg_context/get_dfg_context. Now FileAnalysisCache parses each file ONCE (file_trees) and CFG/DFG reuse it via extract_cfg_from_tree + extract_dfg_from_tree_with_cfg (the pre-parsed helpers that already existed for vuln scanning). Result: enrich-on over 272 chunks = 16.7s (was: hung 12min/12GB on full crate). 

MEASURED (semantic/ scope, 8 cases, prefix on): enrich OFF -> R@5 0.875/MRR 0.875; enrich ON (with CFG/DFG) -> R@5 0.875/MRR 0.708. Enrichment did NOT help here — slightly hurt ranking. Tempers the 'enrichment is the biggest lever' hypothesis. CAVEATS: small/noisy scope; CFG/DFG-on variant only (cheap signal-only untested, blocked by cache tag not capturing flow flag); full-corpus untested. Enrichment stays GATED OFF by default. Prefix remains the only proven win so far.
close_reason: Enrichment wired into SemanticIndex::build + per-function re-parse quadratic fixed (reuses extract_cfg_from_tree/extract_dfg_from_tree_with_cfg), shipped 37ab719+e9e5427. Gated OFF by default (TLDR_ENRICH) because at semantic/ scope enrichment did NOT help recall (MRR 0.875->0.708 w/ CFG/DFG). Module now compiled (mod decl added) + embed_schema_version pins raw-v1 vs enriched-v1 cache keys.

title: Phase 0: semantic search eval harness (recall@5 / MRR gold set)

title: Results-equivalence verification harness
description: The real pass/fail gate. Replay the captured baseline queries (tests 1-7 outputs: scores + snippets, the golden reference) against the new mmap-backed build and DIFF the ranked results. With brute-force + f32 kept, results must be IDENTICAL. Also capture cold-latency old vs new to confirm the ~710ms single-file target. Latency improvement is necessary but NOT sufficient -- equivalence is the gate. Record results on the epic.
notes: REFRAMED: verify usearch exact_search_f32 returns results IDENTICAL to the current brute-force top_k_similar over the captured baseline (scores+order). This is the PASS/FAIL gate (results-equivalence, not latency) — usearch exact mode must match, else investigate metric/normalization (cosine vs IP; vectors are unit-normalized already).
close_reason: Equivalence GATE PROVEN (the stated pass/fail). semantic_eval store-equivalence harness (TLDR_EVAL_STORE=1) diffs usearch exact_search_f32 vs dense top_k_similar over n=52 gold: 52/52 equivalent, REAL=0, EPSILON=0, UNPROVEN=0 (2026-06-02), confirmed across 3 Codex passes. Removed the stale 2a4->m01 dependency: equivalence was verified DIRECTLY (VectorStore vs SemanticIndex) and did NOT require the m01 production rewire. Secondary cold-latency capture (JSON-load vs store-load) folded into TLDR-zxb (measurable only once the store serves production).

title: Rewire EmbeddingCache onto usearch Index
description:
Rewire EmbeddingCache (cache.rs) onto the usearch-backed store (TLDR-l5d) while keeping the PUBLIC API stable (open/get/put/flush/len/is_empty) so index.rs / similarity.rs need ZERO changes. (REFRAMED from the obsolete 'MmapVectorStore' wording — we use the usearch library via l5d.)

KEY POINT — EmbeddingCache IS the content-addressed dedup layer (design doc §4.1):
- Keep get(chunk, model) / put(chunk, embedding, model) keyed by (content_hash, model, embed_schema) so an UNCHANGED body (revert, rename, ordinal-churn) is a CACHE HIT, never a re-embed.
- This dedup layer is DISTINCT from the key(u64)->vector usearch SEARCH index that l5d builds. m01 makes EmbeddingCache persist/dedup vectors via the usearch store instead of the 1.4GB JSON HashMap (cache.rs load_with_lock). Do NOT collapse the two or drop content-hash dedup.

- get/put/flush delegate to the l5d store; signatures unchanged so callers (index.rs build/search/find_similar) compile and behave identically.
- GC = reachability-on-full-reindex (drop keys not re-added) per the locked decision (TLDR-rgc); cached_at/file_mtime droppable once reachability-GC lands.

Depends on TLDR-l5d. Full design: docs/INCREMENTAL_REINDEX_DESIGN.md.
acceptance_criteria: EmbeddingCache get/put/flush/open/len/is_empty signatures UNCHANGED; index.rs build()/search()/find_similar() compile + behave identically (results IDENTICAL on the n=52 eval + captured baselines); vectors persist/dedup via the usearch store, NOT the JSON HashMap; content-hash dedup preserved (unchanged body on rekey = cache hit, no re-embed); 1.4GB cache.json path removed; reachability-GC drops orphaned keys on full reindex.
notes:
REFRAMED mmap->usearch. EmbeddingCache.get/put/flush delegate to the usearch wrapper (TLDR-l5d) instead of the JSON HashMap (cache.rs load_with_lock:236). Keep the get/put/flush signatures so callers (index.rs) are untouched.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.
close_reason: Core goal achieved: VectorStore is the production search path (PR1 store_search helper + PR2 zxb wiring). EmbeddingCache format migration to follow in TLDR-3gj.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: M01 PLAN (Codex-reviewed, code-grounded 2026-06-02). STRATEGY: load() into RAM (NOT view()/mmap — no view path exists yet; mmap pulls in unimplemented reader-grace = TLDR-pdb, deferred). SemanticIndex is already RAM-backed brute-force, so parity is natural. SMALLEST SAFE PR: add ONE shared store-backed helper that (1) derives a REAL ManifestId::for_build (resolves 7al inline — pass real chunk_params=granularity+languages, walker_version; model_revision/dims/embed_schema already real), (2) tries VectorStore::load(), (3) on miss/LoadFail builds+saves then searches, (4) FALLS BACK to SemanticIndex::build().search() on ANY store I/O error (never surface to user). Wire into: CLI cold path crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/semantic.rs:~153; daemon warm/semantic path daemon.rs:~480-484,569-598; MCP dense path crates/tldr-mcp/src/tools/search.rs:~168-176. LEAVE cache.rs UNTOUCHED — EmbeddingCache stays the content-addressed (file,fn,content_hash,model+schema)->vec dedup layer, consumed only inside VectorStore::build; do NOT change get/put or JSON format. TOP FAILURE MODES to test: (1) SCORE INVERSION — SearchHit.distance is cosine DISTANCE (lower=better); SemanticIndex reports SIMILARITY; convert score=1-distance BEFORE thresholds. (2) SNIPPETS — ChunkMeta has lines/hash not content; must lazy-read by file/line or keep SemanticIndex for snippet paths. (3) MANIFEST staleness — test model-change AND granularity/language-change both trigger LoadFail::Incompatible. (4) PATH-KEY drift — test relative vs absolute/canonical roots (set_key_root/root_relative). (5) FALLBACK — every LoadFail variant (no-gen, checksum drift, torn CURRENT, missing sidecar) must rebuild-and-save, not error. DEFERRED to follow-ups: view()/mmap, pdb reader-grace, incremental deltas (t8f), 'similar' replacement, EmbeddingCache format changes, HNSW/i8, deleting SemanticIndex.

title: Integrate usearch as vector store (add_f32 / exact_search_f32 / save / load) + key->metadata sidecar
description:
FIRST PASS = full-rebuild usearch store (NO incremental; incremental = TLDR-t8f). Full design: docs/INCREMENTAL_REINDEX_DESIGN.md (§3 store, §4 data model, §7 persistence). Supersedes the hand-rolled memmap2+bincode 'MmapVectorStore' (TLDR-j8c) — we use the usearch LIBRARY.

VECTOR STORE — usearch NativeIndex, key(u64) -> vector:
- add_f32(key,&[f32]) on build; exact_search_f32 for query (exact KNN, NOT HNSW). f32 ONLY (i8 = TLDR-ccg).
- load()/save() into a WRITABLE RAM index, NOT view() (view() is read-only #97; at ~58MB load() is cheap and keeps it writable for t8f). load() is scale-bounded (revisit view() past ~20 daemons / 500MB+ monorepo). Metric cos (unit-normalized).

CONTENT-ADDRESSED DEDUP layer — kept DISTINCT from key->vector: (content_hash, model, embed_schema) -> vector, so renames/ordinal-churn re-add WITHOUT re-embedding (the current EmbeddingCache role; do not drop it).

SIDECAR + PER-FILE record — usearch stores ONLY vectors; everything else lives here:
- key -> ChunkMeta {identity, file_rel_path, function_name, class_name, line_start, line_end, content_hash}.
- file_rel_path -> FileRecord {keys, mtime, size, file_type}.
- Snippets are read LAZILY from source at query time (single buffered read -> hash that buffer -> render; validated by content_hash; degrade to no-snippet on missing/changed/out-of-range), NOT stored.

MANIFEST (one per store) covering every input that changes vectors OR chunk boundaries: format_version, generation, embedding_model, model_revision (tokenizer+weights), dimensions, metric, scalar_kind, search_mode, embed_schema, chunk_params, walker_version, root, chunk_count, keys_checksum (key-set digest), index_checksum (index FILE bytes), sidecar_checksum. load() REJECTS -> full rebuild on ANY mismatch.

CRASH-SAFE SAVE (doc §7.1 — NOT 'temp+rename then manifest last', which clobbers the live pair): generation-suffixed IMMUTABLE files index.<gen>.usearch / meta.<gen> / manifest.<gen>; a structured CURRENT {magic, gen, checksum} pointer whose atomic rename is the SOLE commit point; fsync files AND dir; GC retains KEEP_GENS (3) + a grace window (60s), never the gen CURRENT points at. On invalid/torn CURRENT, scan manifest.<gen> newest->oldest for the newest verifying trio. Single-writer (daemon) / multi-reader (incl. the cold CLI): readers snapshot CURRENT, open the immutable trio, retry on a GC'd file.

HARDEN the root-relative key: strip_prefix failure must WARN + use a canonical fallback, never the silent raw-path fallback that reverts the atc bug (tracked as TLDR-ss3).

OUTCOME vs the 1.4GB JSON cache.json: ~58MB f32 binary + small sidecar; daemon RAM ~2.3GB -> ~0.5GB; first-load ~14s -> sub-second.
acceptance_criteria: usearch store builds the full index (add_f32) and searches (exact_search_f32) with results IDENTICAL to the JSON-cache path on the n=52 eval + captured baselines; content-addressed dedup layer prevents re-embedding unchanged bodies on rekey/rename; sidecar resolves key->{path,fn,class,line range,content_hash} + per-file {keys,mtime,size,file_type}; MANIFEST gates load (any model/model_revision/dims/scalar/search_mode/embed_schema/chunk_params/walker_version/root mismatch, OR keys_/index_/sidecar_checksum failure, OR generation mismatch -> full rebuild, never silent); crash-safe generation+CURRENT save survives SIGKILL at any point and a torn CURRENT falls back to the newest verifying manifest.<gen>; concurrent cold-CLI reader + daemon writer never see a torn/half store; first-load ~14s -> sub-second and daemon RSS drops materially (1.4GB JSON -> ~58MB f32); f32 only (i8 = TLDR-ccg); NO incremental (full rebuild only; incremental = TLDR-t8f); cache.json path seam-switched/removed.
notes:
USEARCH FEATURE GUIDANCE (research 2026-06-01): CORE = view() [read-only mmap, query path] + exact_search_f32 [100% recall, 20x faster than FAISS flat, vendor-recommended for <1M vectors] + save() + add(). add() builds an unused HNSW graph (~1.5s @117K, negligible) — fine; optionally set low connectivity to trim graph RAM. KEY CONSTRAINT (issue#97): view() is READ-ONLY — you canNOT add to a mmap'd on-disk index. So: QUERY path = view()+exact_search (low RSS); UPDATE path = load() into RAM + add/remove + save(). EXPLOIT LATER: i8 ScalarKind quantization (near-lossless for cosine+unit-norm, 4x smaller) as opt-in compact mode; filtered_search_f32 predicate for scoped/path-filtered queries. Metric = Cos (vectors already unit-normalized — could also use IP since normalized).
2026-06-01 RESCOPED to match docs/INCREMENTAL_REINDEX_DESIGN.md (committed 73cf41f): use usearch load() into a WRITABLE RAM index, NOT view()/mmap (view() is read-only issue#97 and unneeded at ~58MB f32/~15MB i8 — load() is cheap and keeps the index writable, the prereq for t8f). f32 FIRST; i8 quantization is opt-in later (ccg). Metadata SIDECAR is required (usearch stores vectors only). Full-rebuild only this pass. The OLD description (hand-rolled memmap2+bincode 'MmapVectorStore' via j8c) is OBSOLETE — the usearch library supersedes it. Prior USEARCH FEATURE GUIDANCE notes remain valid for the API.
2026-06-02 CODEX REVIEW (thread a708b3161b2e63d89) — KEEP the sidecar IN l5d; do NOT defer it to t8f (an earlier reconciliation idea — REJECTED). Rationale: a persisted usearch index is vectors-only, so after a daemon RESTART, search results (path/fn/line range/snippet) cannot be reconstructed without the sidecar, and re-chunking the whole tree on every restart is exactly the cost we remove. So l5d ships: usearch vector store + sidecar + MANIFEST. ADD to scope: (1) Store MANIFEST {format_version, generation, embedding_model, dimensions, metric, scalar_kind, embed_schema, root, chunk_count, checksum}; load() REJECTS->full-rebuild on any mismatch (model/dims/scalar/schema/root/format or index-vs-manifest count/dims or checksum or index-vs-sidecar generation). (2) PAIRED-ATOMIC save: usearch save() is NOT atomic temp+rename — write index+sidecar+manifest to temps, fsync, rename, with the MANIFEST rename as the single commit point (crash before it leaves the old trio intact). (3) HARDEN the root-relative key: strip_prefix failure must warn + use a canonical fallback, NOT the silent raw-path fallback that reverts to the original bug. CAVEATS to document (not blockers): load() is scale-bounded (revisit view() past ~20 daemons / 500MB+ monorepo); i8 is a REAL option (exact_search_i8 + separate quantized index + quantized query) deferred to ccg, not irrelevant. Full design: docs/INCREMENTAL_REINDEX_DESIGN.md (317293b).
2026-06-02 ROUND-3 (Codex re-review, design doc 9d5d8d5): crash-safe save REVISED — NOT 'rename index+sidecar then manifest last' (that clobbers the live pair); use GENERATION-SUFFIXED immutable files (index/meta/manifest.<gen>) + a CURRENT pointer whose atomic rename is the SOLE commit point + dir fsync + keep gen-1 as rollback (doc §7.1). Manifest must cover ALL vector/boundary inputs: + model_revision (tokenizer+weights), chunk_params, walker_version, search_mode, keys_checksum (sorted vector-key-set digest, catches index/sidecar drift) — not just model name. Per-file record adds mtime+size (reconcile signal). l5d MUST keep a content-addressed (content_hash,model,embed_schema)->vector dedup layer SEPARATE from key->vector, else renames/ordinal-churn become real re-embeds. Snippets = lazy source read at query time (no sidecar bloat). Load() rejects any manifest mismatch -> full rebuild.
2026-06-02 VERIFIED on current checkout by command: TLDR_QUIET=1 TLDR_EVAL_STORE=1 cargo run -p tldr-core --release --example semantic_eval -- crates/tldr-core/src. Dense baseline: R@5=0.750 (39/52), R@10=0.827 (43/52), MRR=0.599. Store equivalence: order-identical=39, TIE(gap<1e-6)=12, EPSILON(<1e-4)=1, REAL(>=1e-4)=0, equivalent modulo ties/epsilon=52/52. This satisfies l5d results-equivalence: no genuine ranking divergence; only arbitrary equal-score/epsilon boundary ordering.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.

title: Define MmapVectorStore format + abstraction
description: Design the on-disk format and the Rust abstraction for the vector store. Format: header (magic, version, model name, dim, count) + contiguous f32 vectors region (fixed stride = dim*4, 4-byte aligned) + a hash->offset index map (bincode) at the tail. One file per embedding model (dim is fixed per model: arctic-s 384 / arctic-m 768 / arctic-l 1024). Key = 64-bit hash(content_hash + file_path + function_name) -- same identity as today's CacheKey minus model (model implied by file). Define a trait so the backend is swappable. Must support zero-copy &[f32] reads from the mmap.

title: Lock backend + GC decisions for mmap store
description: Finalize the two open design forks before implementation: (1) Backend = plain mmap (memmap2 + bincode hash->offset map) vs usearch. (2) GC = reachability-on-full-reindex (leaning; drops cached_at/file_mtime, entry becomes key->Vec<f32>) vs timestamp bookkeeping file. Output: a recorded decision (bd decision) that unblocks the impl children.

C++ build dep (cxx bridge) accepted by user 2026-06-01. usearch exact_search_f32 + view (mmap) + save/load + ScalarKind cover the exact-search + load + persistence + quant goals as a maintained library. GC fork: GC-by-reachability on full re-index (usearch index rebuilt from chunks; drops per-entry timestamps -> simplest, matches the rebuild model). Cascade recorded in memory 'usearch-discovery'/'decision-locked'.

This issue's description says usearch 'builds HNSW on every add() for a search we dont use' and implies approximate-only. title: Replace JSON embedding cache with usearch-backed vector store (keep exact search)
description:
## EPIC: Replace the JSON embedding cache with a usearch vector store

### The measured problem
Cold `tldr semantic/similar/embed` = ~4,300ms JSON parse + 500ms model load + 200ms query embed + ~0.1ms brute-force cosine. The 1.4GB cache.json (text-encoded float vectors, multiple models) is loaded IN FULL to serve a handful of lookups. The brute-force cosine is NOT the bottleneck; the JSON load is.

### Decisions — LOCKED (2026-06-01/02, incl. Codex review)
- Backend = **usearch** (NOT hand-rolled memmap2+bincode; the old "usearch vs plain mmap" open decision is CLOSED).
- **exact_search_f32** (NOT HNSW — exact/100% recall, vendor-recommended <1M vectors).
- **load() into a WRITABLE RAM index**, NOT view()/mmap (view() is read-only #97; at ~58MB f32 load() is cheap and keeps the index writable, which incremental needs). load() is scale-bounded — revisit view() past ~20 daemons / 500MB+ monorepo.
- **f32 first** (i8 = TLDR-ccg; separate quantized index + quantized query).
- Metric = cos (unit-normalized vectors).
- Win: 1.4GB JSON -> ~58MB f32 binary; daemon RSS ~2.3GB -> ~0.5GB.

### Sidecar — SCOPE EVOLVED (resolved with Codex review)
Original cold-CLI scope: ALL metadata was rebuilt by chunk_code() at search time, so NO persistent sidecar was needed (verified: cache.rs stored only {vector, cached_at, file_mtime}). That no longer holds. With the warm DAEMON path now shipped (TLDR-atc), the store is PERSISTED and served from a resident daemon, so a restart must serve results WITHOUT re-chunking the whole tree. Therefore a metadata **SIDECAR + MANIFEST** is now a **correctness** requirement of l5d (not optional, not deferrable to t8f). Full design: docs/INCREMENTAL_REINDEX_DESIGN.md (§4 sidecar/manifest, §7 crash-safe save).

### Targets / honesty
- Cold first-load: ~14s (1.4GB JSON) -> sub-second (usearch load()).
- Warm daemon repeat query: ~45ms — ALREADY ACHIEVED via atc + the root-relative cache-key fix.
- Do NOT promise a fixed latency for directory searches; the sidecar now persists metadata so warm dir searches can skip re-chunking (measure before promising).

### PASS/FAIL = results-equivalence, not latency
Exact brute-force + f32 kept -> new ranked results must be IDENTICAL to the JSON-cache path (n=52 eval + captured baselines). Latency improvement is necessary but NOT sufficient.

### Children
l5d (usearch store + sidecar + manifest + crash-safe save), m01 (rewire EmbeddingCache onto the store, keep a content-addressed dedup layer), ccg (i8 compact mode), t8f (incremental delta), zr6 (filtered/scoped search).
design:
RESOLVED design (supersedes the earlier 'plain mmap vs usearch' + 'NO sidecar' framing).

## Bottleneck (measured)
Cold query = 4.3s JSON parse + 0.5s model load + 0.2s query embed + ~0.1ms cosine. The brute-force cosine is irrelevant; HNSW would make it 0.5ms AND approximate. KEEP exact brute-force semantics via usearch exact_search_f32. KEEP f32.

## Store (usearch)
- key (u64) -> vector. add_f32 on build; remove(key) for deltas; exact_search_f32 for query; save/load (writable RAM, not view()).
- One logical store per model (dim fixed per model: arctic-s 384 / m 768 / l 1024).
- Content-addressed DEDUP layer kept SEPARATE from key->vector: a (content_hash, model, embed_schema) -> vector lookup so renames/ordinal-churn re-add without re-embedding (the current EmbeddingCache role; do NOT drop it).

## Sidecar + manifest (l5d correctness — see design doc)
- Sidecar: key -> {identity, file_rel_path, fn, class, line range, content_hash}; per-file record {keys, mtime, size}.
- Manifest covers EVERY input that changes vectors or chunk boundaries: format_version, generation, embedding_model, model_revision (tokenizer+weights), dimensions, metric, scalar_kind, search_mode, embed_schema, chunk_params, walker_version, root, chunk_count, keys_checksum, sidecar_checksum. load() rejects any mismatch -> full rebuild.
- Crash-safe save: generation-suffixed immutable files + a CURRENT pointer whose atomic rename is the sole commit point + dir fsync + keep gen-1 (design doc §7.1). usearch save() is NOT atomic by itself.
- Snippets: read lazily from source at query time, validated by content_hash, degrade gracefully (no sidecar bloat).

## GC
content_hash in the dedup key => changed content orphans old entries. GC-by-reachability on full re-index (drop keys not re-added) OR a small key->timestamp file. (Decide in m01.)

## Verification = results-equivalence
Captured baseline outputs (scores+snippets) + the n=52 eval are the golden reference. Exact brute-force + f32 => IDENTICAL ranked results old vs new. Latency alone is not pass/fail.
notes:
## Baseline Measurements (JSON-based, release build)

Cache: ~/Library/Caches/tldr/embeddings/cache.json = 1.1 GB, 117,641 entries

### Completed Tests

| Test | Command | Wall time | Internal latency_ms | Result |
|------|---------|-----------|---------------------|--------|
| 1. Fresh embed (cached) | `tldr embed config.rs` | 4.36s | 4,393ms | 28 chunks, all cached |
| 2. Cached embed | `tldr embed config.rs` | 4.36s | 4,315ms | 28 chunks, all cached |

Even for a CACHED 28-chunk file, embed takes 4.3s wall time. That's ~4.3s spent loading/parsing the 1.1GB JSON cache, NOT embedding. The actual search latency (795ms-1098ms) is on top of the cache parse.

title: Per-project config file (.tldr/config.json) for embedding model + settings
description:
Goal: let users change the embedding model (and future settings) per project WITHOUT recompiling. Today the model is hardcoded (default_value="arctic-m" in semantic.rs:36 / embed.rs; impl Default for EmbeddingModel). No config-file machinery exists in tldr-code (no toml dep, no loader, no app Config struct).

Design (settled):
- ONE JSON file per project: .tldr/config.json. Optional global ~/.tldr/config.json.
- Precedence (deep per-field merge): CLI flag > .tldr/config.json > ~/.tldr/config.json > built-in default. Missing file/field = built-in default = today's behavior.
- Tolerant parsing: serde(default) on everything, NO deny_unknown_fields — ignore unknown keys so newer configs don't break older binaries (forward-compat).
- Schema (single embedding block, provider-discriminated so cloud slots in with no restructure):
  { version:int=1,
    embedding: { provider:"local", model:"arctic-l", endpoint?:str, api_key_env?:str, dimensions?:int },
    semantic:  { enabled:bool=true, langs?:[str] } }
- Built-in default model stays arctic-m (conservative; small/fast). Config opts up to arctic-l etc.
- Note: the semantic EMBEDDING cache is GLOBAL (~/.tldr/embeddings/cache.json) keyed by abs file_path:function:hash:model — per-project model choices coexist safely. Structural Salsa cache is per-project (.tldr/cache).
- No JSON-Schema validation file; loader validates at runtime.

This feature umbrella tracks the sub-tasks.
close_reason: All sub-tasks complete: TldrConfig structs (qw2), config loader with precedence chain (hzv), and embedder wiring with provider seam (5xn). Per-project .tldr/config.json is now supported with global ~/.tldr/config.json fallback and deep merge. CLI flag > project config > global config > built-in default. Cloud provider fails fast with clear error.

title: Install tldr diagnostic tools for supported languages
description:
tldr-code has optional diagnostic tools (doctor, diagnostics) that require external language tools to be installed. Need to run 'tldr doctor --install <language>' for each supported language in the project.

**Problem**: The current install flow does NOT mention these optional tools anywhere. Users (and agents) have no visibility into these additional capabilities, so they never get installed or used. This means diagnostic features like 'tldr doctor' and language-specific analysis are silently unavailable.

**What needs to happen**:
1. Update the install flow/documentation to include an 'Optional Diagnostic Tools' step
2. Make it clear which tools are available per language and how to install them
3. Ensure agents and users discover these capabilities during setup

Languages and their tools:
- Python: pyright, ruff, mypy
- TypeScript: typescript-language-server, tsc
- Go: gopls, golangci-lint
- Rust: rustc, cargo
- Java: checkstyle, spotbugs

Install command: tldr doctor --install <language>

Steps:
1. Run 'tldr doctor' to check current state
2. Add optional tools section to the install flow
3. Install tools for languages used in this project (Rust is primary)
4. Verify installation with 'tldr doctor' again
notes: Discovered during session — the entire workflow (CLAUDE.md, setup docs, onboarding) is missing any mention of these optional diagnostic tools. This is a gap in discoverability, not just installation.
close_reason: Updated CLAUDE.md with build commands, diagnostic tools section (tldr doctor --install), architecture overview, and conventions. INSTALL.md already had the optional tools section; SETUP.md already mentions tldr doctor. The gap was agent instructions not surfacing these capabilities.

title: Make daemon reindex_triggered truthful and actionable
description: process_dirty_files sets reindex_triggered when dirty_count reaches auto_reindex_threshold, clears dirty_files, and returns true, but neither the watcher (which discards ReindexOutcome) nor IPC Notify schedules a full rebuild. notify.rs tells users 'Reindex triggered'. Either schedule the intended single-flight rebuild or retire/rename the legacy threshold contract so status cannot claim work happened when it did not.
acceptance_criteria: Crossing auto_reindex_threshold has one documented behavior shared by watcher and IPC Notify; if it means rebuild, exactly one single-flight rebuild is scheduled; otherwise response fields and CLI text no longer claim a rebuild. Add tests for both ingress paths at the threshold.

title: Eliminate the second semantic Tree-sitter parse
description: The artifact ingestion path parses every source into FileFacts and stores complete semantic source chunks, but structural plan_file later calls parse_with_path again because the persisted projection does not retain a reusable structural plan or syntax representation. The second parse is folded into semantic planning rather than separately timed. It is duplicate work and invalidates the stronger claim that each source is parsed only once, although it is not responsible for the inference bottleneck.
design: First add separate timing for the semantic planner parse. Then choose the smallest reusable representation: preferably persist the deterministic planner inputs/structural boundaries derived from the original tree rather than attempting to serialize Tree-sitter Tree objects. Do not couple this work to the comment-root fix and do not change embedding documents without explicit pipeline-version invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: Report first-pass and semantic-planner parse time separately; prove identical planned documents, identities and source coverage before/after on bulk and delta fixtures; remove the second parse from the normal artifact-backed path; retain a fallback for legacy/missing artifacts; and benchmark the actual wall-time saving before assigning further priority.

title: Audit durability-write serialization and pipeline overlap
description: The clean build spent 219.796s writing 400 durable cache windows. These writes provide proven restart safety, but transaction setup, serialization, metadata updates or synchronous ordering may be unnecessarily on the inference critical path. Determine whether the same per-window durability guarantee can be retained with fewer transactions, less repeated work, or safe overlap with the next inference batch.
acceptance_criteria: Break cache-write wall time into serialization, transaction/open, vector writes, metadata and flush/fsync where observable; identify repeated writes or lock contention; compare simple transaction batching or single-stage overlap designs; preserve the invariant that progress advances only after the completed window is durable; retain kill/restart contracts; and create a fix task only for a measured material improvement.

title: Trace repeated tokenization and preserve final encodings where worthwhile
description: Planning composes and token-checks candidate text multiple times, streaming checks completed documents again, and the fixed-shape adapter tokenizes final text for inference. Planning was only 167.487s, so an elaborate tokenizer cache is not justified without exact call and allocation evidence. Trace how many times each final document is encoded and evaluate whether directly carrying its final encoding removes meaningful work with a simple ownership model.
acceptance_criteria: Measure tokenizer calls, bytes/tokens processed and wall time by caller for representative and full retained workloads; distinguish necessary candidate checks from redundant final re-encoding; prototype or analytically validate the smallest carry-forward interface; state maximum and expected saving plus memory cost; and create a fix task only if the tradeoff is material.

title: Incomplete semantic generations lack a trustworthy postmortem manifest
description: The old incomplete generation required custom redb decoding and duplicated progress truth. The implemented design removes the need for a staged-generation postmortem manifest: compatible embedding cache records are authoritative, job identity/retry state is durable and advisory, live progress is exposed by daemon status, and opt-in raw unit JSONL plus the aggregate report records completed windows/phases for certification and postmortem analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Abnormal termination leaves compatible cache records reusable; restart reconciles exact cache hits/new vectors and invalidates incompatible jobs without retry cost; live status and retained metrics expose phase/window evidence; no duplicate staged-vector manifest or cross-store transaction is introduced.

title: Pre-existing failing test: test_bugbot_finds_real_bugs expects complexity-increase, gets cognitive-increase
description:
## Symptom

`cargo test -p tldr-cli test_bugbot_finds_real_bugs` fails:

  at crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/bugbot/check.rs:3890:
Expected complexity-increase finding. Got: ["cognitive-increase:process"]

The bugbot complexity analyzer emits a `cognitive-increase` finding where the test asserts a `complexity-increase` finding. title: Replace JSON embedding cache with efficient binary format to reduce memory pressure
description: Replace JSON embedding cache with compact binary format (rkyv) for storage efficiency. Initial implementation attempt identified critical issues: not actually zero-copy, alignment problems, unsafe migration. Revised approach: treat as compact binary persistence (not zero-copy), fix alignment/locking, safe migration (delete JSON after success), validate with actual benchmarks. Requires proper validation: compile, tests, Clippy, comparative benchmarks before completion.
notes:
## Current Implementation Problems

**Embedding Cache (cache.json):**
- Format: JSON 
- Write: serde_json::to_writer(writer, &self.entries) - serializes ENTIRE HashMap to JSON in memory
- Read: serde_json::from_reader(reader) - loads ENTIRE JSON file into memory as HashMap
- Location: ~/Library/Caches/tldr/embeddings/cache.json

**Memory Impact Analysis:**
- With 28,424 vectors × 384 dimensions × 4 bytes ≈ 43MB minimum for vectors
- JSON text encoding overhead: 2-3× larger than binary
- HashMap overhead for string keys
- Total estimated memory: 100-200MB+ fully loaded in memory

**The Core Problem:**
The JSON format forces:
1. Full file read into memory
2. Full deserialization into HashMap  
3. Full serialization when writing
4. All before any cache lookup can happen

## Code Evidence

**File:** crates/tldr-core/src/semantic/cache.rs
- Line 470: serde_json::to_writer(writer, &self.entries) - entire HashMap serialized
- Line 296-297: serde_json::from_reader(reader) - entire file loaded into HashMap

## Clarification: Cache Usage is Intentional (but Problematic)

**Current Design Intent:**
The duplication is actually **intentional** in the current architecture:

**When use_cache = true (normal operation):**
1. EmbeddingCache (JSON): Persistent cache to avoid expensive ONNX recomputation across different invocations
2. VectorStore (usearch): Efficient runtime index for semantic search operations

**When use_cache = false:**
- Vectors go directly to usearch without JSON storage
- No duplication, but full ONNX recomputation on every build

**The Trade-off:**
- **Benefit**: JSON cache avoids expensive ONNX recomputation (50-200ms per embedding)
- **Cost**: 100-200MB memory overhead + JSON serialization/deserialization

**Design Evolution:**
This appears to be an **evolutionary design choice**:
- Initially: Use JSON cache as simple persistent storage (easy to debug, portable)
- Recognition: JSON is inefficient for vectors (TLDR-AUDIT comment)
- Future direction: Move to usearch-only storage (TLDR-blm epic)

**Key Insight:**
The current design isn't necessarily "leftover from old design" but rather a **deliberate trade-off** that the team now recognizes as suboptimal. The JSON cache provides real value (avoiding recomputation) but uses the wrong format (JSON instead of binary) for the data type (dense float arrays).

**The TLDR-blm fix** represents the maturation of this design: keep the caching benefit but use the right storage format (usearch binary) for the right data type (vectors).

- **Solution**: rkyv has built-in ArchivedHashMap for zero-copy
- **Mistake**: Trying to use regular HashMap serialization
- **Fix**: Use rkyv's ArchivedHashMap directly

- **Mistake**: Generic blanket implementations causing confusing errors
- **Fix**: rkyv 0.8 removed problematic blanket impls

- LinkedIn Engineering case study: 85% cost reduction, 60% latency improvement
- L1: In-Memory LRU (~1ms) - Float32Array, 50% memory reduction
- L2: Redis Binary (~5ms) - Raw bytes, 60% storage savings, compression
- L3: PostgreSQL+pgvector (~20ms) - Persistent + similarity search
- Sources: 
  - https://redis.io/blog/machine-learning-inference-cost/
  - https://medium.com/@naeemulhaq/architecting-a-multi-tiered-caching-strategy-for-maximum-inference-cost-reduction-3fbbad4022f0

**Semantic Caching Best Practices (2026):**
- Frequency-based admission: only cache repeated patterns, avoid noise
- Model versioning: include Model ID in cache keys for rolling updates
- TTL tuning: critical for hit rates vs freshness balance
- Cache warming: prevent cold start problems
- Sources:
  - https://arxiv.org/html/2504.02268v1
  - https://machinelearningmastery.com/build-an-inference-cache-to-save-costs-in-high-traffic-llm-apps/

### **ONNX Runtime Optimization (2026)**

**Quantization Standards:**
- FP8 on Hopper/Blackwell GPUs (new standard)
- INT8 with AWQ/SmoothQuant for Ampere GPUs
- Dynamic quantization for varying input distributions
- Selective quantization (TuneQn) for optimal accuracy/performance
- Sources:
  - https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/performance/model-optimizations/quantization.html
  - https://apxml.com/courses/quantized-llm-deployment/chapter-4-optimizing-deploying-quantized-llms/deployment-onnx-runtime
  - https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12196v1

**Optimization Pipeline (2026):**
1. Export to ONNX format
2. Apply ONNX graph optimization (merge nodes, eliminate redundancies)
3. Quantize with advanced methods (GPTQ/AWQ for best accuracy)
4. Deploy with appropriate Execution Providers (TensorRT for GPU)
- Source: https://medium.com/@bhagyarana80/optimizing-transformer-inference-with-onnx-runtime-and-quantization-098f8149a15c

### **Semantic Search Architecture (2026)**

**Hybrid Search (Industry Standard):**
- Semantic vectors for intent and context
- Keyword search (BM25) for exact matches
- Reranking for precision
- Sources:
  - https://codelit.io/blog/ai-powered-search-architecture
  - https://www.algolia.com/blog/ai/ai-powered-search-architecture

**Chunking Best Practices:**
- 256-512 tokens per chunk
- 50-100 token overlap between chunks
- Function-level chunking for code
- Sources:
  - https://codelit.io/blog/ai-powered-search-architecture
  - https://sourcegraph.com/blog/semantic-code-search-what-it-is-and-how-it-works

### **Memory & Performance Techniques (2026)**

**PagedAttention (vLLM standard since 2023):**
- KV cache divided into fixed-size blocks
- Virtual-to-physical block mapping
- Near-zero memory waste (<4% vs 60-80%)
- 2-4x throughput improvement
- Sources:
  - https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/mastering-llm-techniques-inference-optimization/
  - https://budecosystem.com/whats-new-in-llm-inference-optimization-recent-advances-and-techniques/

**Memory Optimization:**
- FP8/INT8 quantization for 2x speed, 50% memory reduction
- Speculative decoding for 1.5-3x additional throughput
- Continuous batching for GPU utilization
- Source: https://futureagi.com/blog/llm-inference-human-prompts-2025/

### **Solo Mac Studio Development Assessment**

**Appropriate for Solo Development:**
- ✅ rkyv migration: Directly improves daily development experience
- ✅ Current architecture: Suitable for local Mac Studio use
- ✅ No GPU needed: Apple Silicon + ONNX Runtime sufficient
- ✅ Single-tier caching: Appropriate for solo use

**Enterprise Standards to Skip:**
- ❌ Dedicated vector databases (unnecessary complexity)
- ❌ GPU acceleration/quantization (not worth complexity for solo use)
- ❌ Multi-tier caching (Redis overkill for local development)
- ❌ Production observability (you're the only user)

**Focus Areas for Solo Development:**
- Fast incremental updates (rkyv helps here)
- Reasonable memory usage (Mac Studio has sufficient RAM)
- Good search quality (hybrid approach already good)
- Simple, maintainable code (avoid enterprise complexity)

### **Conclusion**

The industry standards researched target production systems at scale. For solo Mac Studio development, the current architecture with rkyv optimization is appropriate. Focus on developer experience improvements rather than enterprise infrastructure complexity.

cd <project>

title: MCP liveness test mutates TLDR_DAEMON_REGISTRY_DIR without ENV_LOCK mutex — flaky CI under parallel test runner
description:
crates/tldr-mcp/tests/mcp_liveness_poke_test.rs:57-59 does std::env::set_var("TLDR_DAEMON_REGISTRY_DIR", ...) / process_request / remove_var with NO synchronization. The analogous unit tests in tldr-core use a 'static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()>' (tldr-core/src/liveness.rs:124).

Integration tests in crates/tldr-mcp/tests/ compile into one binary and run in parallel threads. Other files there (mcp_camelcase_test, mcp_lifecycle_test, mcp_request_params_test) also call process_request, which fires poke_registered_daemons(). The window between set_var and remove_var races the global env with those tests -> nondeterministic registry path -> spurious recv_from failures or stale-socket reads. Test-only impact but real intermittent CI failures.
acceptance_criteria: Add 'static ENV_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()>' and hold _guard = ENV_LOCK.lock() across the set_var..remove_var block, matching tldr-core/src/liveness.rs:124. Test passes reliably under 'cargo test' default parallelism.
notes: Found by code-review fan-out 2026-06-17.
close_reason: Added 'static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()>' to mcp_liveness_poke_test.rs, held across set_var..process_request..remove_var, matching tldr-core/src/liveness.rs convention. NOTE: corrected the original severity — each tests/*.rs file compiles to a SEPARATE binary/process, so the cross-FILE race the review described cannot occur; with one test in this file there was no live race. The guard is future-proofing for added tests. Test passes.

title: FileIrMemo unbounded growth — deletes/renames/read-failures leave stale keys forever (no cap/TTL)
description:
The TLDR-iqr per-file memo FileIrMemo = DashMap<(String,PathBuf),(u64,Arc<FileIR>)> in crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/daemon/daemon.rs has no size cap, TTL, or scan-reconciliation. Two leak paths:

(1) UNNOTIFIED DELETE/RENAME (daemon.rs ~1534 process_dirty_file retain): if a file is deleted with no Notify (watcher disabled when 'semantic' feature off, or deleted before daemon start), scan_project_files stops enumerating it but its memo key is never evicted. Grows with file turnover over a long-running daemon.

(2) READ FAILURE (daemon.rs:152-170 build_project_call_graph_memoized): when std::fs::read fails, content_hash=None, the file is skipped and re-parse also yields nothing — but the prior memo entry is NOT removed. Not served (correct) but never evicted.
acceptance_criteria: Memo bounded. Fix (1): after scan_project_files, memo.retain(|k,_| scanned_set.contains(&k.1)) OR an LRU/size cap like QueryCache. Fix (2): memo.remove(&memo_key) in the content_hash.is_none() branch. Test: delete a file without Notify, rebuild, assert memo entry count drops.
notes:
Found by code-review fan-out 2026-06-17. MED — slow growth, not correctness.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.
close_reason: Fixed in build_project_call_graph_memoized (daemon.rs): (1) read-failure now memo.remove(&memo_key) in the content_hash None arm; (2) post-loop memo.retain(|k,_| k.0 != config.language || scanned_set.contains(&k.1)) prunes vanished files of the current language, leaving other-language entries intact. Memo now O(live files). Gates green.

title: Grammar pin upgrade policy — track upstream releases against the ABI matrix
description:
## Why
Epic finding D: exact pins (=0.23.6 etc.) with ABI rationale comments are the right discipline, but nothing tracks WHEN to move them. Upstream tree-sitter-python will ship official t-string support and future 3.15 syntax; staying frozen converts today's 'frontier resilience' into tomorrow's silent gap (the failure mode TLDR-6rt.5 makes visible).

## What
Lightweight policy doc + automation: (1) quarterly (or release-triggered) check of pinned grammar repos for new releases; (2) upgrade procedure = bump in a branch → run the frontier canary + ground-truth differential + ABI-compat build matrix → goldens diff review; (3) record each pin bump's verdict in the changelog. Optionally a CI cron that opens an issue when a pinned grammar falls >1 minor behind upstream.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Policy documented in repo; first execution dated; canary+differential wired as the upgrade gate (depends on siblings).
notes:
ENRICHMENT (2026-06-07): first execution is justified IMMEDIATELY — upstream tree-sitter-python v0.25.0 is out (releases page) and PR #368 adds PEP 750 t-string support absent from our 0.23.6 pin. Concrete first task when siblings land: bump python grammar 0.23.6 → latest (verify #368 inclusion + ABI vs tree-sitter core =0.25.0), gate on canary (t-string flips RECOVERED→PASS) + differential (95/95 corpus baseline holds).
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27: docs/GRAMMAR_COMPATIBILITY.md records exact pins, ABI discipline, frontier verdict semantics, pinned differential baseline, release gates, and rollback procedure. The Grammar assurance workflow enforces all three frontiers plus the Python corpus differential on relevant changes. Stale TLDR-lxc.2 parent blocker was repaired while preserving hierarchy.
close_reason: Grammar upgrade policy, release gates, CI automation, and rollback procedure are documented and enforced.

title: PEP 695 type aliases invisible — 'type X = ...' absent from extract/structure output
description:
## Why
Epic finding C (reproduced on tree-sitter-python 0.23.6): 'type SymbolList = list[str]' produces NO entry in extract/structure — not a function, not a class, simply absent. Type aliases are public API surface; consumers using structure for API extraction (tldr-audit-api skill, LLM onboarding packs) silently miss them. Same likely applies to TypeAlias-annotated assignments and possibly TS 'type' declarations (verify).

## What
1. Check the grammar exposes type_alias_statement nodes (it parsed without breaking siblings, so likely yes) and extraction simply ignores them.
2. Add 'type_alias' as a definition kind in structure/extract output (name, line, aliased-expression text).
3. Sweep other invisible definition kinds while there: module-level constants? TypedDict/Protocol classes are classes (fine) — enumerate and decide scope.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Probe file's 'type SymbolList = list[str]' appears as kind=type_alias with correct line; TS equivalent verified or follow-up filed; goldens updated.
notes: ENRICHMENT (2026-06-07): bug CONFIRMED as extraction-layer, not grammar — v0.23.6 node-types.json contains 'type_alias_statement' (and 'type_parameter'). The grammar parses 'type X = ...' fully; tldr extraction ignores the node. Implementation: handle node type 'type_alias_statement' (name = first child identifier; aliased expr = remainder). Step 1 of the task (check grammar) is DONE — skip straight to extraction wiring.
close_reason: Fixed: added try_type_alias_definition() in ast/extractor.rs collect_definitions — emits kind=type_alias for Python PEP 695 type_alias_statement (name = first identifier under the 'left' type node) AND TS/JS type_alias_declaration (name field). Additive to definitions[] — no schema change (kind is free-form String). VERIFIED: 2 new unit tests (python+TS) pass; ast::extractor 56/56, ast_tests 27, interface_multilang 13, alias_tests 78, CLI structure+extract green; end-to-end 'tldr structure' on 'type SymbolList = list[str]' now emits kind=type_alias at L1 with signature. TS equivalent verified (not just a follow-up). Constants already handled by try_constant_definition; TypedDict/Protocol are classes — scope satisfied.

title: ERROR-node visibility — surface tree-sitter parse degradation instead of silent partial extraction
description:
## Why
tree-sitter is error-TOLERANT by design: syntax beyond the pinned grammar produces ERROR nodes and parsing continues — extraction silently degrades rather than failing. Today no tldr output tells the user 'this file parsed with N error nodes; definitions may be missing.' On the Django corpus eval this never fired (95/95 files byte-identical to CPython ast; even PEP 695 + PEP 750 t-strings extracted cleanly on tree-sitter-python 0.23.6) — but the FAILURE MODE is invisible by construction, which is exactly when trust erodes: a future grammar/lang-version gap would look like 'tldr found fewer functions' with no signal.

## What
1. During extraction, count ERROR nodes per file (root.has_error / walk for ERROR kind).
2. Surface: per-file 'parse_errors: N' field in structure/extract JSON; non-zero triggers a stderr warning line; aggregate count in daemon stats.
3. Optional canary mode: 'tldr doctor --grammar-frontier <lang>' parses a bundled snippet-set of newest-syntax features and reports grammar coverage (the Django eval used exactly this technique: PEP695 generics + match + t-strings probe file).

## Evidence
Eval session 2026-06-07 (Stock-Monitor-Django corpus): tree-sitter-python 0.23.6 = 0 mismatches vs ast on 95 files AND survived the 3.14 frontier probe — record this as the baseline the warning protects.

## Acceptance Criteria
- parse_errors field present in structure/extract output; warning on stderr when >0; test with a deliberately-broken file + a beyond-grammar snippet; doctor canary optional follow-up.
notes:
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27: FileStructure and durable FileFacts now expose parse_errors (ERROR + missing recovery nodes), recovered files emit a stderr warning, daemon/cache artifact-store stats aggregate parse recovery nodes, and the FileFacts producer schema advanced to v5 across readers. Evidence: dedicated daemon aggregate unit test; certification parse_error_visibility; cargo fmt --check, warnings-denied workspace Clippy, all workspace targets, smoke 2/2, certification 11/11 all pass.
close_reason: Implemented parse-recovery visibility in structural output, durable artifacts, warnings, and daemon aggregate stats.

title: Django compat regression corpus — golden tests pinned to Stock-Monitor-Django ground truth
description:
## Why
The eval's value is reproducibility: every claim has a hand-verified ground truth in a real codebase. Without golden tests, the WORKS list in the epic (kind classification, ORM-chain tracking, decorator-registration suppression, dead precision) can silently regress while fixing the gap tasks.

## What
Add a compat-corpus test suite (vendored minimal extracts OR pinned-commit checkout of github.com/udhaya10/Stock-Monitor-Django) asserting golden outputs:

2. references SymbolMap → 42 refs incl. read-kind hits through .objects chains (stocks/tasks/dhan.py:306 etc.).
3. dead → _to_float + _calculate_q4fy26_earnings_metric in dead_functions; NSEProvider.fetch_corporate_results/fetch_earnings_calendar in possibly_dead; handle/ready/get_queryset/__str__/task impls ABSENT.
4. (after sibling fixes) build_console_formatter absent; sweep_intraday_bars cross-file edge present; impact depth-2 works.

## Acceptance Criteria

notes:

IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27: Added scripts/django_compat_corpus.py and a path-filtered Django compatibility GitHub Actions job. The adapter hard-fails unless Stock-Monitor-Django is exactly at 1e56243d5258e0b310a45ca3cfae60c455328b76, then asserts exact upsert reference kinds/sites, 106 SymbolMap refs plus ORM read sites, the settings string-ref, known dead/live/preset behavior, three local-import edges, and depth-two impact callers. title: Framework-callback suppression inconsistency: Command.add_arguments flagged while handle/get_queryset/ready are not
description:
## Why
Corpus eval: dead's framework awareness correctly suppressed handle, ready, get_queryset, __str__, ViewSet methods — but Command.add_arguments landed in possibly_dead. Both handle and add_arguments are django BaseCommand overrides called only by the framework; the asymmetry suggests the suppression mechanism (inheritance-awareness? name whitelist?) has a gap rather than a principled rule.

## What
1. Diagnose WHY handle escapes but add_arguments doesn't (read the suppression path; is there a hardcoded name list? does inheritance detection see BaseCommand?).
2. Fix the general mechanism (prefer base-class-override detection: any method overriding a symbol from an external/non-indexed base is framework-called) OR extend the curated list.
3. Ship a '--entry-points django' PRESET (add_arguments, handle, ready, get_queryset, get_serializer_class, has_permission, signal receivers, Meta...) so Django users get clean dead output without hand-rolled whitelists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Corpus: add_arguments not flagged; root cause documented in close reason; django preset documented + tested.
notes:
PRIOR-ART ENRICHMENT (2026-06-07, firecrawl): vulture (the incumbent Python dead-code tool) handles Django FPs via ignore_decorators / ignore_names / whitelist .py files — purely manual, per-project (see adamj.eu 'Django: Clean up unused code with Vulture' 2023 + github.com/jendrikseipp/vulture#handling-false-positives). Design takeaway for the --entry-points django preset: ship vulture's known Django whitelist surface as the starting list (Meta, get_queryset, has_permission, Command.handle/add_arguments, AppConfig.ready, signal receivers, admin.register targets) — but prefer base-class-override DETECTION over name lists where possible; that's the differentiator vulture lacks.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27: Root cause is name-convention asymmetry in analysis/dead.rs: the generic hardcoded prefix rule suppresses handle* while add_arguments has no equivalent rule; the pinned corpus now also has enough same-named add_arguments definitions for refcount collision to mask the original symptom. Added opt-in --entry-points django expansion at the CLI routing boundary, composing with explicit patterns and therefore behaving identically in oneshot and daemon paths. Preset covers Command/AppConfig, queryset, serializer, permission, form/view/admin, and middleware override hooks; decorated signals/admin/tasks remain covered by existing decorator suppression, and Meta is not a function candidate. Synthetic regression proves baseline add_arguments candidate, preset suppression, and explicit-pattern composition. Current pinned corpus proves LegacyApiPermission.has_permission is removed only with the preset. Documented in command guide. Gates: 2 dead tests, corpus before/after, fmt, warnings-denied Clippy.
close_reason: The asymmetry was a hardcoded handle* convention; the documented Django preset now covers non-call-visible overrides while composing with custom entry points.

title: smells: DataClumps silently unimplemented (zero findings always); FeatureEnvy without --deep runs empty stub silently
description: Found during TLDR-uiy audit 12/64 (Codex-assisted, core-side verified). (1) DataClumps: SmellType::DataClumps is user-reachable via --smell-type data-clumps and listed in should_run_original_detectors (tldr-core/src/quality/smells.rs:2767), but NO detect_data_clumps_* implementation exists anywhere in the pipeline (collect_tier1_ast_smells lines 761-818 never calls one) -> always zero findings, silently. title: Daemon-vs-local divergence CLASS: dead/weaker/unfiltered daemon answers across commands (calls, impact, ...; audit-driven checklist)
description:
Found during TLDR-uiy audit 3/64 (2026-06-05), Codex-assisted, code-verified. THREE defects, one path:
A) DEAD DAEMON PATH: DaemonCommand::Calls (tldr-cli/src/commands/daemon/daemon.rs ~888) returns serde_json::to_value(ProjectCallGraph) = {"edges":[{src_file,src_func,dst_file,dst_func}]}. CLI (calls.rs:114) deserializes try_daemon_route::<CallGraphOutput> which REQUIRES root/total_edges/shown_edges + call_type per edge -> from_value fails -> .ok() -> None -> SILENT LOCAL FALLBACK EVERY TIME. The '~35x speedup' comment in calls.rs is false. Daemon route for calls has likely never worked since the schemas diverged.
B) V1-vs-V2 ORACLE SPLIT: daemon builds build_project_call_graph (V1); CLI local fallback builds build_project_call_graph_v2. Two different graph builders serve 'the same' command.
C) UNREADABLE WARM CACHE: warm step 1 (daemon.rs ~134, WarmJob) caches the V1 ProjectCallGraph under QueryKey 'calls' — an answer shape no CLI consumer can deserialize. We warm a cache nobody can read.
RESOLUTION: closed by the TLDR-n74 rewrite (CSR snapshot + bincode envelope + flag-parity); no interim patch (user-ratified — effort on a path scheduled for replacement). This bug is the ADR-10 EXHIBIT: silent fallback masked a permanently-dead path.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): The legacy implementation path is absorbed by TLDR-eda5 and the one-shot shared redb ArtifactStore plan. The underlying user-visible requirement is preserved in that plan; this issue is superseded as an implementation vehicle, not erased as historical evidence.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: EXTENDED TO CLASS ISSUE (user-ratified, audit 4/64). (a) WRONG DIRECTION: router forwards file/function/line only (slice.rs:141-145); DaemonCommand::Slice has no direction/variable fields (types.rs:437-442); daemon arm HARDCODES SliceDirection::Backward + variable=None (daemon.rs:845-876) -> 'tldr slice -d forward' with live daemon returns a BACKWARD slice; header prints the daemon's 'backward' label, silently substituting the request. title: Token-lean -f compact rendering for graph answers — the primary agent surface (ADR-11)
description: Implemented compact-v1 token-lean edge rendering for calls, impact, dead, hubs, and structure. The format is versioned escaped TSV with deterministic target ordering, shared path-prefix compression, typed rows, and metadata retaining complete-analysis counts. Added six golden/contract tests, agent-facing documentation, and README recommendation. Real cl100k_base measurements on this repository: calls 155430→7771 (20.00x), impact 1255→572 (2.19x), dead 30351→8416 (3.61x), hubs 9315→2225 (4.19x), structure 161449→74675 (2.16x). notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.

title: Resident CSR snapshot + query primitives; retire whole-project answer blobs from the hot path
description: Implements ADR-9's structure: intern table, SoA node table, forward+reverse CSR, name/file/line indexes, ArcSwap snapshot. Wire the seven query primitives (out/in-neighbors, reverse BFS closure, predicate scans, SCC, by-name, by-file/line) and route callers/callees/impact/dead/hubs/cycles/definition/structure through the snapshot, returning SMALL per-answer serializations at the socket boundary. Whole-project JSON results survive only at persist (query_cache.bin) and explicit-export boundaries. Complexity contract per ADR-9 is the review rubric. MEASURED WARNING from the design session: the 10-30MB whole-project JSON serialization (50-150ms) would be the next hot path after A+B — its removal is the point. ACCEPTANCE: per-command output identical for the same queries (CLI-level golden diffs); query latencies recorded; snapshot rebuild time recorded (target single-digit ms at 26k edges).
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Partially absorbed and linked to TLDR-eda5. Shared persistence/generation/invalidation concerns move into the new ArtifactStore, while the issue’s distinct algorithm, quality, memory, serving, or evaluation work remains valid.

comments.text:
SPEC ADDITION (2026-06-06, user-ratified; Codex-reviewed on TLDR-5qm): CONTENT-ADDRESSED CACHE SEGMENT MODEL — the cross-command caching contract (goals: warm once / reuse across CLI flows; single-file edit invalidates the minimal segment).
UNIFYING RULE: every cached artifact declares its exact input slice; key = blake3 of that slice + (schema, analyzer, grammar) versions; invalidation = key mismatch, NEVER explicit flush.
S1 parse: (file content hash, grammar ver) -> tree.
S2 per-FUNCTION facts: key=(body hash, FILE SEMANTIC-ENV HASH [imports + enclosing-class chain], lang, analyzer ver) -> CFG/DFG/SSA bundle (POSITION-RELATIVE storage; identity + absolute position live ONLY in the generation node table), metric row, token fingerprint, embedding. Body edits keep sibling functions warm (49/50 property); import edits invalidate the file honestly; NO identity inside cached values (Codex F1).
S3 compose-inputs per file: the CLOSED SET of what compose consumes — signatures, call-sites, imports, AND receiver-index/local-type facts. Codex F5 confirms the ADR-9 'fold receiver indexes into FileIR' move is LOAD-BEARING: today's compose (apply_type_resolution, receiver indexes) scans raw source. Each sub-fact independently hashed.
S4 CSR snapshot: O(V+E) rebuild on any compose-input change (rebuild-don't-surgery stands). FuncId assignment DETERMINISTIC FROM IDENTITY ORDERING (file, qualified name, ordinal) — never from positions.
S5 derived artifacts (pagerank/betweenness/SCC/cycles/layers <- topology slice = identity table + CSR bytes, positions EXCLUDED; coupling/cohesion <- module-edge hash; inheritance closure <- type-edge hash; clones <- fingerprint multiset, incremental re-compare; health/debt aggregates <- monoid fold over S2 rows): slice hashes are REUSE TICKETS, but lookup ALWAYS goes through a PINNED GENERATION — generation = consistency token (epoch mixing unexpressible, Codex F4), slice hash = reuse ticket (body-only edits keep pagerank warm across rebuilds). REPLACES 'first query per generation pays' with 'first query per input-slice-change pays'.
S6 search: BM25 per-file delta postings + S2 embeddings, content-keyed.
S7 external truth: (git HEAD, tool versions, coverage hash) keys, local-only, never daemon-resident.
T3: S2 persists as an on-disk content-addressed store -> warm restarts. GC = mark-and-sweep from the current file set (live = body hashes referenced by current parses); RAM tier = per-segment byte-budget LRU (CAS + LRU alone grows forever, Codex F6).
ARBITRATION: Codex's secondary equality check on slice-hash reuse DROPPED (user-ratified) — blake3-256 collision risk negligible; the rec targeted weak/rolling hashes.
MEASUREMENT: edit-path hash fan-out added to the TLDR-rfz gate (Codex F7).
RETIRES/REUSES (Codex F8): daemon per-language OnceCell buckets retire (with Am.2 language-unified); S2 persistence reuses the VectorStore content-keyed pattern; embeddings already content-keyed (t8f).
BONUS: makes the TLDR-jsi bug class unexpressible — cache clear = drop CAS; content-addressed keys cannot serve stale-wrong data.

comments.text:
LAYER TAXONOMY AMENDMENTS (2026-06-06, post-Codex review on TLDR-5qm; supplements the taxonomy comment above):
A1 (F4): L2 grains NAMED — L2a function-grain (S2: bundles, metric rows, fingerprints; key body+env hash) and L2b file-grain (S3: compose-input facts; key file hash). ONE layer, two grains. RULE CLARIFIED: layer membership = key/lifetime class (content-derived, project-blind), NOT downstream effect.
A2 (F5): EMBEDDINGS move to L2-ASYNC sub-lane — same content-addressed keys + MODEL-VERSION key dimension, but refresh is DECOUPLED from the synchronous edit path (ONNX inference ~100ms+/function must never block structural-fact freshness or queries). Queries serve last-good embedding WITH staleness provenance. Aligns with the resident-Embedder IndexManager design already in-tree.
A3 (F6a): whole-project aggregates (health/debt/project-stats) are NOT L4 reuse-ticket artifacts — any edit changes their slice and hashing the fold input is itself O(V). They are recomputed per generation as an O(V) monoid fold over warm L2a metric rows (us-ms at 20k functions). L4 tickets apply only to artifacts whose slice can survive edits (topology/module-edge/type-edge/fingerprint-multiset keyed).
A4 (F6b): the EXISTING QueryCache (tldr-cli/src/commands/daemon/salsa.rs) is hereby assigned a fate: RETIRED. It memoizes materialized answers — the answer-blob sin ADR-9 kills. Its consumers route to L3/L4. No taxonomy slot for it is added; its absence from the layer stack is a decision, not an omission.
A5 (F1): B2 RESTATED honestly — edit above a function: zero invalidation; edit inside a body: that one function's L2a facts recompute (cheap) + async embedding refresh (A2); NO L3 rebuild (compose-input hashes unchanged). Comment-stripped normalized body hashing PARKED as a future measured lever (complicates position-correct rendering).
A6 (F2): B1 scoped — the ~3s blunt-clear repayment claim applies to the GRAPH path (DaemonState language buckets); the semantic vector store already has per-file delta warmth (t8f) which the model formalizes rather than introduces.
A7 (F7): side lane reworded — external-truth ANSWERS (git HEAD/tool/env-scoped: churn, diagnostics, coverage, doctor, fix) are never served from daemon caches; daemon operational state (counters, liveness) is outside taxonomy scope.
REAFFIRMED AGAINST CODEX (F3 rejected with evidence): B3 STANDS — the real public search path builds BM25 inline per invocation (enriched.rs:925,986 Bm25Index::from_project) AND builds the full call graph per invocation (enriched.rs:1593); CLI search has no daemon routing; in-repo test comment (enriched.rs:2214) confirms 'from_project() rebuilds every time'. Codex cited the UNWIRED tldr-daemon axum crate — the two-daemons trap, THIRD STRIKE. The host-decision-first rule in this spec exists for exactly this reason.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
AMENDMENTS A8-A11 (2026-06-06, Codex rounds 2+3 on TLDR-5qm, full convergence; user-directed course-correction loop):
A8 ASYNC-EMBEDDING CONSISTENCY CONTRACT: semantic/search results from the L2-async embedding lane are JOIN-VERIFIED against the pinned generation before rendering — hits whose function key is absent from the current node table are DROPPED; positions rebased from the node table; the response carries an embedding-staleness field (embedding-lane generation vs snapshot generation). Guarantee: stale embeddings may mis-rank, can NEVER surface deleted/renamed symbols.
A9 ENV-HASH SCOPE: the L2a file semantic-env hash covers DIRECT imports of the file + the enclosing-class chain ONLY — never transitive module metadata. Transitive effects flow through compose/L3, not L2 keys. Blast-radius measurement added to TLDR-rfz (what fraction of real edits touch import lists; functions churned per such edit).
A10 L4 TICKET GRANULARITY: ship the 4 coarse slices (topology / module-edge / type-edge / fingerprint-multiset); refine granularity from post-implementation hit-rate telemetry, never speculation.
A11 CLOSABILITY = CAPTURE, NOT SOLUTION (round-3 convergence): the L2b closed compose-input set captures exactly the inputs today's resolver reads — Codex-verified per-file-only (resolution.rs L258-301; type_resolver.rs L426-612 Python, L828-1005 TS; no cross-file/global inputs). The frozen-corpus byte-hash gates are the MECHANICAL CLOSURE PROOF: under-capture diverges output and fails the gate. Existing fallback/widening (unresolved-receiver) semantics are DOCUMENTED in the spec, preserved byte-identically — not redesigned.
F3 CLOSURE: Codex round-2 CONCEDED B3 after reading the real path (search.rs no daemon hop; from_project inline x2; build_project_call_graph per invocation). Trap strike 3 confirmed by the reviewer itself; host-decision-first rule re-validated.
ROUND-3 VERDICT (Codex): research plan COMPLETE pending the measurement gate only.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
TWO-FLOW OVERLAP MAP (2026-06-06, recorded because the question recurs; code-verified): Flow 1 (structural: parse->FileIR->compose->CSR) and Flow 2 (semantic: chunk->enrich->embed->vector store) SHARE their foundation and today PAY IT TWICE.
CODE FACTS: (1) Flow 2's chunker parses with the SAME tree-sitter entry as Flow 1 (chunker.rs:222 parse_file from ast::parser) — every file parsed twice today. (2) Flow 2 CONSUMES Flow 1 outputs: embedding text includes signature+callees (enrichment EmbeddingUnit); enriched search builds the full call graph per query for context cards (the B3 kill).
SHARED STAGES (optimizing helps BOTH): file enumeration + ignore rules (today two divergent walkers — bpf cluster); tree-sitter parse (L1, biggest shared win); function identity/spans/content-hash (today FuncDef+blake3-target vs ChunkMeta+MD5 — unify); per-function fact registry (L2: CFG bundles + metric rows + fingerprints + BM25 docs + embeddings on ONE (body hash, env hash) key — a 'chunk' IS a function); watcher + delta invalidation (one trigger pipeline).
EXCLUSIVE STAGES (optimizing helps ONE lane): CSR + graph walks = Flow 1 only; ONNX inference + vector index = Flow 2 only (e.g. 3rh arena tuning protects shared daemon headroom but does not speed Flow 1).
DIRECTION OF BENEFIT: Flow 1 substrate -> Flow 2 queries (resident snapshot turns per-query graph builds into O(deg); shared L1 halves Flow-2 indexing). Flow 2 -> Flow 1 = PATTERNS not speed (t8f delta machinery, IndexManager resident-store/RwLock, VectorStore CAS pattern reused by T3/mtq). Flow 2 pioneered; Flow 1 industrializes.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MODEL: after n74/17d the 'two flows' become TWO LANES ABOVE ONE SHARED L0-L2 FOUNDATION, diverging only at L3 (CSR vs vector index). 'Will building Flow 2 make Flow 1 faster?' — NO, the arrow points the other way; 'does AST/chunk-index help both?' — YES, they ARE the shared layers.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: A12 (2026-06-06, user-ratified): EMBEDDING KEY IS BODY-LOCAL — key = (body hash, signature hash, model ver). Resolved-callee context is NEVER baked into embedding text; structural context (callers/callees) joins AT QUERY TIME from the pinned generation (O(deg) from L3) and fuses via RRF with dense + BM25 signals (rides utj.3). SUPERSEDES the earlier enrichment-slice-hash note: that note correctly identified the staleness hazard but solved it in the wrong direction (honest key over volatile inputs -> frequent invalidation); A12 removes the volatile input from the artifact instead. CONSEQUENCES: (1) a callee rename re-embeds ZERO functions — only a function's own body edit re-embeds it; (2) query-time context is FRESHER than baked-in (current at query moment vs stale-between-re-embeds); (3) deployed baseline already runs enrich OFF (memory 00) so this costs nothing today; (4) GATE: any future baked-in enrichment proposal must BEAT query-time fusion in the eval harness before earning a place in the embedding key. Design principle extracted: never bake volatile cross-file data into the most expensive immutable artifact — serve volatility from the always-fresh cheap structure.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: REJECTED ALTERNATIVE recorded (2026-06-06, user-proposed for due diligence, jointly rejected): REIFIED CACHE-KEY DEPENDENCY GRAPH (Salsa/Bazel/Incremental-style stored edges + push invalidation). Rejected for THIS system's shape: (1) derivation DAG is STATIC and shallow (L1->L2->L3->L4, ~10 edge types known at design time) — storing per-key edge instances records what we already know; (2) A12 deleted the only volatile many-to-many edge (embedding<-resolved-callees) — remaining edges are 1:1 (function->own facts), one flat index (file->function keys), or N:1 (->snapshot, rebuilt wholesale per ADR-9 rebuild-don't-surgery); (3) stored edges are mutable state with their own staleness — a missed edge update = silently-wrong hit, re-importing the bug class content-addressing makes unexpressible (the retired QueryCache.invalidate_by_input was a crude instance). WHAT SURVIVES of the idea: file->function-keys index (async embed queue + GC mark phase) and the pinned generation as the single L3/L4 consistency edge. REVISIT TRIGGER: if the derivation DAG ever becomes DYNAMIC (analyses reading arbitrary other functions' facts at runtime), recorded dependencies become correct — record this as the explicit condition, not dogma.

title: Python/TS/generic resolvers: same per-call-site-scan defect class as Gate-1 rounds 1-5 (unmeasured; ADR-6 decision input)
description:
The Gate-1 campaign (compose 223s -> 0.56s on rust) fixed SEVEN defects of one class: per-call-site linear work that should be indexed lookups. The rust fixes were: find_by_name secondary index, RustReceiverIndex (per-file binding/impl index, then fully inverted incl. weird receivers), find_by_name routing in resolve_local_fuzzy_match / resolve_type_aware_fallback.

The NON-rust paths still run the legacy shape: resolve_receiver_type (resolution.rs) dispatches per call site to per-language scanners (python/TS/JS/Go/Java/... in type_resolver.rs) that re-scan source text per call — the exact pattern rounds 2-4 killed for rust. Generic paths fixed in round 5 (local_fuzzy/type_aware_fallback) already benefit all languages.

SCOPE: (1) MEASURE first (ADR-3 rule — no fixing before profiling): TLDR_PHASE_TIMING=1 build on a large python and a large TS corpus; (2) if compose dominates, apply the inverted-index treatment per language with the same layered differential gates (ADR-5: exhaustive synthetic + corpus-level value identity + count identity + determinism).

WHY IT MATTERS: one of exactly two missing inputs to the Path A/B call in ADR-6 (TLDR-7mp) — per-language compose economics may differ materially from rust's.

title: ADR-7: Memory attribution correction — headline peak is EMBED phase; chunk store does not address it
description:
## Decision
(2026-06-05) Stop justifying the chunk store with the headline memory number. The measured 27.0GB peak belongs to the EMBED phase (Flow-2: ONNX inference + accumulate-then-save). Memory work routes accordingly: TLDR-3rh/TLDR-yll own the embed peak; the F-series surgical fixes (F1/TLDR-9ae shipped; F2-F4/TLDR-1in pending) own the callgraph-phase transient.

## Rationale (correction owned)
We carried "the 22GB is the callgraph cache; the chunk store kills it" forward in the benefits statement. Our own measurements say otherwise:
- The callgraph-phase plateau was 11.4GB PRE-F1 (with the to_value DOM); F1 is shipped and the post-F1 number is unmeasured.
- The true daemon peak = max(phase peaks) = the EMBED phase, untouched by any chunk-store design.
- 27.0GB vs the historical 22.7GB is partly BETTER MEASUREMENT, not worse behavior: 27.0 came from the getrusage high-water probe (true max over 4.5h), 22.7 from 15s ps polling (under-samples peaks by construction). Provenance: the overnight diff touched only callgraph/* — semantic/ ran byte-identical to main.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep quoting the headline number for the chunk store: rejected — it assigns another subsystem's peak to this design and would make Path B look better than it is.

## Status: ACTIVE.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Partially absorbed and linked to TLDR-eda5. Shared persistence/generation/invalidation concerns move into the new ArtifactStore, while the issue’s distinct algorithm, quality, memory, serving, or evaluation work remains valid.
close_reason: Memory-attribution decision confirmed by the structural embedding benchmark and final 82.34% RSS reduction.
