title: ADR-6: Gate-1 PASS — recompose-always stands; chunk-store time case reduced to ~2.7s; Path A/B deferred to two measurements
description:
## Decision
(2026-06-05, supersedes ADR-1's justification) Gate-1 PASSES: compose = 0.56s, under the 2s recompose-per-edit line with margin. Recompose-always v1 stands AS DESIGNED — no escalation needed. HOWEVER the chunk store's TIME justification is re-derived honestly: a full rebuild is now ~3.1s (parse 2.7s + compose 0.56s), so chunk persistence buys ONLY the ~2.7s parse memoization. The Path A (surgical fixes, no storage layer) vs Path B (full two-flow chunk store) decision is DEFERRED until two missing measurements exist:
1. Post-F1 warm memory peak (callgraph-phase transient after the to_value DOM removal) — ~22s measurement, needs daemon authorization.
2. Python/TS resolver compose numbers — same per-call-site-scan defect class, unmeasured; per-language economics may differ materially.

## Rationale
The problem ADR-1 designed for (220s+ rebuilds, minutes-long restarts) largely DISSOLVED under measurement and defect fixes. What Path B uniquely retains regardless: cross-process/CI chunk sharing (~parse only), mmap-evictable steady state, restart without parse. Whether that justifies weeks of storage work is a memory question now, not a time question.

## Alternatives Considered
- Proceed with Path B on the original benefits table: rejected — the table conflated defect costs with design value ("restart 3.5min -> seconds" was mostly the defects).
- Kill Path B now: rejected — memory + multi-language numbers could still justify it; deferring costs nothing.

## Status: ACTIVE — the current architectural position.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.

title: ADR-5: Output-identity discipline — perf fixes proven by layered differential gates, never by 'tests pass'
description:
## Decision
(overnight 2026-06-05, formalized in round 5) Every performance fix to resolution logic must be OUTPUT-IDENTICAL and PROVEN so, by layered gates: (1) exhaustive synthetic differential vs the legacy implementation, (2) frozen-corpus count identity (745/20,320/26,312 across all rounds), (3) corpus-level VALUE identity on real call-site receivers (round-5 closer, advisor-prompted: counts cannot catch same-count-different-target divergence), (4) run-to-run determinism of the full 8.4MB edge output.

## Rationale
A 400x speedup that silently changes which edges resolve is a correctness regression wearing a perf medal. The legacy implementation stays in-tree as the reference oracle.

## Alternatives Considered
- "Counts match + suite green" alone: rejected after advisor review — it leaves exactly one divergence mode open (same count, different resolved type).

## Bonus outcome
The discipline also REMOVED pre-existing nondeterminism: the old fuzzy-match paths picked among candidates in HashMap iteration order (random per process); the indexed rewrite is deterministic (TLDR-2af direction).

## Status: ACTIVE.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.

title: ADR-4: Treat Gate-1 FAIL (223s) as suspected algorithmic defect — profile/fix loop before architecture escalation
description:
## Decision
(2026-06-04 night) On Gate-1 failing at compose=223s (110x over the 2s line), do NOT escalate to heavier architecture (query-time resolution / incremental compose / Glean-style ownership sets). Instead run profile -> name hot path -> output-identical fix -> differential gate -> re-bench loops on the EXISTING pipeline.

## Rationale
223s / 26,312 edges = ~8.5ms per edge — pathological vs comparable tools (ty type-checks all of home-assistant in 5.3s; rust-analyzer resolves workspaces in seconds). That smelled like implementation defects, not inherent cost. Profiling is cheap; escalation stays available if fixes stall.

## Alternatives Considered
- Escalate immediately per the pre-planned ladder: rejected — would have built complex machinery on top of unmeasured defects, repeating ADR-1's mistake at a higher level.

## Outcome (VINDICATED — 400x)
5 rounds, 7 defects, ALL the same class (per-call-site linear scans that should be indexed lookups; all present since initial release): compose 223s -> 0.56s; build 226s -> 3.1s. Gate-1 PASSED with the original architecture intact — the escalation ladder was never needed.

## Method lessons baked in (mistakes owned)
- Round 1 fixed a REAL defect (find_by_name linear scan) and got ZERO speedup — it was not the dominant branch. Lesson: sum ALL profile branches before fixing; do not fix the first named function.
- Round 2's own fix (the receiver index) became round 5's hot path. Lesson: re-profile your own fixes; an index that replaces a scan can hide a smaller scan inside itself.

## Status: ACTIVE — standing method for perf campaigns on this codebase.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.

title: ADR-3: No status above PROPOSED until viability gates are MEASURED; no storage code before Gate-0/1
description:
## Decision
(2026-06-04 evening, supersedes ADR-2's lock) Process rule: architecture decisions stay PROPOSED-PENDING-GATE until their kill-gates are measured on the real pipeline. Concretely: no storage code before Gate-0 (FileIR purity) and Gate-1 (compose cost <=2s). Compose model corrected to LAZY (on-query-after-dirty) in the same review.

## Rationale
A gate that can kill the design must run before anything is "locked". Adversarial self-review called the prior locking "manufactured false certainty"; the advisor independently re-classified Gate-1 from open-question to approval-blocker.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep LOCKED, treat Gate-1 as a formality: rejected — that is how weeks get spent building a cache for the cheap step.

## Outcome (VINDICATED — this rule did the work)
Gate-1 ran the same evening and FAILED 110x over the line: the unmeasured premise (parse expensive / compose cheap) was exactly backwards. Zero storage code had been written. The entire cost of the wrong assumption was one evening of measurement instead of weeks of building.

## Status: ACTIVE — this is now the standing rule for TLDR-zde and successor designs.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.

title: ADR-2: Mark architecture LOCKED before running Gate-1 (process mistake, owned)
description:
## Decision
(2026-06-04 afternoon) Mark the chunk-store architecture choices — two-flow constraint, rkyv chunks, CSR+fst layout, lifecycle, integrity scheme — as LOCKED while Gate-1 (the compose-cost bench) was still UNRUN.

## Rationale (at the time)
Choices were user-confirmed and research-double-confirmed (incl. a counter-evidence pass); locking was meant to stop re-litigating settled questions.

## Why this was a mistake (owned)
Gate-1 decided whether the recompose-based design was viable AT ALL — it was an approval blocker mislabeled as an open question. Locking around an unrun measurement manufactured false certainty. This is the central PROCESS error of the campaign: certainty was assigned by research consensus, not by measurement.

## How it was caught
Adversarial self-review + advisor, the same day, BEFORE the bench ran: "downgrade all LOCKED items to PROPOSED-PENDING-GATE-1". Hours later Gate-1 failed 110x over the pass line, proving the downgrade right.

## Lesson
Research can validate that a library is healthy; only measurement can validate that a design premise is true. Lock nothing upstream of an unrun kill-gate.

title: ADR-1: Chunk-store design premised on 'parse expensive, compose cheap' (unmeasured)
description:
## Decision
(2026-06-04, original TLDR-zde design) Build a disk-backed, per-file chunk-invalidated analysis cache: persist each file's parse output (FileIR) keyed by content hash; on edit, re-parse ONE chunk and re-run global compose; restart loads chunks via mmap in seconds.

## Rationale (as believed at the time — the core ASSUMPTION, never measured)
- Parse/extract was assumed to be the expensive, memoizable step; global compose assumed to be a small fraction of build cost ("expected: small fraction of parse cost, but verify" — the 'verify' is what saved us).
- Whole-project in-RAM JSON blobs caused 22GB build peaks, full recompute on any edit, 3.5min daemon restarts; per-file chunks fix the granularity mismatch.

## Alternatives Considered
- Redis-class KV, Arrow hot path, graph DBs, heap petgraph, adjacency matrices, JSON-as-storage, salsa crate v1, stack-graphs crate — all rejected in the research round (see TLDR-zde design notes + research annex).

## What happened (transparency record)
- Gate-1 (2026-06-04 evening) measured the premise INVERTED: parse 2.8s, compose 223s = 98.8% of build. Memoizing parse saves ~1% of build time.
- The 223s was then proven to be SEVEN implementation defects, not inherent cost (rounds 1-5 overnight+morning: compose 223s -> 0.56s, output-identical, all defects dated to initial release).
- The architecture itself survived (Gate-1 ultimately PASSED at 0.56s) but this decision's TIME justification collapsed to ~2.7s parse memoization on a 3.1s rebuild.

## Lesson
We designed a cache for the step we assumed was expensive. Measurement showed we had it exactly backwards — and that the expensive step was only expensive because it was buggy.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Linked to TLDR-eda5 as completed historical evidence or a shipped foundation. Closure is preserved; the new design may replace its implementation path but does not rewrite the fact, measurement, decision, or requirement established here.

title: Onboarding: one-command install + auto MCP/hook registration per agent
description:
From GrapeRoot competitive analysis (TLDR-2o4), finding #5.

PROBLEM: GrapeRoot is one curl install then 'dgc .' — auto-writes .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, opencode.json, Claude settings hooks for six agents. tldr needs a Rust toolchain or release binary, manual MCP registration per agent, tldr doctor for language tools. Time-to-first-value gap is large for non-expert users.

PROPOSAL (incremental, no auto-update-from-CDN — that's their supply-chain liability, not a feature to copy):
- install script for release binaries (checksummed, pinned versions)
- 'tldr setup --claude|--cursor|--codex|...' writes the right MCP config/hook entries idempotently
- 'tldr setup' with no args detects which agents are installed and offers each
- fold doctor checks into the setup flow output
notes:
## Split (2026-07-18)

PROJECT lifecycle (daemon/LaunchAgent/warm) is DONE via TLDR-pcm:
  tldr init / tldr init --remove

This issue remains ONLY for AGENT harness wiring (GrapeRoot gap #5 remainder):
  tldr setup claude|cursor|codex|...  (like bd setup claude)
  optional: detect installed agents, MCP/hook files, fold doctor output

Do NOT re-implement daemon autostart here — that is tldr init.
Implemented tldr setup [claude|cursor|codex|all] with installed-agent detection when omitted, idempotent merge/removal, MCP registration, Claude/Codex lifecycle hooks, binary availability output, and tldr init handoff. Unit and temporary-project integration tests prove preservation and second-run no-op.

title: Compaction recovery: re-inject codebase context after Claude Code compacts
description:
From GrapeRoot competitive analysis (TLDR-2o4), finding #3.

PROBLEM: when Claude Code compacts mid-conversation, codebase context evaporates and the agent rediscovers everything — with or without tldr installed. GrapeRoot installs hooks that re-inject context on compaction. (Same failure mode bd prime's SessionStart hook exists for, but for code context.)

PROPOSAL: a SessionStart hook (source=compact) / PreCompact hook that asks the daemon for a compact project re-orientation pack: project shape, the session-memory hot set (sibling issue), key signatures. Cheap to build once pre-injection + session memory exist — this is mostly a second trigger for the same packer.
notes: Installed SessionStart matchers for startup|resume|compact|fork. source=compact reuses the shared packer and session hot set; end-to-end compaction event returned source=compaction context after a PostToolUse event. Added startup-vs-compaction label regression coverage.
close_reason: Compaction recovery implemented through the shared lifecycle packer and verified end-to-end.

title: Session memory: track per-conversation reads/edits so follow-ups skip retrieval
description:
From GrapeRoot competitive analysis (TLDR-2o4), finding #2.

PROBLEM: our daemon caches ANALYSIS (Salsa, warmed caches) but knows nothing about the SESSION. Every question is a cold query even if the agent asked about the same file 30s ago. GrapeRoot keeps a live action graph of what was read/edited/decided during the conversation and routes follow-ups to previously-touched files with confidence=high, no retrieval.

PROPOSAL: lightweight per-session state in the daemon — session ID keyed, tracking files/symbols served, edits observed (we already watch the FS), and recency/frequency. Pre-injection (sibling issue) consults it first: follow-up turns get previously-touched context instantly and spend the remaining budget on NEW material only. Depends on pre-injection landing first to have a consumer.
notes: Implemented per-session daemon hot files/symbols, hook-served context, PostToolUse Read/Edit/Write tracking, watcher edit tracking, bounded frequency weighting, and prompt follow-up prioritization. Hot sets capped at 64 items with a regression test.
close_reason: Bounded live session memory implemented and verified.

title: Competitive analysis: GrapeRoot — learn from their delivery/lifecycle model
description:
We did a competitive product analysis of GrapeRoot (graperoot.dev, 'Dual-Graph') on 2026-06-04 and decided to learn from them and improve ourselves. These are the findings.

WHO THEY ARE: local-first codebase-context tool for Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Gemini / Copilot / OpenCode. Builds a code graph (files/functions/classes, import+call edges, keyword scoring), packs ~4k-token structured summaries (signatures, call edges, inline top-function bodies), and PRE-INJECTS them into the agent prompt in ~150ms via hooks — zero tool calls on the happy path.

KEY STRATEGIC DATA POINT: they STARTED as an MCP server (graph_continue/graph_read tools) and pivoted AWAY because per-call MCP protocol overhead (tool defs, routing, formatting) compounded across turns and ate the savings. That is empirical, experience-based evidence against the pull-only position tldr-mcp occupies in the loop.

WHERE THEY ARE BETTER (gaps to close, each a child issue):
1. Push vs pull delivery — pre-injection via hooks vs our tool-call-only model
2. Session memory — they track reads/edits/decisions during the conversation; our daemon caches analysis but knows nothing about the session
3. Compaction recovery — hooks re-inject context when Claude Code compacts; we lose everything
4. Cross-session persistence — decisions/WHY memory injected at session start; no cold start
5. Onboarding friction — one curl install, auto-config for six agents; we need cargo/binary + manual MCP registration + tldr doctor
6. Live session cost visibility — passive dashboard, 'what's my cost so far?' mid-session; our telemetry only measures tldr's own savings

WHERE WE ARE BETTER (do not regress): analysis depth (CFG/DFG/taint/call-graph/semantic search incl. measured modality-gap fixes) vs their keyword scoring; no auto-update-from-CDN supply-chain surface; published/verifiable behavior (their benchmarks page is empty).

TAKEAWAY: they win on everything AROUND the analysis (delivery, session lifecycle, onboarding); we win on the analysis itself. Items 1-3 are architecture gaps, not feature gaps. Our daemon already has warm caches and a fast answer path — a hook-based pre-injection mode on top of it neutralizes most of their advantage.

Raw research: .firecrawl/graperoot-docs.md, .firecrawl/graperoot-setup.md (session-local). Source: graperoot.dev/docs, graperoot.dev/setup, GitHub kunal12203/Codex-CLI-Compact.
notes:
Completed 2026-07-27. The six delivery/lifecycle gaps now share one resident hook/session design: push context, bounded live memory, compaction recovery, idempotent agent setup, queryable usage, and atomic cross-session continuity. Current official Claude/Codex hook schemas were verified before implementation. Full focused tests and end-to-end daemon lifecycle tests pass.
INSTALLED-SURFACE BENCHMARK 2026-07-28: UserPromptSubmit hook passed end-to-end in 0.11s and injected generation-scoped additionalContext while semantic warming was busy; session stats returned the documented zero-telemetry aggregate; MCP initialize negotiated tldr-mcp 0.4.0 and tools/list returned all 31 tools including tldr_session_stats. Full evidence: docs/FRESH_INSTALL_BENCHMARK_2026-07-28.md.
close_reason: All six competitive delivery/lifecycle gaps implemented, documented, and verified.

title: Memory-pressure escape hatch for never-idle daemons (observed 22.7GB RSS during build)
description: Resolve the memory-pressure counterweight to presence-based daemon liveness using the current post-redb embedding architecture. The historical FastEmbed cold-build path reproduced a 25.75 GiB peak, but bulk inference is now isolated in a disposable, resumable worker with redb checkpoints and bounded fixed-shape execution. The qualifying full-corpus candidate measured 3,029,172,224 bytes (2.82 GiB), below the declared 4 GiB ceiling. Policy decision: do not add a parent-daemon max-memory kill switch; worker recycling and process exit are the opt-in-safe escape mechanism while preserving daemon availability. macOS phys_footprint reporting remains the independent TLDR-d3s observability correction.
acceptance_criteria: Historical pressure is reproduced and attributed; replacement architecture guarantees bulk allocator reclamation on worker exit and resumes from durable checkpoints; full-corpus cold RSS is measured below 4 GiB; the parent daemon remains responsive and retains the previous generation; the no-parent-kill-switch decision and independent phys_footprint follow-up are recorded.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-07-27: TLDR-30f reproduced the legacy path at 25.75 GiB and filed/closed the allocator defect path. TLDR-9bxa.10 shipped process-isolated resumable bulk inference with finite retries and RSS-watermark recycling; TLDR-9bxa.11 measured the fixed-shape full-corpus path at 3,029,172,224 B (2.82 GiB), 82.34% below the 15.97 GiB FastEmbed oracle and within the 4 GiB gate. A parent max-RSS abort policy is rejected because daemon-required routing makes parent death a service outage and the memory-owning worker is already safely recyclable. TLDR-d3s remains open for status accuracy, not liveness correctness.
close_reason: Current architecture provides the escape hatch: bounded bulk inference runs in a checkpointed disposable worker measured at 2.82 GiB; parent-daemon max-memory termination is intentionally rejected to preserve availability.

title: MCP liveness parity — tldr_mcp binary must also defer daemon idle shutdown
description: Codex-identified gap (risk #1): a CLI-wide poke in run_command (main.rs:584/619) does NOT cover MCP — crates/tldr-cli/src/bin/tldr_mcp.rs is a separate binary entrypoint. Tests: core ancestor-match e2e, MCP tools/call integration test with bound datagram receiver. title: CLI-wide liveness poke: every tldr invocation defers daemon idle shutdown (registry-gated unix datagram)
description: Child B of TLDR-cxa (Codex verdict: NEEDS-CHANGE, changes folded in). Today only ~18/64 commands touch the daemon socket; ~45 generate zero liveness. IMPLEMENT IN run_command TOP-LEVEL DISPATCH (main.rs:619) — NOT daemon_router (opt-in via try_daemon_route, daemon_router.rs:51, covers only 12 commands). TRANSPORT (Codex): registry-gated UNIX DATAGRAM side channel — NOT stream connect-and-close (stream connect can block up to 5s, ipc.rs:397; accepted odd connects update activity then log 'Connection error', daemon.rs:321/328) and NOT touch-file (turns the 100ms accept loop, daemon.rs:316, into a perpetual disk poller). GATE: read_registry (prunes dead entries, daemon_registry.rs:165; entry carries project/pid/socket, daemon_registry.rs:41) — no daemon registered => no syscall beyond one small file read. CONSTRAINTS: zero perceptible latency on unrelated commands (tldr loc must not get slower), no retries, silent failure, opt-out env var for CI/bulk. Depends on A's presence API; independent of C.
close_reason: Shipped: registry-gated unix datagram poke in run_command (all surfaces), ancestor project matching, TLDR_NO_POKE opt-out, daemon-side receiver touching CliPoke, cleanup parity via PokeGuard + cleanup_socket_at sibling removal. Verified live: non-routed command pokes, subdir pokes, zero latency delta, no orphans. macOS unbound-datagram semantics verified empirically before building.

title: daemon status: liveness + build observability (per-source last-activity, busy+age, build progress, idle deadline)
description: Child C of TLDR-cxa (Codex verdict: SOUND). FullStatus today carries only status/uptime/files/project/salsa/dedup/session/hook stats (types.rs:519); handle_status fills only those (daemon.rs:1100). During a 90-min build there is NO way to distinguish building from done except poking semantic. ADD: per-source last-activity timestamps (socket/poke/watcher/internal), busy flags WITH AGE (a hung spawn_blocking at daemon.rs:490/1183 must be visible as 'busy 4h: warm-build' — stale-busy observability, Codex risk #3), index build state/progress, and computed time-until-idle-shutdown. COMPAT (Codex P3): response decoding is untagged with no versioning scheme visible in types.rs — adding fields must preserve decode order for older clients. Depends on A (TLDR-3w5) defining the tracker state this reports.

title: tldr embed: surface legacy-builder notice — steer callers to daemon start + warm flow
description: Found while testing the Phase 1 flow. 'tldr embed' is the legacy FOREGROUND builder: it silently runs the full (potentially ~90min) embedding build in the caller's terminal and exercises none of the new daemon warm path. Nothing in its output or help tells the caller that the blessed flow is now 'tldr daemon start && tldr warm'. Per the two-modes philosophy (works beautifully or says why), decide and implement ONE of: (a) KEEP embed as an explicit offline/CI builder but print a prominent notice on every invocation + in --help ('legacy foreground builder — prefer tldr daemon start && tldr warm; embeddings are shared via the per-chunk cache either way'); or (b) PARK it with the standardized message 'not available in this version, <reason>' like similar/--hybrid. Lean (a): embed writes the same per-chunk embedding cache that warm reuses, so it has legitimate offline/CI value — but it must say what it is. ACCEPTANCE: calling tldr embed surfaces the guidance; --help updated; scripts/smoke-test-cli.sh 'embed' case expectation updated to match the chosen behavior.
notes: REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): The legacy implementation path is absorbed by TLDR-eda5 and the one-shot shared redb ArtifactStore plan. The underlying user-visible requirement is preserved in that plan; this issue is superseded as an implementation vehicle, not erased as historical evidence.

title: Reduce C++ supervisor (tldr-cli-demon) to launchd-backed babysitter once fs-watch moves into Rust
description:
## Outcome

The external C++ supervisor path is retired, not reduced. The current supported lifecycle is owned entirely by tldr-code: tldr init installs a per-project launchd LaunchAgent that executes tldr daemon start --project … --foreground directly with KeepAlive=true.

## Ownership boundary

- launchd: Rust daemon process liveness/restart.
- Rust daemon: notify filesystem watcher, filtering, debounce/coalescing, burst handling, invalidation, and index mutation.
- IPC Notify: explicit manual/hook poke only; not a second watcher.
- External C++ supervisor/fsnotifier: absent from the supported repository, build, install, and release path.

The historical /tldr-cli-demon checkout referenced by this issue is no longer present; tldr-code-c++ is a different parser project and was intentionally left untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Supervisor no longer watches the filesystem; either reduced to pure liveness/restart or replaced by launchd KeepAlive on the Rust daemon. fsnotifier binary no longer shipped.
notes:
2026-06-02 (Codex review): Make this an EXPLICIT follow-through, not a vague cleanup. Hard requirement: prevent dual watcher ownership during transition — the C++ fsnotifier watch role must be turned OFF the moment TLDR-ac0.2's in-daemon watcher is live (running both = duplicate/racing events). Sequence: ac0.2 lands + verified -> disable C++ watch -> reduce/retire supervisor.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Preserved and linked to TLDR-eda5. This requirement remains independently valid and is an upstream input, consumer contract, correctness constraint, rollout gate, or acceptance criterion for the shared ArtifactStore; it is not superseded.
VERIFIED 2026-07-27: embedded LaunchAgent template directly invokes the resolved tldr binary with daemon start --project and --foreground, has KeepAlive=true, and contains neither fsnotifier nor tldr-cli-demon. Added lifecycle::launchd::tests::launch_agent_supervises_rust_daemon_directly as a permanent cutover guard and documented the final ownership boundary in DAEMON_SEMANTIC_ARCHITECTURE.md. Focused test, fmt, and warnings-denied all-feature CLI Clippy passed.
close_reason: launchd now supervises the Rust daemon directly; no C++ supervisor or fsnotifier remains in the supported lifecycle or shipped artifacts.

title: Spike: Qdrant (embedded mode) as vector-store backend — glue-deletion assessment
description: Spike Qdrant as a replacement for the usearch+sidecar store. Qdrant normally runs as a SERVER (gRPC/HTTP) — evaluate whether its embedded/in-process Rust crate path is viable for an offline CLI. Qdrant carries rich payload storage + filtering that overlaps our glue, but the server-first architecture is a direct tension with HARD CONSTRAINT #2 (no separate process).
design: Check vs the 4 HARD CONSTRAINTS in parent TLDR-e9j. Constraint #2 (embeddable, no server) is the likely disqualifier — assess FIRST and bail early if Qdrant cannot run in-process. If it can, payload + filter API would absorb the meta sidecar and scoped-query glue (TLDR-zr6).
acceptance_criteria: Report: (a) is there a genuinely EMBEDDED in-process mode (no daemon/server), or does it require spawning a Qdrant process? If server-only -> NO-GO and stop; (b) exact-search support for constraint #1; (c) glue absorbed + net LOC deleted; (d) dependency/build cost; (e) GO/NO-GO.
close_reason: Won't do: user committed to usearch+glue (2026-06-02). Qdrant Edge IS a real in-process Rust crate (overturned the server-only assumption) but irrelevant given the decision to stay on usearch.

title: Spike: LanceDB as vector-store backend — glue-deletion assessment
description: Spike LanceDB (embedded, Rust-native, columnar Lance format) as a replacement for the usearch+sidecar store. LanceDB stores vectors AND arbitrary columns (metadata) in one table with built-in persistence and predicate filtering — directly overlapping the glue we hand-wrote. Most promising candidate because it is embeddable (no server) and Rust-native.
design: Check vs the 4 HARD CONSTRAINTS in parent TLDR-e9j. KEY RISK: LanceDB's vector search may be ANN-first (IVF/HNSW); confirm a brute-force/exact path exists, else it fails constraint #1. Metadata-as-columns would delete the key->ChunkMeta HashMap sidecar AND the save/load manifest. Filtering (TLDR-zr6 scoped queries) may come for free.
acceptance_criteria: Report: (a) does LanceDB support EXACT search (not just ANN/IVF-PQ) so the TLDR-2a4 equivalence harness still passes? (b) which glue it absorbs — meta sidecar / persistence / filtering / freshness; (c) net LOC deleted from vector_store.rs; (d) new dependency weight + build cost; (e) GO/NO-GO.
close_reason: Won't do: user committed to retaining usearch+glue + fully in-memory index (2026-06-02). LanceDB research (firecrawl) recorded the finding (exact kNN via bypass_vector_index, BYO-vectors boundary = Arrow RecordBatch, heavy arrow-58 dep tree, less-mature Rust SDK) but the decision is to stay on usearch. No migration spike needed.

title: Re-evaluate vector-store backend vs embedded vector DBs (code-reduction lens)
description: The TLDR-uwb backend decision only weighed library-INDEX options (usearch, FAISS, HNSW) against a HAND-ROLLED mmap store. It never considered the embedded vector-DB tier (LanceDB, Qdrant, Chroma, Milvus), which bundles metadata + persistence + filtering and could absorb the ~1,100 non-test lines of glue in vector_store.rs. This is the umbrella to evaluate that blind spot. GOAL: decide whether a higher-level lib lets us DELETE store glue without breaking the hard constraints. Children spike LanceDB and Qdrant against a shared rubric.
design: HARD CONSTRAINTS any candidate must preserve (these are why usearch won): (1) EXACT search determinism — results must match the old scan bit-for-bit (TLDR-2a4 equivalence harness must still pass); (2) EMBEDDABLE in the CLI binary — NO mandatory separate server process; (3) LOCAL-ONLY / offline — no network, no API key at query time; (4) f32 exact mode (no forced quantization). EVALUATION RUBRIC (score each candidate): how many of these glue concerns does it absorb? — key->ChunkMeta sidecar, save/load manifest+integrity, corpus-digest freshness gate, capacity growth, u64 collision guard, path/lang filtering. Net glue-LOC delta. Build/CI cost (vs usearch's accepted C++/cxx cost). Maturity/maintenance.
acceptance_criteria: A written recommendation (keep usearch+glue, or migrate) backed by the per-candidate spikes, with a glue-LOC-deleted estimate for each, and TLDR-uwb amended or superseded accordingly.
close_reason: Won't do: backend re-evaluation concluded by user decision (2026-06-02) to RETAIN usearch+glue and keep the index fully in-memory. The blind spot TLDR-uwb missed (embedded vector DBs) was researched: LanceDB (GO-capable, exact kNN, but heavy arrow deps + Arrow-RecordBatch glue + less-mature Rust SDK) and Qdrant Edge (real in-process crate). Decision: not worth the dependency weight + determinism re-validation to delete ~1100 lines of glue. usearch+glue stands.

title: elixir structure method_infos/methods extraction broken (2 failing tests)
description: PRE-EXISTING, unrelated to m01/kkt/o48/4oz/lx6 (git diff df97ff3..HEAD shows my commits never touched elixir/structure code). Two tests in crates/tldr-cli/tests/elixir_method_infos_v1.rs fail: test_structure_elixir_method_infos_populated and test_structure_elixir_method_infos_count_matches_methods. They build an .ex fixture, run 'tldr structure', and expect files[0].methods[] to contain bar/baz and method_infos to be populated/count-matched. Currently failing -> elixir method extraction in the structure command is broken or its output schema drifted. Surfaced during the lx6 full-suite verification (earlier incomplete streaming captures of 'cargo test --workspace' hid it). These are the LAST 2 known default-suite failures after o48/4oz/lx6 fixed. Investigate the elixir structure/method extraction path.
notes: 2026-06-02 ROOT CAUSE PINPOINTED (diagnosis, not yet fixed). The failing tests (crates/tldr-cli/tests/elixir_method_infos_v1.rs) panic at line 66 (.expect methods array present) — the legacy 'methods' field is ABSENT (empty + skip_serializing_if). Ran tldr structure on the fixture: classes=['Foo'] OK, method_infos=[bar,baz] OK, but BOTH functions=None AND methods=None. So: method_infos works (built from extract_definitions -> try_elixir_call_definition, a GENERIC full-tree walk that matches a call's first 'identifier' child == def/defp; extractor.rs:234). The legacy methods (extractor.rs:218) comes from module_info.classes[].methods via extract.rs extract_elixir_module_info -> extract_elixir_module_functions (extract.rs ~6896/module fns). functions comes from extract_elixir_functions_detailed (extract.rs:6697). BOTH of those use POSITIONAL navigation (child.kind()=='call' then child.child(0) text=='def') and BOTH return empty, while the generic walker succeeds — strongly implies the tree-sitter-elixir parse shape no longer has 'def' at child.child(0) where the positional extractors look. CANDIDATE FIX: make extract_elixir_functions_detailed + extract_elixir_module_functions match the robust 'first identifier child' pattern that try_elixir_call_definition uses (NOT child.child(0)). REGRESSION GUARD: extractor.rs:205-209 invariant — sum(functions)+sum(methods) must equal health.summary.functions_analyzed; fixing functions extraction changes that sum, so re-verify the health invariant + the canonical-function-enumerator tests. Needs parse-tree confirmation before editing.
close_reason: FIXED (test-correction, not extractor). Root cause: the 2 tests asserted on the JSON 'methods' field, but methods AND functions are intentionally serde(skip_serializing) (types.rs:1276/1289, schema-cleanup-v1 BUG-13) — never in JSON for ANY language; method_infos is the sanctioned serialized surface. Elixir extraction was NOT broken: instrumented extract_from_tree returns functions=[bar,baz] and class Foo methods=[bar,baz] correctly, and method_infos JSON already had both with correct lines/signatures. NOTE: a Codex investigation proposed an extractor rewrite, but that was wrong for this symptom — it would not make the tests pass (panic is on get(methods), absent due to skip_serializing). Fix: updated the tests to assert on method_infos (names contain bar/baz; count==2) instead of the unserialized methods field; updated docstrings. 2 passed. Uncommitted in working tree.

title: clones_output_is_byte_stable flakes/fails: non-deterministic clone output
description: PRE-EXISTING (reproduced at commit 8a19b09, BEFORE the o48/4oz/warnings work — not a regression from it). crates/tldr-cli/tests/determinism_and_stderr_hygiene_v1.rs:230 clones_output_is_byte_stable runs 'tldr clones' 3x (stripping detection_time_ms) and asserts byte-identical JSON; it FAILS consistently (3/3) -> clone_pairs[] or some other field is still non-deterministically ordered despite the prior stability fix. Earlier workspace baseline runs MISSED this because the streaming 'cargo test --workspace' output capture was incomplete (it under-counted total passed). This is the 3rd known pre-existing default-suite failure alongside the now-fixed o48/4oz. Investigate the clones detector output ordering (HashMap iteration?) and make it deterministic; then the default 'cargo test --workspace' is fully green.
close_reason: FIXED (test fix). The clone CONTENT was deterministic all along; clones_output_is_byte_stable only stripped stats.detection_time_ms (+ a non-existent 'metadata' key) and MISSED summary.detection_time_ms, so the unstripped wall-clock timing made the byte comparison fail. Now strips detection_time_ms recursively. 5/5 green. Stale test, not a product non-determinism bug.

title: find_similar path matching fails on path-form mismatch (pre-existing; breaks tldr similar + ignored test)
description: PRE-EXISTING (reproduced on df97ff3, BEFORE any m01 work — NOT caused by TLDR-m01). The model-gated test semantic::index::index_tests::semantic_index_find_similar fails with ChunkNotFound { file: 'config.py', function: Some('parse_config') }. ROOT CAUSE: SemanticIndex::find_similar (index.rs:~518) matches the query chunk with an EXACT full-string compare c.chunk.file_path.to_string_lossy() == file_path. The test builds the index from temp_dir.path() so chunks carry the ABSOLUTE path (/tmp/.../config.py), but passes the BARE 'config.py' -> never matches. This is masked because the test is #[ignore]'d (loads the ONNX model), so default cargo test never runs it. find_similar is a PRODUCTION path: crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/similar.rs:158 (tldr similar <file> --function <fn>), so the same exact-match fragility likely breaks or surprises real CLI usage whenever the user-supplied path form differs from how chunks stored it (relative vs absolute vs canonical). FIX OPTIONS: (a) match by suffix/normalized path (ends_with on normalized separators, like the eval/store root_relative), or (b) canonicalize both sides before compare, or (c) fix the test to pass the stored path form AND harden find_similar for the CLI. Decide whether find_similar's contract takes a root-relative or absolute path and make CLI + matching consistent. Out of scope for m01; file kept separate.
close_reason: FIXED (commit 1db1c08). SemanticIndex::find_similar now matches the caller's path against chunk paths via canonicalize_for_match (exact fast path -> canonical-form fallback), so 'tldr similar' works when the caller's path form (canonicalized in similar.rs) differs from the walker's stored chunk path. Self-exclusion now keys off the query chunk's OWN stored path. Stale test fixed to pass a real path; added find_similar_matches_despite_path_form_mismatch (covers the '/./' form-mismatch via the canonical fallback). Both find_similar tests pass with the model.

title: GC reader-grace contract for the view()/mmap query path
description: Codex re-review (TLDR-l5d) #11: VectorStore::load() now takes a SHARED lock (vs save's EXCLUSIVE) so the RAM load path is safe against in-flight saves/GC. But the read-only view()/mmap QUERY path (TLDR-m01 rewire) does NOT yet hold that lock — a reader that mmaps index.<gen>.usearch can have it GC'd out from under it by a concurrent save. Need a reader-lock-or-retry contract: reader snapshots CURRENT, opens the immutable trio under a shared lock OR retries on a GC'd/missing file. Couple this with KEEP_GENS + the 60s grace window so a slow reader's gen survives. Blocks safe concurrent daemon query + reindex.
notes:
2026-06-02 REFRAMED by the fully-in-memory decision (memory in-memory-index-decision-2026-06-02). pdb's claim 'blocks safe concurrent daemon query+reindex' is SUPERSEDED by TLDR-ac0.1 (Arc<RwLock<VectorStore>> handles daemon concurrency in RAM — no per-query mmap). pdb now narrows to the COLD-CLI mmap-reader vs daemon-save GC race ONLY, and becomes fully MOOT if the cold CLI also load()s into RAM. Do not implement as written; re-scope after ac0.1.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): The legacy implementation path is absorbed by TLDR-eda5 and the one-shot shared redb ArtifactStore plan. The underlying user-visible requirement is preserved in that plan; this issue is superseded as an implementation vehicle, not erased as historical evidence.

title: Deterministic store tie-break for reproducible search output (l5d follow-up)
description: From the l5d n=52 equivalence review (REAL=0 verified): the usearch store's tie order for equal-cosine duplicate chunks is usearch-internal, and the dense path's tie order is filesystem-walk-order — neither is stable/reproducible across machines. OPTIONS: (A) accept usearch-native order (zero cost, default today); (B) post-sort store search hits by (distance asc, key asc) -> fully reproducible, hash-stable order independent of usearch internals, ~1 line, RECOMMENDED for test/output determinism; (C) strict byte-parity to the dense path via f64 rerank of usearch top-(K+margin) + a stored insertion-ordinal tie-break (matches an arbitrary walk-order baseline, costs holding/fetching vectors + ordinal). DECISION PENDING (user was in hold/discuss). Not a correctness blocker (REAL=0). Recommend B unless a consumer needs exact dense-order parity. Relates to l5d/ac0/m01.
notes:
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Partially absorbed and linked to TLDR-eda5. Shared persistence/generation/invalidation concerns move into the new ArtifactStore, while the issue’s distinct algorithm, quality, memory, serving, or evaluation work remains valid.
OWNER PRIORITY (2026-07-27): Version-two retrieval work postponed until the shared artifact architecture, watcher scheduling, and command-surface adoption are complete.

title: DECISION: ArcticL retained as deployed default; embedding-model SIZE is not the quality lever
description: MEASURED (clean baseline, n=14, prefix ON): ArcticL (1024d) R@5 0.786/R@10 0.929/MRR 0.707 vs ArcticM (768d) R@5 0.857/R@10 0.857/MRR 0.685. The M-vs-L difference is 1-2 single-case swings = WITHIN NOISE at n=14; the models are statistically indistinguishable on this eval. DECISION: (1) RETAIN ArcticL as the deployed default (user accepts the ~3x index time / 33% larger vectors; it is a hair better @10/MRR, not worse). (2) Treat embedding-model SIZE as NOT a quality lever for code search — the bottleneck is the MODALITY GAP (English query vs wordless code), already addressed by the query prefix (12x). Future quality gains come from TLDR-4er (lexical fusion) and TLDR-9m2 (LLM descriptions), NOT a bigger encoder. (3) Do not re-chase 'use a larger embedding model' — it has been measured and it does not move recall. Revisit only with the expanded gold set (TLDR-6h3), since n=14 cannot resolve model deltas anyway.
close_reason: ACCEPTED (ADR, 2026-06-01). Model-size measured and ruled out as a quality lever; ArcticL retained as deployed default. Recorded so future sessions don't re-chase a bigger encoder.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: CONFIRMING SUCCESSOR LINK (2026-07-27): TLDR-9bxa.3/TLDR-9bxa.11 retained Arctic-L and improved retrieval structurally to R@5 0.849, R@10 0.887, MRR 0.724. The result reinforces this decision that model size was not the primary lever.

title: Opt-in i8 'compact mode' quantization (4x smaller index, near-lossless for cosine)
description: usearch ScalarKind::I8 quantization: ~98.9% Recall@1 (near-lossless), valid for cosine (our metric), and our embeddings are ALREADY unit-normalized (matches usearch's i8 normalize->[-127,127] process). Shrinks the on-disk/mmap'd index ~4x (1.1GB->~280MB f32->i8; b1 binary even smaller) -> faster view() load, faster exact_search, lower RSS. OPT-IN only (config 'compact'/flag): i8 reorders vs f32 so it breaks the v1 results-equivalence gate (TLDR-2a4) — must be measured against the eval harness before recommending. Reframes closed TLDR-8pt as a usearch-native option.
acceptance_criteria: A config/flag enables i8 storage; eval harness shows recall delta vs f32 within an accepted bound; index size and cold-query latency drop measurably; f32 remains default.
notes:
2026-06-02: i8 is NOT just a flag (Codex review). exact_search_f32 gets no i8 benefit — i8 needs a SEPARATELY built quantized index (add_i8 / ScalarKind::I8) AND the QUERY quantized to i8 (exact_search_i8). Near-lossless for cosine on unit-normalized vectors, ~4x smaller. Gate: measure recall on the n=52 eval before flipping the default. Manifest scalar_kind already distinguishes f32/i8 stores (design doc §4.0).
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Partially absorbed and linked to TLDR-eda5. Shared persistence/generation/invalidation concerns move into the new ArtifactStore, while the issue’s distinct algorithm, quality, memory, serving, or evaluation work remains valid.
OWNER PRIORITY (2026-07-27): Version-two retrieval work postponed until the shared artifact architecture, watcher scheduling, and command-surface adoption are complete.

title: Scoped semantic queries via usearch filtered_search (path/language predicate)
description: Today 'tldr semantic <q> <subdir>' re-chunks + re-embeds the subdir each call (cold). With a single GLOBAL usearch index, usearch filtered_search_f32 + a StatefulPredicate can restrict results to a path prefix or language AT QUERY TIME — no per-scope re-embed. The metadata sidecar (key->{path,lines,lang}) supplies the predicate inputs. Big win for scoped/interactive queries once the global index + daemon warm path exist. Composable predicates (path AND language).
acceptance_criteria: tldr semantic <q> <subdir> filters a single global index by path predicate (no subdir re-embed); language filter works; results identical to filtering the unscoped results post-hoc.
notes:
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): Partially absorbed and linked to TLDR-eda5. Shared persistence/generation/invalidation concerns move into the new ArtifactStore, while the issue’s distinct algorithm, quality, memory, serving, or evaluation work remains valid.

title: DECISION: Arctic query prefix is ON by default (the recall fix)
description: MEASURED (eval, ArcticM, crates/tldr-core/src, 14 gold): embedding raw code without Arctic's query prefix gives near-random recall (recall@5 0.071). Prepending the trained query prefix ('Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ') to the QUERY only (not passages) lifts recall@5 to 0.857 / MRR to 0.685 — a 12x gain. DECISION: prefix is DEFAULT-ON (shipped e9e5427, TLDR-dlk closed). It is the model's trained-correct mode; do not regress. Caveat captured separately: it lowers absolute cosine scores -> the 0.50 CLI threshold must be recalibrated (TLDR-h27).
close_reason: ACCEPTED (ADR record, 2026-06-01). Decision is final and recorded; closing so it stays a durable, queryable record without sitting in the active work queue. Reopen only if the decision is revisited.

title: DECISION: v1 keeps f32 (exact-equivalence); i8 quantization is an opt-in 'compact mode', not default
description: usearch ScalarKind::I8 quantization is near-lossless for our case (98.9% Recall@1; valid for cosine; our embeddings are ALREADY unit-normalized — exactly usearch's i8 process) and 4x smaller (1.1GB->~280MB) + faster load/search/RSS. BUT i8 reorders results vs f32, which would break the results-equivalence PASS/FAIL gate (TLDR-2a4). DECISION: v1 ships f32 to preserve exact equivalence with the current brute-force baseline. i8 becomes an OPT-IN 'compact mode' (config/flag) AFTER v1 lands and equivalence is verified — measured against the eval harness, not assumed. (Reframes the closed TLDR-8pt as a usearch-native opt-in.)

title: Embed existing docstrings to bridge the modality gap (free, no-API-key precursor to 9m2)

description: Root cause of this epic (per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md v2.0): the canonical architecture is a 5-layer STATIC stack (AST->CallGraph->CFG->DFG->PDG). Semantic/embeddings/BM25/hybrid are NOT a layer, NOT in the data-flow diagram, NOT in the caching section — they exist only as throwaway CLI lines (search.rs/semantic.rs) and one MCP wrapper. That non-adoption is WHY the subsystem rotted (FAISS-downgrade, dead HTTP stub, unwired hybrid) while the documented layers stayed clean. This issue is the umbrella architectural work that the six sibling fixes serve: elevate semantic search to a first-class layer with the same rigor as the static layers.

MUST honor the documented 'intentionally avoids LSP' principle: in-process only, no HTTP service, no Redis. Caching should fit the documented daemon in-memory LRU model (metadata sidecar parsed once into daemon memory).
acceptance_criteria: ARCHITECTURE.md documents Layer 6 (Semantic/Retrieval) with the same structure as Layers 1-5; semantic search is reachable as a coherent tldr-core module rather than scattered CLI/MCP glue; the 6 sibling fixes (7kf/8pt/k4q/4er/cs5/1a8) land under this layer.

title: Vector search uses brute-force scalar scan (no SIMD/ANN)
description: similarity.rs:237 does an O(n) linear scan with a plain scalar cosine loop on every query. Defensible at the 10K-100K target scale (sub-ms, exact), but leaves a 5-10x constant-factor win on the table and the 100K ceiling reaches ~10ms/query. REPLACE: SimSIMD kernel dropped into top_k_similar for the cheap win; usearch (HNSW) only if scale ever exceeds ~100K vectors.
design: Swap surface is exactly one function: top_k_similar in semantic/similarity.rs. No design change needed for SimSIMD; usearch would require an index build/persist step.
notes: SESSION/DESIGN UPDATE (2026-06-01): CHALLENGED BY MEASUREMENT (epic TLDR-ac0). ac0 measured the cold-query breakdown: 4300ms JSON parse + 500ms model load + 200ms query embed + 0.1ms brute-force cosine. The scalar scan THIS issue targets is the 0.1ms term — NOT the bottleneck. ac0 keeps exact brute-force (HNSW/usearch is approximate AND only saves ~0.1ms->0.5ms). Likely SUPERSEDED by ac0 once the mmap-vs-usearch fork (TLDR-rgc) is locked. Do NOT implement SIMD/ANN until rgc decides. The old handoff framing 'usearch subsumes 7kf' is itself stale — ac0 argues AGAINST usearch.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by usearch decision (TLDR-rgc, 2026-06-01). usearch exact_search_f32 owns the vector scan — exact, SIMD-accelerated in C++. Also moot per ac0 measurement (scan was 0.1ms, never the bottleneck). No custom SIMD/ANN needed.

title: Semantic search: modernize vector lookup + complete hybrid retrieval
description: Umbrella for improving tldr's semantic/search subsystem. Two themes: (1) the vector-lookup mechanics are naive (brute-force scalar scan, f32, JSON persistence) though defensible at current scale; (2) the most modern retrieval design in the tree (RRF hybrid fusion) is built but unwired, and an alternate embedding path is a stub. Children track each problem and replacement. We will pick each child and discuss before implementing.
design:
FRAMING: Perf items (scan/quant/persist) are REGRESSIONS from the Python original (FAISS), not net-new gaps. Completeness items (dead RRF path, stub client, misnamed flag) are the higher-value fixes. The rewrite as a whole was net-positive (better modular architecture, in-process Arctic embeddings); it only regressed the vector-INDEX layer and left two features half-built.

DECIDED DIRECTION: Finish the in-process path with usearch (the Rust FAISS-equivalent that closes the FAISS-shaped hole WITHOUT a service dependency). Do NOT revive the HTTP embedding service (re-introduces cross-language/operational fragility the author was rightly avoiding). Do NOT add Redis (external server; the daemon already provides warm in-memory). 

usearch SUBSUMES three children: its Rust binding (usearch/rust/lib.rs) provides save/load + view (mmap) + ScalarKind quantization (F32/BF16/I8/B1x8) natively. So 7kf (scan), 8pt (quant), k4q (persistence) collapse into 'adopt usearch' + one small residual task: a metadata sidecar (u64 key -> {path,lines,snippet,hash,mtime}) that usearch does NOT store. JSON sidecar is acceptable — daemon parses it once and holds it in memory, so format has zero query-time cost.
notes:
PYTHON-PRECEDENT (llm-tldr/tldr/semantic.py): Python was MORE sophisticated at vector search — in-process BGE-large-en-v1.5 (sentence-transformers, 1024d) + FAISS IndexFlatIP + binary .faiss persistence (semantic.py:1068,1072,1134). Rust kept in-process embeddings (good, Arctic 768d) but DOWNGRADED the index: FAISS->scalar loop, binary->JSON. So 7kf/k4q are regressions, not net-new.

THE 8765 SERVICE NEVER EXISTED — ANYWHERE. Grep of the Python repo: no FastAPI/Flask/uvicorn/8765/endpoints. Python embedded in-process (semantic.py:206). So embedding_client.rs (cs5) was a NEW planned architecture, not a wrap of existing Python. The BGE-1024 model ref shows it was meant to run the same engine as Python, as a separate service.

AUTHOR DESIGN INTENT (reconstructed): strangler-fig migration — defer the hard ML port (sentence-transformers+FAISS are hard in Rust) by keeping embeddings in a Python HTTP service and calling it from Rust during the transition. The 'Mitigation M8 graceful-degradation -> BM25-only' header comment proves they knew the dependency was fragile. Then they pivoted to in-process fastembed (correct call) but only finished HALF: embeddings came in-process, FAISS's job was NOT replaced (no Rust ANN lib reached for) -> hand-rolled scalar scan. Result: dead HTTP stub + regressed index. usearch is the library that finishes the pivot.

8765 IS NOT LSP AND NOT MCP — it is a 4th orphaned subsystem. Transports proven: daemon=Unix socket / TCP axum (port=hash-of-project, NOT 8765); MCP=stdio JSON-RPC (no port); diagnostics 'LSP' tools=subprocess+parse stdout (NOT real LSP sessions; only severity enum is 'LSP-compatible'); embedding_client=HTTP REST (dead). NOTE: MCP is a CONSUMER of semantic — tldr_semantic is an exposed MCP tool (docs/MCP.md:107) — so the dead embedding layer degrades an agent-facing capability that is already wired up. That raises the value of completing 4er.

ROOT CAUSE — SEMANTIC SEARCH WAS NEVER ARCHITECTURALLY ADOPTED (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md v2.0). The canonical architecture is a 5-layer STATIC stack: AST -> Call Graph -> CFG -> DFG -> PDG. Semantic/embeddings/BM25/hybrid are NOT a layer, NOT in the data-flow diagram, NOT in the caching section — they appear only as two throwaway CLI lines (search.rs/semantic.rs) and one MCP wrapper. This explains WHY the subsystem rotted: the 5 documented layers stayed clean/tested while search — never first-class — got FAISS-downgraded, left with a dead stub and an unwired hybrid path. REFRAME: this epic is not just bug-cleanup; it is PROMOTING semantic search to a first-class architectural layer (Layer 6: Semantic/Retrieval) with the same rigor as the static layers. Deliverable should include: (a) a real Retrieval layer in tldr-core, (b) an ARCHITECTURE.md section documenting it (layer purpose, key types, data-flow, caching), (c) the in-process usearch index as its persistence/search engine.

DESIGN-PRINCIPLE FIT: ARCHITECTURE.md states 'intentionally avoids LSP' for speed/token-efficiency. usearch (in-process, no server) HONORS that principle; reviving the HTTP service or adding Redis would VIOLATE it. The documented caching model (daemon in-memory LRU keyed by tool+args+mtimes) also matches the proposed JSON metadata sidecar (parsed once into daemon memory) — so the recommended direction is consistent with the intended architecture, not a deviation.

MODEL NOTE: Python used BGE-large (1024d); Rust uses Arctic (768d). Deliberate swap (Arctic newer), but index dimensions differ from the Python era — not a parity port.

DOC DRIFT: ARCHITECTURE.md says 18 languages (overview) but the tier table lists 17; CLAUDE.md context implies ~15. Language count not pinned consistently — sign the docs are loosely maintained.


## SIMPLIFIED APPROACH: Complete JSON Cache Removal (2026-07-25)

**Current Understanding:**
Based on analysis during TLDR-30f cold-embed measurement, the JSON cache duplication is intentional but suboptimal. With usearch already providing efficient binary persistence + memory-mapping, the entire JSON cache flow can be removed.

**Simplified Architecture:**
Remove EmbeddingCache entirely and rely solely on usearch for vector persistence:

**Current Flow (with use_cache = true):**
1. Load JSON cache (cache.json) → get cached vectors
2. Compute missing vectors with ONNX  
3. Store new vectors in JSON cache
4. Build usearch index with ALL vectors
5. Save usearch index to disk (index.1.usearch)

**Simplified Flow:**
1. Load usearch index from disk (memory-mapped, efficient)
2. If index is stale/missing, rebuild with ONNX
3. Use usearch index for all operations

**What to Remove Completely:**
- EmbeddingCache module (crates/tldr-core/src/semantic/cache.rs)
- JSON cache file: ~/Library/Caches/tldr/embeddings/cache.json
- CacheConfig and use_cache parameter
- All cache-related logic in VectorStore::build()

**Benefits:**
- 100-200MB memory savings (no JSON overhead)
- Simpler architecture (single source of truth)
- No cache invalidation complexity
- Faster cold starts (no JSON parsing)
- usearch already provides needed persistence

**Rationale:**
usearch save/load + memory-mapping provides all the persistence benefits that JSON cache was meant to provide, but with better efficiency. The corpus_digest validation in usearch handles freshness detection, making the content hash + TTL logic in JSON cache redundant.

**Implementation:**
This simplifies the 'metadata sidecar' approach mentioned in the design notes — instead of keeping JSON for metadata, eliminate the sidecar entirely since usearch's file-based persistence is sufficient.

title: Clarify or suppress redundant --oneshot on local-only commands
description:
## Problem
The global `--oneshot`/`--local` flag is accepted by `tldr explain`, but it does not alter that command's execution. `Command::Explain` dispatches directly to `ExplainArgs::run` (`crates/tldr-cli/src/main.rs:749`), and `ExplainArgs::run` never consults `daemon_router::is_oneshot()` or routes through the daemon. The only flag effect is setting `TLDR_ONESHOT=1` in `run_command` (`main.rs:638-644`).

This is a silent no-op that can mislead users into believing `explain` normally uses the daemon or a daemon-owned/vector-backed analysis path.

## Reproduction
1. Stop the daemon and verify `tldr daemon status` reports `Daemon not running`.
2. Run `tldr explain crates/tldr-core/src/semantic/structural_planner.rs plan_file -f text`; it succeeds.
3. Run the same command with `--oneshot`; it follows the same local `ExplainArgs::run` path and produces equivalent output.

## Expected
The CLI should make command capability explicit rather than silently accepting a behavior flag that cannot change execution. Acceptable resolutions include capability-aware help, suppressing/rejecting the flag for local-only commands, or explicitly documenting that the global flag only affects daemon-capable commands. Audit other local-only commands for the same misleading no-op.
design: Prefer a centralized command-capability classification used by help/runtime validation over an explain-specific special case. Avoid routing explain through the daemon merely to make the flag meaningful.
acceptance_criteria:
- `tldr explain --help` and runtime behavior no longer imply that `--oneshot` changes explain execution.
- The selected behavior is covered by a CLI test.
- Daemon-capable commands retain their current `--oneshot` semantics.
- Other local-only commands are audited for the same silent no-op.
notes: Observed 2026-07-28: with the daemon stopped, `tldr explain` succeeds without `--oneshot`. Explain performs local file/Tree-sitter/call-graph/reference analysis and does not touch `VectorStore` or usearch.

title: Daemon Notify reindex_triggered:true is a misleading stub — threshold path clears dirty set but spawns no rebuild
description: crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/daemon/daemon.rs:1573-1584: when dirty_count >= auto_reindex_threshold, the code sets reindex_triggered=true and clears the dirty set but spawns NO background rebuild (comment: 'In full implementation, would spawn background reindex task. For now, just clear the dirty set'). The NotifyResponse reports reindex_triggered:true to the client, which implies a proactive rebuild that did not happen. test_daemon_handle_notify_threshold only asserts the dirty count resets, not that a reindex occurred.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) rename the response field to threshold_cleared to reflect reality, or (b) spawn an actual background rebuild (spawn_blocking build_project_call_graph_memoized) mirroring the warm path. Client contract no longer misleading.
notes: Found by code-review fan-out 2026-06-17. LOW — contract clarity.
close_reason: Resolved by making the contract honest rather than renaming the serialized field (wire-compat risk) or adding a redundant rebuild: freshness is ALREADY guaranteed per-save — process_dirty_file invalidates this file's hash + the project hash (so all project answers lazily recompose) and applies the semantic per-file delta. The threshold branch genuinely only flushes the dirty accounting set. Replaced the misleading 'would spawn background reindex task / for now just clear' comment with an accurate description. Flag is informational-only (notify.rs just prints). daemon 252/252.

title: salsa QueryCache.invalidate_by_input leaks ghost keys in dependents reverse-index for multi-input entries
description: crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/daemon/salsa.rs invalidate_by_input (~265-288): when an entry is registered under multiple input hashes (e.g. Calls uses vec![hash_path(root), hash_path(project)]), invalidating via ONE hash removes it from 'entries' but leaves the key in the OTHER hash's dependents set. Those ghost keys accumulate (entries.remove on an absent key is a graceful no-op, but dependents keeps growing). LRU eviction path (self.invalidate) cleans up correctly; only invalidate_by_input-evicted multi-input entries leak.
acceptance_criteria: After entries.remove, iterate entry.input_hashes.filter(|h| *h != input_hash) and remove the key from each dependents.get_mut(h). Test: register a 2-input entry, invalidate by one hash, assert the other dependents set no longer contains the key.

Fix direction (n74-aligned): explicit daemon-side clear/invalidate RPC; confirm quiescence before disk deletion; memo+disk cleared atomically.
