title: Cross-session persistence: inject project decisions/context at session start (no cold start)
description:
From GrapeRoot competitive analysis (TLDR-2o4), finding #4.

PROBLEM: GrapeRoot persists decisions and 'WHY' memory across sessions and injects them at startup — no cold start. tldr has nothing; this repo papers over it with beads/bd remember, but that's a personal setup, not a tldr feature.

PROPOSAL: persist a distilled session digest (hot files/symbols, decisions surfaced) in the project cache dir; SessionStart hook injects it. Builds on session memory (TLDR-2o4.2). SCOPE CAUTION: decision/WHY capture borders on issue-tracker territory (beads) — keep tldr's slice to CODE context continuity (hot set, recent structural changes), not task memory.
notes: Implemented atomic .tldr/session-context.json persistence, 32-session retention, bounded hot sets, daemon startup restore, and new-session project-hot injection. Restart test restored the prior epic-test ledger and supplied a generation-177 startup pack to a fresh cross-session-test session. Scope remains code-context continuity only.
close_reason: Cross-session code-context persistence implemented and restart-tested.

title: Live session cost visibility: queryable mid-session token/cost stats
description:
From GrapeRoot competitive analysis (TLDR-2o4), finding #6.

PROBLEM: our telemetry measures tldr's OWN savings (justifies tldr) but gives the user no session-cost observability. GrapeRoot has a passive dashboard and answers 'what's my cost so far?' mid-session.

PROPOSAL: daemon-side session token ledger (fed by hooks' session-end/usage events where available) + 'tldr session stats' command + expose via MCP so the agent itself can answer cost questions. Lowest priority of the set — nice-to-have vs the architecture gaps. Note overlap with existing savings telemetry (TLDR daemon stats) — extend, don't duplicate.
notes: Extended the daemon ledger with host-reported input/output tokens and cost plus locally measured injected tokens. Added tldr session stats and uncached MCP tldr_session_stats with explicit provider-telemetry caveat. End-to-end CLI output verified exact injected/provider totals.
close_reason: Live session token/cost visibility implemented through CLI and MCP.

title: disk-backed per-file chunk-invalidated salsa cache (replace whole-project in-RAM entries)
description: Full design sketch in TLDR-k8s design notes §5. Today: in-RAM DashMap of WHOLE-PROJECT JSON blobs; one changed file nukes the entire entry (full 22GB recompute); daemon restart loses everything. Proposal: persist per-FILE chunks (FileIR) keyed by (path, content_hash) in compact binary (rkyv → mmap zero-copy); project queries become compose-over-chunks (only cross-file resolution recomputes); file change → recompute ONE chunk (mirrors t8f semantic delta — invalidate_by_input plumbing already exists, only storage granularity + compose step are new); restart → seconds of mmap instead of 3.5min + 22GB. Open questions: measure standalone compose cost; schema versioning; atomic write via vector_store generation pattern; chunk enumeration must share corpus rules with TLDR-1qv/TLDR-kkt or caches drift.
design:
# DECISION STATE (consolidated 2026-06-05, post Gate-1 PASS — supersedes the 2026-06-04 consolidation; full evolution in the ADR chain TLDR-cv9..ab6, index comment 2026-06-05)

## MEASURED FACTS (rust on tldr-code, 745 files / 20,320 funcs / 26,312 edges)
- Phase split: scan ~10ms / parse 2.5-2.8s / compose 0.56s / total ~3.1s.
- Original premise "parse expensive, compose cheap" was INVERTED (ADR-1, closed):
  baseline compose was 223s = 98.8% of build — but that was SEVEN defects of one
  class (per-call-site linear scans -> indexed lookups), all dated to initial
  release, fixed output-identical across 5 rounds (commits 100f465/8ca8f0c/
  106738d/<round-5>). Campaign net: compose 400x, build 73x.
- GATE-1: PASS (0.56s < 2s line). Gate-0 (FileIR purity): PASS (earlier).
- Correctness: exhaustive synthetic differential + corpus-level value-identity
  gate (real call-site receivers) + frozen-corpus count identity + 8.4MB edge
  JSON deterministic run-to-run (old code was HashMap-order random).

## CURRENT ARCHITECTURAL POSITION (ADR-6 / TLDR-7mp)
- Recompose-always v1 STANDS as designed; escalation ladder (query-time
  resolution / incremental compose / Glean sets) NOT needed.
- BUT the chunk store's TIME case is now only ~2.7s parse memoization on a
  3.1s rebuild. Time alone no longer justifies Path B.
- MEMORY attribution corrected (ADR-7 / TLDR-ab6): headline 27GB peak is the
  EMBED phase (TLDR-3rh/yll), untouched by any chunk-store design; the
  callgraph transient was 11.4GB PRE-F1, post-F1 unmeasured.

## PATH FORK — DEFERRED pending exactly two measurements (ADR-6)
1. TLDR-myd: post-F1 warm memory peak (~22s run; needs resident-daemon auth).
2. TLDR-olg: python/TS resolver phase split (same defect class, unmeasured).
Decision rule: if F1 already took most of the callgraph transient AND other
languages respond to the same index treatment, Path A (surgical, no storage
layer) wins; Path B retains cross-process/CI chunk sharing (~parse only),
mmap-evictable steady state, restart-without-parse (~2.7s).

## STANDING RULES (active ADRs)
- ADR-3 (TLDR-k89): nothing above PROPOSED until kill-gates are MEASURED;
  no storage code before gates. (Replaced the LOCKED status of 2026-06-04.)
- ADR-4 (TLDR-w9z): pathological perf numbers = suspected defect first;
  profile->fix->re-bench before architecture escalation. Sum ALL profile
  branches; re-profile your own fixes.
- ADR-5 (TLDR-f0n): perf fixes proven output-identical via layered
  differential gates; legacy implementation retained as oracle.

## TECH CHOICES (status: PROPOSED, unchanged content)
rkyv 0.8.x chunks / fst symbol index / CSR fwd+rev / mmap zero-copy /
generation-commit lifecycle / ignore-first membership (TLDR-bpf oracle) /
bytecheck-once + header checksum. Rejections stand (Redis-class KV, Arrow hot
path, graph DBs, heap petgraph, JSON-as-storage, salsa v1, stack-graphs crate).
A6 format spike (rkyv vs epserde for CSR artifact) only relevant if Path B.

## POST-V1 PARKED (unchanged)
TLDR-38j oxc_resolver spike; Parquet/DataFusion analytics sidecar; Codex
independent review re-run (brief: /tmp/tldr-analysis-store-review-brief.md).

## ADR-9 (2026-06-05): query-serving half unparked
ADR-9 (TLDR-t0s, 2026-06-05) UNPARKS THE QUERY-SERVING HALF of this design:
the graph-native CSR fwd+rev + interning + ArcSwap snapshot layout moves
into the daemon as a RAM-resident structure (epic TLDR-7pp, child TLDR-n74).
The DISK layer (rkyv chunks, mmap, generation commits) remains PARKED per
ADR-8 — restart ~3s (parallel re-parse + recompose) is accepted; if restart
pain is ever measured, this design's chunk store slots under the per-file
fact layer (TLDR-iqr) unchanged. Also: TLDR-iqr implements the in-RAM kernel
of this design (per-file FileIR memo, content-hash keyed) — "Path A.5".

## ADR-8 (2026-06-05): PARKED
Path A adopted, this issue PARKED (P3). Chain: ADR-1(closed) -> ADR-6(closed)
-> ADR-8(active). No measured problem remains in storage layer's scope.

## ADR-12 (2026-07-25): REOPENED — JSON-elimination + true delta-write constraint supersedes ADR-8's park

TRIGGER FOR REOPEN (satisfies ADR-8's own bar: 'reopen only on new measured pain'):
1. NEW MEASURED PAIN, live (TLDR-30f re-measurement session, 2026-07-25): cold
   embed run on this exact corpus (1592 files) ran 66+min without plateauing,
   peak_rss (getrusage) hit 25.75GB, vmmap showed 195x uniform 128MB
   MALLOC_LARGE blocks (~93% of resident footprint) — reproduces the
   historical 22-27GB headline live, on current main, post every prior fix.
   This is EMBED-phase (TLDR-3rh territory per ADR-7), NOT this issue's
   callgraph/salsa scope — but it is new evidence the 10x-corpus-scale bar
   ADR-8 set for reopening is now plausible sooner than assumed.
2. NEW EXPLICIT CONSTRAINT (owner, 2026-07-25): eliminate JSON from every
   on-disk cache (salsa query_cache.bin, structure cache, callgraph cache —
   all currently serde_json despite this design's own 'JSON-as-storage:
   rejected' tech-choice line above) AND require genuine per-entry delta
   writes, not just cheaper full-cache rewrites. This is a decision-input
   change ADR-6/ADR-8 did not have: those ADRs judged the STORAGE layer
   against a time/memory bar (restart ~3s, memory not this layer's problem);
   they never evaluated it against a 'must support incremental writes'
   correctness/architecture bar.

CORRECTION TO 'TECH CHOICES' ABOVE — rkyv + generation-commit lifecycle does
NOT deliver true delta writes: verified against the ALREADY-SHIPPED reference
implementation of this exact pattern (crates/tldr-core/src/semantic/cache.rs,
the embedding cache). Its flush() deserializes the ENTIRE latest generation,
applies small in-RAM overlay/tombstone deltas, then re-serializes and writes
the WHOLE merged map as a new generation file. Generations buy atomicity
(crash-safe swap), not incrementality — every flush is O(whole cache) in both
disk I/O and transient RAM (old+new merged maps coexist). This was fine for
ADR-8's bar (bounded restart cost) but does NOT satisfy 'incremental write'
as a correctness requirement.

OPTIONS EVALUATED (2026-07-25, for salsa/structure/callgraph caches — NOT
proposing to touch the embedding cache's shipped code without separate
measurement):
A. Encoding-only swap (serde_json -> rkyv, same whole-file-per-write shape).
   Removes JSON parse-tree tax; does NOT solve delta-write. Low effort/risk.
B. Extend the existing DiskMap generation pattern to the other 2 caches.
   Cheaper+smaller writes than A, but per the correction above still
   O(whole-cache) per flush — same architecture class as what's already
   shipped, not genuine delta writes. Medium effort.
C. Adopt a real embedded KV/LSM engine (turbo-persistence [Vercel/Turbopack,
   SST files, per-key WriteBatch, bloom-filter reads, background compaction —
   purpose-built for incremental compiler caches, research in
   .firecrawl/turbo-persistence-readme.md] or redb [simpler pure-Rust B-tree
   KV, ACID, not yet researched in this repo]). Only option where a single
   file's write touches only that file's record, never the whole cache;
   compaction is the engine's job. NOTE re 'Rejections stand' above:
   'Redis-class KV' referred to a networked/out-of-process store (Redis
   itself) — redb/turbo-persistence are in-process embedded libraries, a
   different kind, not covered by that original rejection; worth a fresh,
   explicit call rather than assuming the old rejection extends to them.
   Highest effort (new dependency, rewrite salsa.rs's persistence layer
   around a KV API, one-time cache-format migration).
D. No structural change, just flush less often. Doesn't meet the constraint.

RECOMMENDATION (pending owner confirmation): Option C for salsa/structure/
callgraph caches specifically, since B was shown above to not actually meet
the stated constraint. Next step if approved: research redb (no firecrawl
notes exist yet) head-to-head against turbo-persistence's already-researched
design before committing engineering effort; prototype against the smallest
cache first (structure cache) to get a concrete before/after size + delta-
write-latency number.

STATUS (superseded by ADR-13 below): REOPENED, P3.

## ADR-13 (2026-07-25): DECISION RATIFIED — redb, scoped to durability + incremental-warm, not the live hot path

Supersedes ADR-12's 'pending comparison' status. Verdict, grounded in tracing
actual call sites (not just cache API shape) in salsa.rs/enriched.rs/
daemon.rs:

REDB RESEARCH (github.com/cberner/redb, docs.rs/redb, verified 2026-07-25):
pure Rust, no C/C++ FFI, dual MIT/Apache-2.0, standalone crates.io publish
(v4.1.0, Apr 2026), 1.0-stable since 2023-06-16 with a file-format stability
guarantee, very active (commits last week, 4.7k stars, 2.2k dependents).
Copy-on-write B+trees (LMDB-inspired), zero-copy BTreeMap-like API, full
ACID + MVCC (readers never block writer), crash-safe by default, savepoints.
Official benchmark vs lmdb/rocksdb/fjall/sqlite: wins outright on individual
writes (920ms vs lmdb 1598/rocksdb 2432/sqlite 7040) — closest proxy to our
delta-write need — loses on raw read latency (lmdb ~2x) and disk footprint
(needs explicit compact(), same class of maintenance as our current
hand-rolled DiskMap generations, but via a tested built-in API).

TURBO-PERSISTENCE: confirmed NOT published to crates.io (404). Only exists
as internal source inside vercel/turbo's (now vercel/next.js's) monorepo,
consumed via path deps, no independent semver release. Adopting it means
git-pinning into someone else's fast-moving monorepo with no stability
contract. Rejected on standalone-viability grounds alone.

USAGE-PATTERN TRACE (2026-07-25, reading actual call sites, not just the
cache API shape) — this reframed the justification entirely:
None of the 3 JSON caches has a hot per-entry disk-write path today.
- query_cache.bin: live queries hit an in-RAM DashMap only (zero disk I/O
  per query). save_to_file() has exactly ONE call site — daemon.rs:656,
  persist_stats(), on the CLEAN-shutdown path only, right before
  DaemonStatus::Stopped. No periodic checkpoint exists during a live
  session. load_from_file() has one call site (cache_stats.rs, daemon
  startup / separate `tldr cache-stats` CLI invocation).
- structure/callgraph caches: one full rewrite per `tldr warm` run (whole
  corpus), one read per query session; no incremental per-file update path
  exists in production code (only tests roundtrip write->read).
- Writes ARE already atomic (write-to-temp + rename, checksum +
  schema-version, graceful-discard on corruption per v031-cluster-M3b) —
  this is not a naive hack.
- Incidental bug found: daemon.rs::persist_stats() writes
  cache_dir/query_cache.bin but cache_stats.rs::load_salsa_stats() reads
  cache_dir/salsa_cache.bin — filename mismatch, `tldr cache-stats` silently
  never finds the persisted cache today. Filed separately as TLDR-bbhv
  (unrelated to the redb decision, should ship independently/first).

ADOPT redb for:
1. Salsa query-cache DURABILITY CHECKPOINT — persist_stats() today only
   runs on clean shutdown; an unclean exit (crash, OOM-kill — a live risk
   per TLDR-30f's 20GB+ RSS finding) loses the entire cache. redb gives
   per-commit durability. Implementation: checkpoint on a timer or
   invalidation-batch boundary, NOT per query — the live DashMap hot path
   stays exactly as-is (pure RAM, zero disk I/O per query).
2. Structure/callgraph caches, keyed by file path — enables true
   incremental `tldr warm` (recompute+write ONE file's entry) where today
   it's always a full-corpus JSON rewrite with no incremental path in
   production code.

DO NOT adopt redb for:
- The live per-query invalidate/insert path itself (already free;
  transaction commits would only add latency for no offsetting benefit).
- The embedding cache (cache.rs) — already shipped on rkyv, out of scope
  without separate measurement.

ROLLOUT ORDER: (1) TLDR-bbhv filename-mismatch bugfix (independent, ship
first), (2) prototype redb on structure cache only, measure real
write-latency + on-disk-size before/after, (3) if validated, apply to
callgraph cache, (4) add redb checkpoint under salsa's DashMap for
crash-safety. Embedding cache untouched throughout.

STATUS: ACCEPTED. Priority reconsideration: the crash-safety angle (item 1)
is now causally tied to a live, currently-open risk (TLDR-30f's OOM
exposure), which argues for re-prioritizing above P3 — flagged for owner,
not unilaterally changed here.

## ADR-14 (2026-07-25): PROPOSED — unified single-file redb store (full redesign, CLI contract frozen)

CONSTRAINT (owner, 2026-07-25): the ONLY frozen contract is the external tldr
CLI surface (subcommands, flags, output schemas). Everything internal may
change. All 3 caches hide behind Rust function signatures
(read/write_structure_cache, read_callgraph_cache, QueryCache methods,
cache-stats JSON shape), so the storage engine can be swapped with zero
CLI-visible change.

PROPOSAL: one store.redb per project replacing query_cache.bin +
structure.json + call_graph.json, with tables mapped 1:1 onto existing
in-memory shapes (no reshaping):
- queries:           Table<QueryKey, CacheEntry>        (1:1 with DashMap<QueryKey, CacheEntry>)
- query_dependents:  MultimapTable<u64, QueryKey>       (1:1 with DashMap<u64, HashSet<QueryKey>> -- redb has a NATIVE multimap type for exactly this shape)
- structure:         Table<PathBuf, Vec<DefinitionInfo>> (per-file granularity already latent in StructureCacheEnvelope, never exploited)
- callgraph_fwd/rev: MultimapTable<String, String>      (today read_callgraph_cache rebuilds BOTH direction HashMaps from a flat edge list on EVERY read; pre-indexed multimap tables remove that per-read rebuild)
- meta:              single-row table for OUR logical schema version only
  (redb's txn log subsumes the hand-rolled CACHE_MAGIC/checksum/atomic-rename
  /graceful-discard framing in salsa.rs -- ~100+ lines DELETED, not ported)

IMPROVEMENTS RANKED:
1. Crash-safety: periodic redb checkpoint under the (unchanged) DashMap hot
   path bounds cache loss to minutes-since-last-commit instead of everything.
   Causally tied to live OOM risk (TLDR-30f, 25.75GB peak observed).
2. True incremental tldr warm: recompute+write ONE file's key; write cost
   decouples from corpus size (the delta-write constraint rkyv-generations
   could not satisfy).
3. New consistency guarantee: structure+callgraph commit in ONE ACID txn,
   eliminating the crash window where the two JSON files drift (latent bug
   class today).
4. Faster callgraph reads for free (no JSON parse + no per-read HashMap
   rebuild; zero-copy reads).
5. Net code deletion (bespoke durability framing removed; filename-drift bug
   class of TLDR-bbhv structurally eliminated -- one Database::open()).
6. JSON fully eliminated from these caches per owner constraint.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS / HONEST LIMITS:
- Zero impact on the 25GB embed-phase memory headline (ONNX arena territory,
  TLDR-30f) -- different problem.
- No hot-path query speedup (already free in RAM; deliberately untouched).
- Disk footprint needs periodic compact() -- same maintenance class as
  today's generational files, but via a tested built-in API.
- Embedding cache (cache.rs) remains EXCLUDED (bulk zero-copy mmap over large
  vector blobs is a different access pattern; already meets its bar per
  ADR-8; would need separate measurement before folding in).

OPEN FORK (owner to decide): salsa tables in the SAME store.redb as
structure/callgraph (simpler, enables cross-cache atomicity, but redb allows
only ONE write txn in flight per Database so a warm write and a salsa
checkpoint would briefly serialize) vs. a separate file (fully independent
write paths, loses cross-cache atomicity). Recommendation: one file -- both
write classes are low-frequency, serialization is negligible.

MIGRATION: none needed -- legacy JSON caches treated as stale on first run
(matches the established v031-cluster-M3b graceful-discard convention);
cold-rebuild-on-upgrade is today's behavior for any format bump already.

STATUS: PROPOSED (pending owner ratification + redb capability research --
see notes for the docs.rs deep-dive).
notes:
PARKED by ADR-8 (TLDR-asv, 2026-06-05): no measured problem remains in the storage layer's scope. Design + ADR chain preserved; reopen only on new measured pain (e.g. 10x corpus scale).
ADR-12 (2026-07-25) REOPENS this issue for the JSON-elimination + delta-write axis (owner-driven new constraint + new measured embed-phase pain from TLDR-30f), superseding ADR-8's park for that specific axis. ADR-8's original memory/restart-cost finding is untouched. See design field for full options analysis (A: encoding-only, B: extend existing generation pattern -- shown NOT to give true delta writes, C: real embedded KV/LSM engine [turbo-persistence or redb] -- recommended, D: rejected). Scope: salsa query_cache.bin + structure cache + callgraph cache (all still serde_json today, violating this design's own pre-existing 'JSON-as-storage: rejected' tech choice). Explicitly NOT proposing to touch the already-shipped embedding cache (cache.rs) without separate measurement.
RESEARCH COMPLETE (2026-07-25) for ADR-12's pending redb-vs-turbo-persistence comparison:

REDB (github.com/cberner/redb, docs.rs/redb) — verified via GitHub+docs.rs, 2026-07-25:
- Pure Rust, no C/C++ FFI. Dual MIT/Apache-2.0. Standalone crates.io publish (v4.1.0, 09 Jul 2026); NOT tied to any larger monorepo.
- Stable since 1.0 (2023-06-16); file format has a stability guarantee w/ upgrade paths. Very active: 1602 commits, last commit last week (Jul 17 2026), 64 releases, 39 contributors, 4.7k stars, 2.2k dependents on GitHub.
- Design: copy-on-write B+trees, loosely LMDB-inspired. Zero-copy BTreeMap-like API (AccessGuard), full ACID txns, MVCC (readers never block writer), crash-safe by default, savepoints/rollbacks.
- Official benchmark (redb repo, Ryzen 9950X3D/NVMe) vs lmdb/rocksdb/fjall/sqlite: redb wins 'individual writes' outright (920ms, beats lmdb 1598/rocksdb 2432/fjall 3488/sqlite 7040) -- this is the closest proxy to our per-entry delta-write pattern. redb loses on raw random-read latency (lmdb ~2x faster) and loses badly on disk footprint (rocksdb 893MB vs redb 4.00GiB uncompacted / 1.69GiB after explicit compact()) -- redb needs periodic manual compaction like our current DiskMap generations, but via a real, tested, built-in API rather than hand-rolled logic.
- Verdict: strong fit for our actual requirement (single-key incremental write, correctness/ACID, no external process) even though it is not the fastest KV store on every axis.

TURBO-PERSISTENCE — re-verified 2026-07-25 (resolves prior session's open question):
- Confirmed NOT published to crates.io (crates.io/crates/turbo-persistence -> 404 'not found'). Only exists as source inside vercel/turbo's (and now vercel/next.js's, post 2024 monorepo move) internal workspace, consumed via path deps by turbopack/turbo-tasks crates, never as an independent semver-versioned dependency.
- Practical consequence: adopting it would mean git-pinning to a commit inside a large, fast-moving, externally-unstable-API monorepo not designed for third-party embedding, with no crates.io release cadence, no semver contract, and dependency-graph risk (would need to vendor or maintain a git dependency across future turbo/next.js repo reorganizations, which have already happened once).

CONCLUSION / RECOMMENDATION (supersedes 'pending comparison' in ADR-12): choose **redb** over turbo-persistence. redb is a standalone, 1.0-stable, actively-maintained, permissively-licensed, pure-Rust embedded KV store with a real one-line crates.io dependency and no external monorepo coupling; turbo-persistence's design (SST/LSM/bloom-filter/compaction) is architecturally elegant but not consumable outside vercel/turbo's own build. Next concrete step: prototype redb against the smallest target (structure cache in search/enriched.rs) to get an actual before/after write-latency + on-disk-size number, per ADR-12's stated next step.
REFRAMED FIT ANALYSIS (2026-07-25) after reading actual call sites in salsa.rs/enriched.rs/daemon.rs (not just the cache API shape):

None of the 3 JSON caches has a hot per-entry disk-write path today:
- query_cache.bin: live queries hit an in-RAM DashMap only (zero disk I/O per query). save_to_file() has exactly ONE call site -- daemon.rs:656, persist_stats(), on the CLEAN-shutdown path only, right before DaemonStatus::Stopped. No periodic checkpoint exists. load_from_file() has one call site (cache_stats.rs, on daemon startup / separate tldr cache-stats CLI invocation).
- structure/callgraph caches: one full rewrite per tldr warm run (whole corpus), one read per query session; no incremental per-file update path exists in production code (only tests roundtrip write->read).
- Writes ARE already atomic (write-to-temp + rename, checksum + schema-version, graceful-discard on corruption per v031-cluster-M3b) -- this is not a naive hack.

REVISED VERDICT: redb's actual value here is NOT 'faster writes' (current writes are rare/batch, not a measured bottleneck) -- it's:
1. CRASH-SAFETY: persist_stats() only runs on clean shutdown. An unclean exit (crash, OOM-kill) loses the ENTIRE query_cache.bin. Directly relevant to this session's live TLDR-30f finding (daemon RSS climbing past 20GB, real OOM risk) -- with redb, per-transaction durability means a crash only loses activity since the last commit, not the whole cache. Strongest concrete justification found.
2. TRUE INCREMENTAL WARM: structure/callgraph caches are all-or-nothing full-corpus rewrites; no 'just this file' path exists yet. A redb table keyed by file path enables writing only changed keys on file-watcher-triggered re-warm -- this matches TLDR-zde's own stated goal.
3. Incidental bug found while reading: daemon.rs::persist_stats() writes cache_dir/query_cache.bin but cache_stats.rs::load_salsa_stats() reads cache_dir/salsa_cache.bin -- filename mismatch, so 'tldr cache-stats' silently never finds the persisted cache today. One redb Database::open() call removes this whole bug class (single file, single API, no naming drift across call sites).

INTEGRATION GUIDANCE: do NOT route the live per-query invalidate/insert hot path through redb transactions (it's currently free/pure-RAM; even relaxed durability adds real per-query overhead for no offsetting benefit). Keep DashMap as the hot layer; use redb only as the periodic/checkpoint durability sink underneath it (e.g. commit on invalidation batches or a timer), and as the keyed store for structure/callgraph per-file entries. Cross-process concurrency (tldr cache-stats reading while daemon runs) already works safely today via atomic rename; redb's MVCC replaces that convention with a tested one but isn't fixing existing brokenness there.
ADR-13 ratifies the redb decision (see design field): scoped to (1) a periodic durability checkpoint under salsa's existing DashMap hot path and (2) per-file keyed structure/callgraph caches for true incremental tldr warm. Explicitly NOT touching the live per-query hot path or the embedding cache. Filed a separate bug for the query_cache.bin/salsa_cache.bin filename mismatch discovered during this trace (unrelated to redb, should ship independently/first).
ADR-14 (PROPOSED) added to design: full unified-store redesign -- one store.redb per project (tables: queries, query_dependents [MultimapTable], structure [per-file keys], callgraph_fwd/rev [MultimapTables], meta), replacing all 3 JSON caches behind unchanged internal function signatures; CLI contract untouched. Key gains: crash-safe periodic checkpointing (bounded loss vs total loss on OOM-kill), true per-file incremental warm, single-txn structure+callgraph consistency, per-read callgraph rebuild eliminated, ~100+ lines of bespoke durability framing deleted. Open fork for owner: single shared DB file vs separate salsa file (single-writer serialization trade-off). Next: deep redb capability research (docs.rs) before implementation.
REDESIGN AUDIT (2026-07-27): The legacy implementation path is absorbed by TLDR-eda5 and the one-shot shared redb ArtifactStore plan. The underlying user-visible requirement is preserved in that plan; this issue is superseded as an implementation vehicle, not erased as historical evidence.

TWO VIABILITY GATES: Gate 0 — FileIR must be pure parse output: VERIFIED 2026-06-04, resolution phase takes &file_ir immutably (builder_v2.rs:924,953) and writes resolved edges to separate structures (956); compose iterates ir.files.iter() as shared refs — no write-back, chunks cannot cache stale resolution. Gate 1 — compose-only cost bench (steps 5-12 over pre-built FileIRs) is an APPROVAL BLOCKER, not an open question: full-recompose-per-delta is only viable if global compose is ~sub-2s; if compose is a large fraction of build time, incremental compose is forced into v1 (much bigger design). NOTE this is NOT what TLDR-335 measures (that's parse-plateau allocation attribution) — separate cheap spike needed. PRECISION: this design kills the TRANSIENT 22GB build peak (ASTs+DOM); steady-state resident becomes composed-graph size in ArcSwap — bounded but uncharacterized; idle/warm was already fine at 1.4GB. NAMING: drop 'salsa v2' label — Q10 (adopt real salsa crate for compose layer?) shouldn't be prejudged by the name.

# Research: 2026 state-of-the-art for persistent, zero-copy, incremental analysis caches
## TLDR-zde research annex — sources scraped 2026-06-04 via Firecrawl (.firecrawl/)
## Status: research base. Codex review (pending retry) merges into this; user requirements R1-R6 are the rubric.

## A. What each production system does (2026)

### A1. salsa crate — persistent caching MERGED (PR #967, Aug 11 2025, `persistence` feature)
Source: github.com/salsa-rs/salsa/pull/967 + hackmd.io/@ibraheemdev/S17Bxowwxg
- ADDITIVE OPT-IN persistence: only queries/structs marked serializable are persisted;
  unmarked intermediate memos are dropped and their input deps are FLATTENED into the
  serialized query's dep list (so correctness survives partial persistence).
- `ValidateInput` trait: after deserialize, inputs re-sync against the real world
  (read file → if changed, set_field → revision bump → downstream invalidation).
  This is exactly tldr's kkt freshness-gate idea, formalized.
- Compile-time consistency: a serializable struct cannot contain a non-serializable
  one (can't persist an ID without its data).
- Limitations (per PR): transitive deps forced serializable, no query hashing yet,
  accumulators not serializable. Followups active — a Jan 1 2026 issue comment marks
  this as THE live thread (driven by ty/Astral's needs; MichaReiser asked for it
  in Apr 2024 explicitly because "persistent cache is essential for CLI + CI").
- FORMAT: serde-based → parse-on-load. NOT zero-copy. This is the gap vs R1.

### A2. Turbopack — filesystem caching SHIPPED on-by-default (Next.js 16.1)
Source: nextjs.org/blog/turbopack-incremental-computation + turbo-persistence README
- Persists the ENTIRE incremental-computation state: dependency graph, aggregation
  graph, and all intermediate value cells. Restart = resume warm. "Over a year of
  dedicated work" to meet quality bar.
- Aggregation graph: coarsened layers over the fine dep graph (hundreds of thousands
  of nodes) so invalidation traversals don't walk the full graph — their answer to
  graph-walk cost at scale.
- turbo-persistence (custom store, LSM-flavored):
  - Immutable files named by sequence number; single CURRENT file holds committed seq
    (same shape as tldr's vector_store generation pattern — independent convergence!).
  - Static Sorted Tables (.sst) + blob files + tombstone files + meta files with
    hash-range + AMQF (approximate membership filter) for fast key routing.
  - Value tiers: INLINE (≤8B in key block) / SMALL (≤4KB shared blocks) /
    MEDIUM (≤64MB dedicated blocks) / BLOB (>64MB separate file).
  - Single write transaction, concurrently fillable from many threads; uncommitted
    leftovers auto-cleaned on startup. Optimized for bulk-write + fast random read.

### A3. rust-analyzer — durabilities (the validation-cost insight)
Source: rust-analyzer.github.io/blog/2023/07/24/durable-incrementality.html (+ issue #4712)
- No persistent cache in-process (still true; #4712 remains open; their hopes ride on
  the new salsa persistence work).
- KEY IDEA TO STEAL — durability tiers: inputs classified volatile/normal/durable
  (user file vs deps vs stdlib). Validation flooding stops at durability boundaries:
  a change to a volatile input doesn't force re-validating the durable universe.
  Without this, even no-op revalidation walks the whole query graph.
- Maps directly to tldr: per-file chunks = normal; project config (Cargo.toml,
  tsconfig, .tldrignore!) = durable inputs whose change invalidates ModuleIndex
  and the compose layer wholesale; compose output = volatile derived layer.

### A4. Cloudflare mmap-sync — zero-copy reads in production (the R1+R3 existence proof)
Source: crates.io/crates/mmap-sync (v2.x)
- rkyv-archived data in shared mmap; wait-free single-writer / many-reader via
  Synchronizer; readers access archived structs IN PLACE — zero deserialization,
  zero copies, RAM cost = page cache only.
- Production-proven (Cloudflare bot-scoring ML feature store). Proves the
  "disk holds archived data, RAM holds only the map + index" model at scale.

### A5. rkyv — the zero-copy format itself
Source: rkyv.org/zero-copy-deserialization.html, docs.rs/rkyv
- Total zero-copy: archived form IS the in-memory form (relative pointers);
  `access` = pointer cast + optional bytecheck validation. No allocation, no parse.
- Cost side: requires Archive derives across the whole type tree (PathBuf/String/
  HashMap-heavy types need rkyv-compatible mirrors); archived types are read-only
  views; schema evolution = explicit versioning discipline.
- bincode/postcard by contrast: compact but ALWAYS parse+allocate on load.

## B. Synthesis: the 2026 architecture for tldr's analysis cache, vs requirements

R1 (near-zero ser/de CPU):
  Chunk payloads = rkyv archives, mmap'd, accessed in place (mmap-sync model).
  Write cost: one archive serialize per changed file (cold-path only).
  Read cost: pointer cast + bytecheck. NO parse on daemon restart or query.
  v1 pragmatic fallback: bincode chunks (serde-native, zero derive churn) are
  acceptable ONLY if the restart budget tolerates parse — the research says the
  2026 answer is rkyv; bincode is the 2020 answer.

R2 (disk is cheap): rkyv archives are larger than bincode (alignment, relative
  pointers) — explicitly acceptable. Value-tier packing (turbo-persistence INLINE/
  SMALL/MEDIUM/BLOB) available later if small-file overhead bites.

R3 (RAM = index only):
  - RAM holds: key index {rel_path → (generation, offset/len, content_hash)} = O(#files),
    + mmap page cache (OS-managed, evictable under pressure — not process heap).
  - CRITICAL EXTENSION the user's framing demands: the COMPOSED graph must also be
    an rkyv artifact on disk (per generation, keyed by corpus digest), mmap'd and
    queried in place — exactly like usearch view(). Otherwise ResidentGraph in an
    ArcSwap re-creates a heap-resident O(V+E) structure and violates R3.
  - Queries walk the archived graph zero-copy; hot pages stay cached, cold pages
    get evicted. Process heap stays O(#files) + small.

R4 (O(n)/O(n log n) audit):
  - Disk: chunks O(source bytes); edges as per-file OUTGOING adjacency lists →
    total O(E) (real-world E ≈ near-linear; the O(n²) trap is adjacency matrices
    or all-pairs precomputation — design stores none); manifest O(#files);
    interning table O(unique strings). Sorted key index → O(n log n) build,
    O(log n) lookup (SST model).
  - RAM: index O(#files); compose working set O(V+E) TRANSIENT during recompose
    (streamed, then archived + dropped); steady-state = page cache only.
  - Aggregation-graph idea (Turbopack) reserved for when invalidation traversal
    itself becomes the bottleneck — not v1.
  - Watch item: reverse-edge index ("who calls X") doubles E on disk — still O(E).

R5 (ignore-first):
  - ONE membership oracle (gitignore + tldrignore + excludes, TLDR-bpf/9w8) applied
    at ENUMERATION; ignored paths are never stat'd into the manifest, never hashed,
    never parsed, never chunked, never watched-through (TLDR-1j2 pre-channel filter),
    never composed. Salsa's ValidateInput formalizes the restart re-sync: validate =
    diff manifest against oracle output; only members get content-hash checks.
  - .tldrignore/.gitignore THEMSELVES are durable inputs (A3): their change
    invalidates membership → manifest diff → chunk add/drop + recompose.

R6 (Codex as research base): pending retry (thread handle alive). Its Q1-Q10
  answers get merged into this annex; disagreements adjudicated against THIS
  evidence base, not vibes.

## C. Sharpened answers to the design doc's open questions

Q3 (format): rkyv for chunk payloads AND the composed-graph artifact is the 2026
  answer (A4/A5). Middle ground struck differently than originally guessed: it's
  not "bincode chunks + rkyv composed graph" — if we pay rkyv derive churn at all,
  pay it once for both. bincode survives only as a v0 spike format.
Q4 (persist composed graph): YES — upgraded from "maybe" to REQUIRED by R3.
  Per-generation, keyed by corpus digest, mmap'd; this is what makes restart O(seconds)
  and steady-state RAM index-only.
Q10 (real salsa crate?): NOT for v1. Evidence: salsa persistence is serde-based
  (violates R1 on the hot path), still limitation-heavy (no query hashing,
  transitive-serializability constraints), and tldr's dependency structure is
  shallow (file → chunk → compose) — it doesn't need salsa's general recursive
  query machinery. STEAL its concepts (additive persistence, ValidateInput,
  dependency flattening, durability tiers) without the crate. Revisit if compose
  ever needs fine-grained incrementality (deep derived-query chains).
Q1 (compose cost): still THE open gate — none of the researched systems make
  full-recompose cheap by magic; Turbopack's answer (aggregation layers) is what
  we'd reach for IF the bench fails the ~2s budget. Bench remains the blocker.

## D. Source inventory (scraped, in .firecrawl/)
- turbopack-incremental.md — Next.js engineering blog (2025/2026 era, FS cache stable)
- turbo-persistence-readme.md — store format spec
- ra-durable.md — durabilities design
- ra-persist-issue.md — rust-analyzer #4712 thread
- salsa-pr967.md — merged persistence prototype PR
- salsa-persist-design.md — ibraheemdev HackMD design doc
- salsa-issue10.md — 7-year persistence RFC thread incl. ty/Astral demand signal
- mmap-sync.md — Cloudflare zero-copy mmap crate

comments.text: PROBLEM STATEMENT v2 + DS DECISION (user direction 2026-06-04): treat as a GRAPH, not a JSON document. Schema adherence to old JSON explicitly waived (JSON survives only as per-response output projection). Priorities: write/index may be slow; READ must be near-free; in-RAM index mandatory; mirror the semantic-store lifecycle exactly ('singular' code flow). DATA STRUCTURES: composed graph = CSR (forward callees + reverse callers, flat offset+edge arrays, rkyv/mmap, O(deg) access); string interning to u32 IDs (kills path/name duplication); FST (fst crate) for in-RAM symbol→node index (prefix/fuzzy for free); file→node-range map in manifest (chunk invalidation meshes with CSR: changed file = contiguous ID range); optional xor/AMQF filter for O(1) negative membership. Query costs: calls=FST+1 CSR row (µs); impact=reverse BFS O(touched); dead=reachability O(V+E); hubs=degree array O(1). Explicitly rejected: graph DBs, heap petgraph, adjacency matrices (O(n2) trap), any deserialize-on-read. Lifecycle mapping: same store root, same generation-commit code, same freshness oracle (TLDR-bpf ignore rules), GraphManager mirrors IndexManager, delta mirrors t8f, status shows 'Graph: warm (N nodes / M edges)'. ~19 of 42 CLI commands benefit (calls/impact/dead/structure/tree/complexity/context/extract/imports/slice/smells + arch/changes/coupling/definition/diff/explain/hubs/temporal + bugbot). Open gates unchanged: Gate 1 compose-cost bench; ID-stability-across-recompose contract = manifest range map.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: REJECTED ALTERNATIVES (ADR note, user-confirmed 2026-06-04): (1) Redis-class network KV: violates R1 (ser/de + socket roundtrip per read, ~50-100µs vs ~100ns mmap read), violates R3 (dataset fully RAM-resident), adds external service to a local CLI tool; our shape is single-writer/local-readers/immutable-generations — mmap IS the IPC. (2) Apache Arrow: columnar/analytical-scan format; our hot path is point lookup + neighbor traversal (row/graph-oriented) — Arrow would force edge-list tables + joins and an extra runtime dep while CSR-in-rkyv already gives equal zero-copy with native Rust types. LEGIT FUTURE NICHE: Parquet/DataFusion sidecar for analytics-flavored commands (temporal, churn/complexity trends) — v3 idea for ~2 commands, not an architecture driver. Principle: match storage layout to access pattern (vectors→HNSW, traversal→CSR, columnar analytics→Arrow).

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: GOVERNING CONSTRAINT (user, 2026-06-04, supersedes anything conflicting): AT MOST TWO data flows in the entire system — Flow 1 = analysis store (per-file rkyv chunks → composed CSR graph + FST index), Flow 2 = existing semantic vector store. Identical lifecycle for both (enumerate via ignore-oracle → build → generation-commit → mmap → per-file delta). ALL CLI commands are READ-ONLY PROJECTIONS over these stores — no command may own storage, caching, or invalidation. Consequences: (1) Q5 ANSWERED: the per-command QueryKey response cache is DELETED — projections over mmap'd CSR are µs-cheap, caching them is pure liability; the per-command invalidation problem ceases to exist structurally. (2) Chunk schema carries ALL per-file facts incl. parse-time metrics (complexity etc.) so complexity/smells project from the same substrate. (3) New command = new projection fn, zero new storage. BOUNDARY: single-function queries (slice/CFG/DFG) are stateless on-demand compute from source — not cached at all, which is consistent with (not an exception to) the two-flow rule.

# IN-HOUSE DESIGN REVIEW — analysis store (TLDR-zde)
# Substitute for the Codex review (provider outage); same brief, same deliverables.
# Reviewer: Claude (session) + advisor pass + Firecrawl web verification. 2026-06-04.

## 1. VERDICT: APPROVE WITH 5 NAMED AMENDMENTS (below). No R1-R6 violations found.

## 2. WEB-VERIFIED FINDINGS (deliverable 4)

(a) rkyv 0.8 for mmap workloads — FIT, with one pattern mandated.
    Source: https://rkyv.org/faq.html
    - The FAQ explicitly blesses the exact pattern we need: full bytecheck validation
      is OPTIONAL; "there are many other ways you can verify your data, for example
      with checksums". Even when validating, "validation is still faster than
      deserializing with other high-performance formats".
    - AMENDMENT A2 derived: validate ONCE after write (bytecheck) + store xxh3
      checksum in the artifact header; subsequent opens verify checksum then use
      access_unchecked. Avoids O(artifact-size) bytecheck on every daemon start —
      without it, a multi-GB artifact would pay a full scan per open and quietly
      violate R1.
    - Risks priced: derive churn across FileIR tree is real but bounded (std types
      incl. PathBuf supported); schema evolution is manual → version field in
      header + rebuild-on-mismatch (already in design).

(b) fst crate — OVERQUALIFIED for our scale, adopt without reservation.
    Sources: https://blog.burntsushi.net/transducers/ , https://github.com/burntsushi/fst
    - Canonical demo indexes 1.6 BILLION keys; the crate is designed around mmap
      ("leverages memory maps to make range queries fast"). Our symbol index is
      30k-1M keys — three to five orders of magnitude below its design point.
    - Bonus: prefix/range/fuzzy (Levenshtein) queries built in — future `tldr`
      symbol-completion features come free.

(c) salsa persistence followups since PR#967 — ACTIVE but architecture unchanged.
    Source: https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa/pulls?q=is%3Apr+persistence
    - Followup PRs #969, #973, #975, #992, #1027, #1088 (8 closed) — persistence is
      maturing fast, BUT remains serde-based opt-in serialization (parse-on-load).
    - Decision unchanged: steal concepts (ValidateInput, additive persistence,
      durability tiers), skip the crate for v1. Re-evaluate at v2 if compose ever
      needs fine-grained derived-query incrementality.

(d) Prior art: Meta Glean incremental indexing — VALIDATES our simpler v1 choice.
    Source: https://glean.software/blog/incremental/
    - Glean's model: per-unit facts; incremental DB "hides" changed units' facts
      (≈ our chunk overwrite); visibility propagated via OWNERSHIP SETS
      (Elias-Fano coded, interval-mapped, ~7% DB overhead); derived facts carry
      boolean ownership expressions that "can get arbitrarily large".
    - Lesson: ownership/visibility machinery is what you must build if you do NOT
      recompose derived state from scratch. It is substantially complex. Our
      recompose-always v1 (given Gate 1 passes) avoids that entire class.
      Glean's design is the documented ESCALATION PATH if incremental compose is
      ever forced — do not invent a third alternative (Amendment A5).

## 3. GATE ANSWERS (deliverable 2)

GATE 1 — compose-cost bench spec (THE precondition; ~20 lines of instrumentation,
no refactor needed):
  - Instrument build_project_call_graph_v2 with env-gated phase timers
    (TLDR_PHASE_TIMING=1): T_parse = build_indices_parallel (step 4);
    T_compose = steps 5-12 (add_file, build_indices, ModuleIndex,
    ImportResolver/ReExportTracer loop, edge creation).
  - Run on (i) tldr-code (1570 files/~28k fns) and (ii) one 5-10x larger corpus
    (big OSS repo) to get the scaling slope, not just a point.
  - PASS: T_compose ≤ 2s on tldr-code AND slope ≤ O(n log n) between sizes.
  - MARGINAL (2-5s): acceptable — deltas are already debounced/coalesced by the
    serialized worker; recompose at most once per quiet window.
  - FAIL (>5s or superlinear): v1 must add incremental compose; adopt the Glean
    escalation path (per-file edge lists + visibility) — STOP and redesign first.

ID-STABILITY CONTRACT:
  - Node IDs are generation-local. NEVER persisted outside the artifact, NEVER
    returned to clients (responses carry symbol names + file:line). All external
    entry via FST lookup. This single rule eliminates cross-generation dangling-ID
    bugs by construction.
  - Readers pin a generation at open; on unix an unlinked-but-mapped file stays
    valid, so GC can delete eagerly. WINDOWS CAVEAT: mapped files cannot be
    deleted → GC must tolerate failure + retry later (Flow 2 has the same issue;
    share the code).
  - GC policy: keep ≥2 generations + age threshold = the reader-grace contract;
    adopt/extend TLDR-pdb's Flow-2 decision rather than inventing a second one.

MULTI-LANGUAGE (Q6): chunks already carry language; compose runs PER LANGUAGE
  (builder_v2 is per-language today — no cross-language edges exist to lose).
  One manifest with per-language sections: file list + node-range map + CSR
  artifact offset per language. Language-agnostic projections (structure, tree,
  extract) read chunks directly and ignore compose entirely.

Q8 — WHAT SURVIVES FROM salsa.rs:
  - revision counter → generation sequence number under CURRENT (monotonicity
    preserved; same role, better durability).
  - dependents map (input_hash → QueryKeys) → DELETED, replaced structurally by
    the file→node-range manifest. Nothing hash-shaped to maintain.
  - maybe_evict byte caps → generation GC + orphan-chunk GC by manifest
    reachability (mirrors TLDR-za0 on Flow 2).
  - Busy-token/liveness semantics (TLDR-3w5) and warm-ack latency (utj.7):
    untouched by design; recompose runs inside the existing serialized worker.

## 4. ADVERSARIAL PROJECTION HUNT (deliverable 3)

Examined all ~19 commands. NO command requires a third flow. Three findings:
  - `temporal` + `coupling` (co-change): need GIT HISTORY as an additional INPUT.
    Git is an input source read at query time, not a store we own — consistent
    with the two-flow rule the same way source text is. (If churn queries ever
    get slow, the v3 Parquet sidecar note in the ADR covers it.)
  - `explain`/`context`: need source text snippets → read from disk on demand,
    stateless. Fine.
  - `dead`: needs root/entry-point determination → derivable from chunk facts
    (main fns, pub visibility, test attrs). Requires the chunk schema to carry
    visibility/attr flags — ADD to chunk schema checklist.
  Confirmed dependency: `complexity`/`smells` require parse-time metrics in chunks
  (already mandated by the two-flow decision D2).

## 5. TABLE-STAKES OMISSIONS FOUND (deliverable 5)

  - Crash mid-generation-write: covered by CURRENT-flip pattern (Flow 2 proven).
    But chunk overwrites OUTSIDE a generation flip (delta path) need atomic
    rename + manifest update ordering: write chunk → fsync → update manifest →
    fsync → THEN recompose. Spell this out in the implementation issue.
  - Windows mmap deletion semantics (above) — share Flow 2's handling.
  - Concurrent CLI reader during GC — adopt TLDR-pdb contract (above).
  - Artifact integrity on partial disk (ENOSPC mid-write): generation pattern
    handles (incomplete generation never becomes CURRENT); chunk delta path must
    write-to-temp + rename, never truncate-in-place.

## 6. AMENDMENTS (the verdict's conditions)

  A1. Gate-1 phase-timer bench is a HARD precondition to any storage code.
  A2. Integrity pattern: bytecheck-once-after-write + header checksum +
      access_unchecked on subsequent opens.
  A3. Reader-grace/GC: adopt TLDR-pdb semantics for Flow 1; Windows
      deletion-failure tolerance shared with Flow 2.
  A4. Manifest gets per-language sections (Q6); chunk schema checklist grows
      visibility/attr flags (for `dead`) + parse-time metrics (for complexity/smells).
  A5. If Gate 1 fails: escalate to the Glean ownership-set path — documented,
      named, no third invention.

## 7. DISAGREEMENT LOG
  None between this review, the advisor pass, and the research annex. The one
  correction this review adds over earlier session statements: per-open bytecheck
  would have silently violated R1 at scale — caught by verification (a).

# Research annex v2 — second Firecrawl sweep (2026-06-04)
# Focus: library-first opportunities (user philosophy) + production validation of the chunk model.

## F1. GitHub stack-graphs — OUR ARCHITECTURE, VALIDATED AT GITHUB SCALE
Sources: https://github.blog/open-source/introducing-stack-graphs/ ,
         https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.01224 , https://github.com/github/stack-graphs
- Their index-time rule is verbatim our Gate-0 invariant: "we look at each file
  COMPLETELY IN ISOLATION ... we must ignore [other files] while extracting
  incremental facts". Per-file graphs extracted at push time; merged at query time.
- They go one step FURTHER than our design: resolution is QUERY-TIME PATH-FINDING
  over the merged per-file graphs (stack-based scope resolution), not an eager
  compose. Merge = cheap graph union; the expensive part is lazy and per-query.
- DESIGN IMPACT: this is a SECOND escape hatch for Gate 1, cheaper than Glean's
  ownership sets: if eager compose busts the 2s budget, shift import/call
  resolution to query time over per-file graphs (cacheable per query). Updated
  escalation ladder in F5.
- Their storage: per-file graph blobs (SQLite-backed store in the crate) — the
  chunk model again.

## F2. epserde (Vigna) — candidate to BEAT rkyv for the composed artifact
Sources: https://github.com/vigna/epserde-rs (+ WebGraph-next-gen paper
         https://hal.science/hal-04494627/document , crates.io/crates/webgraph)
- ε-copy deserialization: at load, build a MINUSCULE struct skeleton; all bulk
  (slices/vectors) referenced directly from the mmap backend. Key quote: "the
  performance of the deserialized structure will be IDENTICAL to that of a
  standard, in-memory Rust structure, as references are resolved at
  deserialization time."
- This eliminates rkyv's principal tax: NO Archived* mirror types, no wrapper
  navigation on every access — native &[u32] slices over mmap. For a CSR
  artifact (flat offset/edge/degree arrays + interned string table) this is the
  IDEAL shape. Explicit huge-pages support; MemCase couples instance + backend;
  mmap_rs integration built in.
- Powers webgraph-rs: WebGraph "next generation (is in Rust)" — billions of
  edges, mmap'd, in production research use. CSR-at-scale prior art.
- License: LGPL-2.1 — COMPATIBLE with tldr's AGPL-3.0 (verified Cargo.toml:16).
- DESIGN IMPACT (amendment A6): the format decision is now a TWO-WAY spike, not
  settled: (i) rkyv everywhere, (ii) rkyv for chunks (deep nested FileIR) +
  epserde for the composed CSR artifact (flat arrays, native-speed access).
  Lean (ii): each format used exactly where its strength is; both are
  wiring-only per the library-first philosophy. webgraph's BVGraph compression
  itself is likely overkill (web-graph-specialized gap coding) — epserde + plain
  arrays is the sweet spot.

## F3. ty (Astral) launch data — calibrates the incrementality ceiling
Source: https://astral.sh/blog/ty
- Salsa-based, MIT, shipped. After editing a LOAD-BEARING file in PyTorch:
  diagnostics recompute in 4.7ms (80x faster than Pyright, 500x than Pyrefly).
  10-60x faster than mypy/Pyright WITHOUT caching.
- Validates: fine-grained salsa incrementality delivers millisecond-class
  per-edit updates at huge-repo scale — that is the v2 ceiling if tldr ever
  needs it. ALSO notable: ty runs IN-MEMORY (salsa persistence still maturing) —
  tldr's disk-chunk design is AHEAD of ty on the restart/CI axis, behind it on
  per-edit granularity. Different products, right trade for each.

## F4. oxc-resolver — library-first candidate for part of compose
Sources: https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc-resolver , oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/resolver
- Rust port of webpack enhanced-resolve, maintained by oxc, used by Rspack/
  Rolldown in production. Handles tsconfig paths/aliases, package.json exports
  maps, monorepo workspace resolution.
- DESIGN IMPACT (candidate only, NOT a v1 decision): tldr's hand-rolled JS/TS
  ModuleIndex/ImportResolver (incl. the VAL-007 workspace-alias logic) could
  potentially be replaced by oxc_resolver — directly per the user's philosophy
  (delete bespoke resolution code, keep wiring). Needs a compatibility spike:
  does oxc_resolver's semantics match builder_v2's resolution contract for the
  languages tldr supports? File as follow-up; do not block v1.

## F5. UPDATED GATE-1 ESCALATION LADDER (supersedes single Glean path)
  1. PASS (compose ≤2s): recompose-always v1 (current design).
  2. MARGINAL: debounce/coalesce recompose (already in design).
  3. FAIL, first resort: stack-graphs model — compose becomes cheap graph union;
     resolution moves to query-time path-finding (cacheable). Production-proven
     at GitHub scale, much simpler than ownership tracking. (F1)
  4. FAIL, heavy artillery: Glean ownership sets / fine-grained salsa (ty-class
     machinery). Only if query-time resolution also proves too slow. (F3 + annex v1)

## F6. AMENDMENT LIST DELTA (extends in-house review's A1-A5)
  A6. Format spike: rkyv-everywhere vs rkyv-chunks + epserde-CSR. Measure load
      cost, access cost (Archived* wrappers vs native slices), derive burden.
  A7. File follow-up issue: oxc_resolver as replacement for hand-rolled JS/TS
      module resolution in compose (library-first; post-v1).

# RESEARCH ROUND 3 — counter-evidence / double-confirmation (2026-06-04)

## C1. MAJOR CORRECTION: stack-graphs is ARCHIVED (Sep 9, 2025)
Verified on repo banner: "This repository was archived by the owner on Sep 9,
2025. It is now read-only" (github.com/github/stack-graphs, final commit = the
archival PR #502). Annex v2 called it "production-proven at GitHub scale" —
that needs qualification: the TECHNIQUE shipped in GitHub precise code-nav and
the arXiv paper documents it, but GitHub has discontinued the OSS project.
Implications:
  (a) The architecture lesson STANDS (per-file isolation at index time, merge
      at query time) — it is documented, shipped prior art.
  (b) Do NOT take a crate dependency on stack-graphs.
  (c) F5 escalation ladder rung 3 reworded: "query-time-resolution PATTERN
      (implement ourselves, per the stack-graphs paper)" — not a library.
  (d) Cautionary signal: GitHub found per-language graph-rule maintenance
      costly enough to wind down. tldr's per-language extraction already
      exists, so the marginal risk differs — but worth remembering.

## C2. epserde constraints CONFIRMED from its own Cons section
  - No references in types (no trees) — fine for flat CSR.
  - ε-copy fields must be TYPE PARAMETERS implementing DeserInner — the one
    artifact type must be written in epserde's generic style (contained burden).
  - Vectors of NON-zero-copy elements deserialize recursively in memory —
    nested FileIR gets ZERO ε-copy benefit → epserde is ONLY a candidate for
    the flat composed artifact; chunks stay rkyv regardless.
  - serialize/deserialize APIs are unsafe-marked; recent API renames
    ("Warning to Previous Users") = mild churn risk. LGPL-2.1 OK with AGPL-3.0.

## C3. rkyv health CONFIRMED: 0.8.8 latest, steady 0.8.x patch cadence.
## C4. fst health CONFIRMED: 20.4M downloads, MIT/Unlicense, BurntSushi.
## C5. oxc_resolver scope CONFIRMED: enhanced-resolve port = JS/TS ONLY.
    It can replace only the JS/TS slice of compose; py/rust/go/java stay ours.

## LOCK RECOMMENDATIONS (post-double-confirmation)
LOCKED NOW:
  - rkyv 0.8.x for per-file chunks (no competitor exists for nested types).
  - fst for the symbol index.
  - CSR layout for the composed graph.
  - Query-time-resolution as escalation PATTERN, not dependency (C1).
SHARPENED PRIOR (decided by the A6 spike, not by fiat):
  - For FLAT u32 arrays, rkyv's archived form is essentially the native form —
    the Archived* tax bites on nested/string types, not PODs. epserde's
    advantage on CSR specifically is therefore likely SMALL, and it costs a
    second framework + generic-style type + unsafe API churn.
  - Default = rkyv-everywhere. epserde adopted only if the spike shows a
    meaningful (>=2x) access/load penalty on the CSR artifact. Either way the
    spike is cheap: one struct, two serializers, one criterion bench.

# IMPLEMENTATION BLUEPRINT (2026-06-04 — the contract for implementation sessions)

DISK: stores/<hash>/analysis/v1/ → chunks/<xxh64-path>.fir (rkyv FileIR incl.
visibility flags + parse-time metrics; header{lang, content_hash, checksum}),
generations/<seq>/{manifest.bin (per-lang sections, file→node-range),
graph.csr (fwd+rev offsets/edges/degrees), strings.tbl, symbols.fst}, CURRENT.

RAM: GraphManager (mirrors IndexManager) = mmap handles + FST + manifest map.
O(#files+symbols). No heap graph, no response cache.

PATHS: cold = oracle→parse∥→chunk+drop-AST→compose→generation→flip.
restart = CURRENT→checksum→mmap→stat-sweep→delta for stale.
edit = watcher(1j2-filtered)→one chunk swap (write-temp+rename, fsync order:
chunk→manifest)→debounced recompose→new gen→reader-grace GC (pdb semantics,
Windows delete-failure tolerant).
query = FST→CSR walk→JSON at the edge; CLI-no-daemon mmaps directly.

CODE: tldr-core/analysis_store/ (chunk io, manifest, compose, CSR, projections);
builder_v2 split parse(file)→FileIR | compose(chunks)→CSR; daemon GraphManager
+ warm step + delta route + 'Graph: warm (N nodes / M edges)' status; DELETE at
cutover: QueryKey cache entries, triple-copy inserts, per-command paths.

PHASES (feature-flagged, Flow 2 untouched):
0 preconditions: TLDR-9ae F1; Gate-1 phase-timer bench; A6 rkyv-vs-epserde
  spike (default rkyv); TLDR-bpf oracle (9w8→1j2/1qv).
1 chunk layer. 2 compose split. 3 artifact+projections (19 cmds).
4 daemon integration. 5 cutover+deletion.

ACCEPTANCE: restart<5s; edit-to-fresh<2s; build peak<8GB; query µs-ms;
idle RAM≈index; CI chunk reuse; 10x project = linear disk, index-only RAM.

# BENEFITS STATEMENT (what this design buys — measured baseline vs target)

PERFORMANCE
- Daemon restart: 3.5min + 22GB full recompute (measured) -> SECONDS (mmap + checksum, zero parse)
- Single file edit: whole-cache eviction -> next query full rebuild (measured) -> one chunk re-parse + recompose, <=2s end-to-end
- Query latency: cache-miss = minutes -> FST lookup + CSR walk = microseconds, always
- Cold CLI / CI: full build per invocation -> chunks shared across processes AND runs (the ty/Astral CI motivation)

MEMORY
- Build peak: 22.0GB phys_footprint (measured, MALLOC_LARGE) -> <8GB target (streaming parse->chunk->drop-AST; no JSON DOM; no triple copies)
- Steady-state heap: composed graph + JSON blobs -> O(#files + symbols) index only; graph bulk in OS page cache, EVICTABLE under pressure
- Scaling: 10x project = linear disk, index-only RAM growth (R4 audited: no O(n^2) structure exists)

CPU (R1)
- Reads: zero serialization/deserialization, ever (rkyv access_unchecked after one post-write validation)
- Writes: serialize once per CHANGED file only; ignored paths never touch CPU (oracle at enumeration)

CORRECTNESS / MAINTAINABILITY
- The invalidation bug class is STRUCTURALLY GONE: no per-command caches to invalidate; chunk granularity matches change granularity
- Ignore-correctness by construction: one membership oracle, one front door (kills the .tldrignore bug family of TLDR-bpf at the root)
- One lifecycle shared with the semantic store = half the correctness surface; generation commits give crash consistency for free
- New command = one projection function: zero new storage, zero new invalidation, zero new lifecycle
- Library-first: rkyv/fst/ignore/notify maintained upstream; our code is wiring + domain extraction only

PRODUCT
- ~39/63 commands (62%) ride warm stores directly; the rest enter the same door for navigation
- tldr's value prop upgrades from "fast while one daemon stays warm" to "FAST ALWAYS — across restarts, processes, and CI"
- On-disk artifacts are inspectable/debuggable vs today's opaque in-RAM blobs

CONCLUSION (fact): 97% of sampled compose sits in three NAMED sites, all the same defect class as rounds 1-4 (per-call-site linear work that should be indexed lookups). Nothing sampled looks like inherent global-resolution cost.

HYPOTHESIS (explicitly NOT a result — round-1 lesson): fixing all three should cut compose materially; magnitude unknown until fixed AND re-benched. Candidate fix shapes for the authorization discussion: (a) extend round-3's inverted pass to weird receivers — per let-line, index each 'let '/'let mut ' occurrence remainder keyed by the text preceding ': '/' = ' -> O(occurrences) build, O(1) lookup, output-identical by the same construction argument as rounds 3-4; (b) resolve_local_fuzzy_match -> find_by_name(bare_target) then filter by file; (c) resolve_type_aware_fallback -> find_by_name likewise. All three await user authorization (no-code directive in force).

COST OF THIS ROUND: 3 bench runs (~70s wall), zero rebuilds (overnight unstripped HEAD binary reused), bench-process RAM only. Profiles: /tmp/compose-sample.txt, /tmp/compose-sample2.txt.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
ECONOMICS RE-DERIVATION (queue item 4, 2026-06-05 — honest numbers, conditional verdict; supersedes the 2026-06-04 17:49 benefits statement where they conflict).

TIME AXIS — what chunking actually buys now:
- Measured: parse 2.5-2.7s, compose 19.5-20.7s. Chunks memoize PARSE ONLY; compose is global and re-runs on every edit AND restart regardless of chunking. So chunk persistence buys <=2.7s per rebuild. That is the ENTIRE time-economics of the chunk store unless compose goes incremental (a much bigger design, explicitly out of v1).
- The original 'restart: 3.5min+22GB -> seconds via mmap' claim CONFLATED parse + compose + the (now-fixed) rounds-1-4 defects. Post-overnight, a full callgraph rebuild is ~22s with NO chunk store at all. Restart-from-chunks = compose-only ~19.5s today. Chunk-store restart win = the parse share = ~2.7/22.3 = ~12%.
- Gate-1 verdict: OPEN pending round-5 fixes + re-bench. Scenarios: S1 (compose -> ~2-5s): recompose-always viable, Gate-1 effectively passes — but then full rebuild is ~5-8s total and chunking's time value shrinks to ~2.7s saved = MARGINAL. S2 (compose stays >=10s): per-edit recompose-always dead; lazy compose = 10-20s first-query-after-edit (tolerable-ish for CLI, weak for interactive); incremental compose forced if better is required. NOTE THE SHAPE: in BOTH scenarios the time case for Path B is far weaker than at design time, when the premise was saving ~220s.

MEMORY AXIS — the honesty correction:
- The 27.0GB peak is the EMBED phase (Flow-2, TLDR-3rh): overnight diff touched only callgraph/* + daemon warm-insert; semantic/ ran byte-identical to main. Also the 27.0 came from the getrusage high-water probe (shipped 2 days ago) vs the historical 22.7 from 15s ps polling — a true max SHOULD read above a sampled poll; partly better measurement, not necessarily worse behavior. Post-redesign daemon peak = max(phase peaks) = EMBED. The chunk store does not touch the headline memory number. That peak belongs to TLDR-3rh/yll.
- Callgraph-phase plateau: 11.4GB measured PRE-F1 (with the to_value DOM). F1 is shipped; post-F1 plateau is UNMEASURED (= morning-queue item 2: daemon warm ~22s; awaiting user authorization since it leaves a resident daemon). The chunk store's memory win = whatever transient remains AFTER F1 (+ what surgical F2-F4, TLDR-1in, could take without any storage layer).

NET: BOTH axes moved toward Path A (surgical: F1 shipped + F2-F4 + round-5 compose fixes + naive generation persistence) and away from Path B (full two-flow store) this session. NOT a verdict — two decision inputs still missing: (1) post-round-5 compose number (needs code authorization), (2) post-F1 warm peak (item 2, needs daemon authorization). Make the Path A/B call only when both exist; do not re-lock anything before then.

CAVEAT: all numbers are rust-on-tldr-code. Python/TS/generic resolvers share the defect class (queue item 3) and their compose economics may differ materially per language. What Path B uniquely retains regardless: cross-process/CI chunk sharing (worth ~parse only), mmap-evictable steady-state, restart without parse — re-weigh these against Path A once (1) and (2) land.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
GATE-1 ROUND 5 RESULT — GATE-1 PASSES (2026-06-05 morning, commit follows round-5 profile; user-authorized code round, <1h budget, actual ~35min).

Implemented the three profiled fixes (one shared defect class):
(a) RustReceiverIndex weird path: inverted at construction — per let-line, every candidate (var,kind) enumerable as text-between-prefix-occurrence-and-separator; lookup is now a hash get for dotted receivers too. scan_weird/let_lines/weird_cache deleted; resolve/lookup take &self.
(b) resolve_local_fuzzy_match -> find_by_name (identical multiplicity: one yield per (module,name) alias, argued + gate-verified).
(c) resolve_type_aware_fallback -> find_by_name + alloc-free methods checks.

MEASURED (3 runs, HEAD corpus): scan ~10ms / parse 2.5-2.7s / COMPOSE 0.55-0.56s / total ~3.1s. Round-over-round: compose 19.5s -> 0.56s = 35x this round. CAMPAIGN NET: compose 223s -> 0.56s = ~400x; total build 226s -> 3.1s = ~73x. Parse now dominates (~83% of build).

GATE-1 VERDICT: PASS — compose 0.56s is under the 2s recompose-per-edit line with margin. Recompose-always v1 is RESURRECTED as designed; the escalation ladder (query-time resolution / incremental compose / Glean sets) is NOT needed.

CORRECTNESS EVIDENCE: (1) frozen-corpus (/tmp/tldr-bench @001fdcb) counts BYTE-IDENTICAL to the entire overnight campaign: 745/20,320/26,312; (2) exhaustive differential test extended with 9 weird-receiver stressors (empty receiver, 'mut a', 'a: A', separator-containing vars) — green; (3) 1,053 callgraph tests green; full core+cli suites green except the documented pre-existing TLDR-wks/TLDR-6q2 families (cpp-inheritance x1, explain/taint x36, embed x18 — verified same families, zero new); (4) full 8.4MB edge JSON byte-identical across two runs — output is now DETERMINISTIC (old iter()-order code was per-process random; same nondeterminism class as TLDR-2af).

ECONOMICS DELTA (updates the conditional in the prior comment — scenario S1 realized, stronger than projected): full rebuild ~3.1s, parse-dominated. Chunk-store time value = the 2.7s parse memoization on a 3.1s build; restart-from-chunks ~0.6s vs 3.1s rebuild. Time case for Path B storage is now MARGINAL on rust-on-tldr-code; the live decision inputs are memory (post-F1 warm peak, item 2, still awaiting daemon authorization) + other-language resolvers (queue item 3: python/TS share the per-call-site-scan defect class — their compose numbers unknown).

REMAINING perf note (not blocking, unprofiled): compose 0.56s not yet re-profiled; next marginal candidates if ever needed: per-lookup var_name.to_string() key alloc, enclosing_class_for_call/find_best_vartype per-call scans. Diminishing returns — parse is the new ceiling.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: ROUND-5 VERIFICATION CLOSER (advisor-prompted): the 'byte-identical' claim for fix (a) was count-level on the real corpus + value-level on synthetic input only. Closed: new permanent corpus-level differential gate (rust_receiver_index_matches_legacy_on_real_corpus) — for 400+ REAL Method/Attr call-site receivers extracted from the crate's own callgraph sources, index and legacy scanner agree value-level (catches same-count-different-type divergence). Green. (b)/(c) remain honestly characterized as count-identical + newly-deterministic (legacy iter() order was per-process random, so value-level equivalence is not even well-defined for them).

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text:
DECISION EVOLUTION CHAIN (ADR set, 2026-06-05): the full journey — wrong assumption, premature lock, the gate that caught it, the 400x fix campaign, and the honest re-derivation — is captured as decision records, superseded ones kept deliberately:
- TLDR-cv9 ADR-1 [CLOSED, superseded by ADR-6]: design premised on 'parse expensive, compose cheap' — never measured, measured backwards.
- TLDR-v88 ADR-2 [CLOSED, superseded by ADR-3]: marked architecture LOCKED before Gate-1 ran — the owned process mistake (manufactured false certainty).
- TLDR-k89 ADR-3 [ACTIVE]: nothing above PROPOSED until kill-gates are measured; no storage code before Gate-0/1.
- TLDR-w9z ADR-4 [ACTIVE]: Gate-1 FAIL treated as suspected defect -> profile/fix loop, not architecture escalation (vindicated: 223s -> 0.56s, 7 defects, 5 rounds; lessons: sum ALL branches, re-profile your own fixes).
- TLDR-f0n ADR-5 [ACTIVE]: output-identity discipline — layered differential gates, legacy kept as oracle.
- TLDR-7mp ADR-6 [ACTIVE, supersedes ADR-1]: Gate-1 PASS; recompose-always stands; time case reduced to ~2.7s; Path A/B deferred to post-F1 warm peak + python/TS numbers.
- TLDR-ab6 ADR-7 [ACTIVE]: headline 27GB peak is EMBED phase — memory work routed to 3rh/yll + F-series, not the chunk store.
Point of the chain: not why a stale decision exists, but that the evolution is on the record.

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: DECISION EVOLUTION CHAIN UPDATE: ADR-8 (TLDR-asv) ratified — Path A adopted, this issue PARKED (P3). Chain: ADR-1(closed) -> ADR-6(closed) -> ADR-8(active).

comments.author: Udhayakumar
comments.text: ADR-9 (TLDR-t0s, 2026-06-05) UNPARKS THE QUERY-SERVING HALF of this design: the graph-native CSR fwd+rev + interning + ArcSwap snapshot layout moves into the daemon as a RAM-resident structure (epic TLDR-7pp, child TLDR-n74). The DISK layer (rkyv chunks, mmap, generation commits) remains PARKED per ADR-8 — restart ~3s (parallel re-parse + recompose) is accepted; if restart pain is ever measured, this design's chunk store slots under the per-file fact layer (TLDR-iqr) unchanged. Also: TLDR-iqr implements the in-RAM kernel of this design (per-file FileIR memo, content-hash keyed) — 'Path A.5'.

title: F2-F4: structural memory reductions in callgraph builder (AST streaming, index dedup, string interning)
description: F2: build_indices_parallel (builder_v2.rs:638) — drop source text + tree-sitter AST immediately after FileIR extraction; consider bounding rayon width for peak control. F3: unify the duplicated FuncIndex/ClassIndex (builder_v2.rs:682-685 'We need our own copies because the IR's indices use a different format'). F4: intern strings (ustr/lasso) for file paths/names/signatures across nodes, edges, indices. Sequence and prioritize per the Phase-A measurement (TLDR-335) — do the biggest measured contributor first.
notes: Deprioritized by ADR-8: target (GB-scale callgraph warm transient) eliminated — warm peak measured 549MB post-F1+Gate-1-rounds (TLDR-myd).
close_reason: Target gone + subsumed: GB-scale callgraph memory target eliminated (549MB warm peak). Surviving ideas are absorbed by the ratified architecture — string interning = ADR-9 intern table (TLDR-n74), AST non-retention = L2 facts-not-ASTs rule (TLDR-17d/rem). Keeping this open would duplicate n74/17d work.

title: run Phase-A malloc attribution protocol on the 22GB callgraph plateau
description: Execute the step-by-step protocol in TLDR-k8s design notes §3: MallocStackLogging=1 daemon start → warm → malloc_history <pid> -allBySize mid-plateau (60-180s in) + vmmap + footprint snapshots. Also run the foreground-warm secondary harness (/usr/bin/time -l, daemon stopped — callgraph only, skips the daemon copy stack): the DELTA between daemon footprint and foreground max-RSS ≈ cost of the triple-copy (cause a) alone. Deliverable: top-10 allocation sites by bytes, each mapped to causes (a)-(d), recorded on TLDR-k8s. PRECONDITION: embedding cache warm (so embed phase is cache-hits and only the callgraph phase recomputes — ~5min total run).
notes: Deprioritized by ADR-8: the 22GB callgraph plateau no longer exists (warm peak 549MB, TLDR-myd correction). Protocol retained for embed-phase work if TLDR-3rh needs allocation attribution.
close_reason: Target gone: the 22GB callgraph plateau no longer exists (post-F1+Gate-1 warm peak 549MB, TLDR-myd evidence). Attribution of a fixed defect is archaeology. Remaining GB-scale memory scope is embed-phase only (TLDR-3rh/yll).

title: ignore-file mid-session reload: watcher rebuilds matchers when .tldrignore/.gitignore change
description: Reload root .tldrignore and .gitignore matcher state during a live daemon session. Watcher policy events atomically rebuild and replace the shared matcher snapshot before any paths from that event are evaluated; ordinary source events do not rebuild matcher state. Presence tracking remains independent from ignore membership.
acceptance_criteria: Creating, changing, or deleting root .tldrignore or .gitignore replaces watcher matcher state without daemon restart; the replacement happens before paths from the policy event are evaluated; ordinary source events do not trigger reload; existing watcher debounce/burst behavior and workspace gates pass.
notes: COMPLETION EVIDENCE 2026-07-27: LiveIgnoreMatcher owns lock-protected shared matcher state; policy events reload once before path evaluation. Focused tests prove add/remove lifecycle for both .tldrignore and .gitignore plus no reload for ordinary source events. Watcher tests 7/7 passed; workspace Clippy/tests, smoke 2/2, and certification 10/10 passed.
close_reason: Implemented lock-protected live reload for root .tldrignore/.gitignore policy with focused lifecycle tests and complete green gates.

title: idle_timeout semantics migration: client-idle -> project-presence-idle (config naming + docs)
description: Codex-identified gap (risk #4): idle_timeout_secs is documented as client 'idle timeout' (types.rs:52). TLDR-cxa changes its meaning to project-presence idle — existing user configs silently change behavior (a 1800s timeout that used to reap daemons on busy-build machines no longer will). SCOPE: decide naming (keep key + redefine vs new key + deprecation), update config docs + DAEMON_SEMANTIC_ARCHITECTURE.md §11, and emit a one-line startup log stating the effective liveness policy so the change is visible. Lands with or immediately after A.
close_reason: Shipped: keep-key-redefine decision documented in types.rs field doc; startup log line states effective liveness policy; §11.2b in architecture doc documents presence sources + retired workarounds; TROUBLESHOOTING/daemon.md purged of fictional --idle-timeout flag and stale 300s claim.

description: All verified to fail identically on base tree (git stash) on 2026-06-04: (1) med_cleanup_bundle_v1::m14_smells_notes_deep_only_analyzers — expects a --deep notice on stderr that no longer appears; (2) bench_patterns_security_multilang::test_inheritance_cpp_unsupported — asserts C++ inheritance returns 0 classes but the module now extracts 3 (stale assertion after C++ support landed); (3) exhaustive_matrix explain/taint x18 — 'function_name' vs 'function' schema drift, already tracked as TLDR-wks (commented); (4) exhaustive_matrix embed x18 — test_embed_on_c HANGs >30s (debug ONNX first load) then poisons embedding_mutex cascading PoisonError to 17 cells (also in TLDR-wks comment); (5) schema_cleanup_v1 x10 — requires /tmp/repos/flask fixture, absent on this machine.

It already funnels into the one invalidation path (handle_notify -> process_dirty_file, same as the watcher worker; never a parallel mechanism).
